     1→# Lock Code Manager
     2→
     3→> NOTE: This integration is in very early stages, so expect things to not work as expected.
     4→> Feel free to open issues to report anything you find, but I would not recommend using
     5→> this for production usage yet.
     6→
     7→Lock Code Manager is a Home Assistant integration that allows you to more easily manage
     8→your usercodes on your locks. Once you have configured it, the integration will set and
     9→clear codes on your locks as needed depending on how you decide to configure them.
    10→
    11→Features:
    12→
    13→- Synchronize multiple locks with a single set of codes
    14→- Optionally use a condition entity to control when a code is active. Supported entity types:
    15→  - `calendar` - code is active when an event is in progress
    16→  - `binary_sensor` - code is active when the sensor is `on`
    17→  - `switch` - code is active when the switch is `on`
    18→  - `schedule` - code is active when the schedule is `on`
    19→  - `input_boolean` - code is active when the input boolean is `on`
    20→- Optionally define a maximum number of uses for a code before the code is disabled
    21→
    22→Locks from the following integrations are currently supported:
    23→
    24→- Z-Wave
    25→- [Virtual](https://github.com/twrecked/hass-virtual) custom integration. See the
    26→  [Wiki page on this integration](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki/Virtual-integration)
    27→  for more details on why it was built and how it works.
    28→
    29→The code was written to make it (I think) easy to add support for locks in other
    30→integrations. Check the [Wiki](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki) if you
    31→want to learn more about that and take a stab at it. Contributors welcome!
    32→
    33→## Installation
    34→
    35→The best way to install this integration is via HACS.
    36→
    37→1. Set up your locks as entities to your Home Assistant instance through the corresponding
    38→   integration (e.g. Z-Wave)
    39→2. Add this repository as a custom integration repository in HACS
    40→3. Go to Settings > Devices & Services > Add Integration
    41→4. Select Lock Code Manager
    42→5. Follow the prompts - additional information about the configuration options are
    43→   available in the Wiki
    44→
    45→## Learn More
    46→
    47→The [Wiki](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki) is a WIP but has some
    48→content that might be helpful for you!
    49→
    50→## UI & Dashboards
    51→
    52→Lock Code Manager can generate Lovelace dashboards for managing and monitoring PINs. You
    53→can use the dashboard strategy (full dashboard), the view strategy (single view for a
    54→config entry), or the custom card directly.
    55→
    56→See [this wiki article](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki/Add-a-UI-for-lock-code-management#dashboard)
    57→for more details.
    58→
    59→### Dashboard Strategy
    60→
    61→Use the dashboard strategy to build a full dashboard with one view per config entry, and
    62→an optional "User Codes" view that shows lock codes cards across all managed locks.
    63→
    64→| Option                              | Default              | Description                                                 |
    65→| ----------------------------------- | -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
    66→| `use_slot_cards`                    | `true`               | Use streamlined slot cards instead of legacy entities cards |
    67→| `show_code_sensors`                 | `true`               | Show code sensors in lock status section                    |
    68→| `show_conditions`                   | `true`               | Show conditions section in slot cards                       |
    69→| `show_lock_status`                  | `true`               | Show lock status section in slot cards                      |
    70→| `show_lock_sync`                    | `true`               | Show sync status per lock in lock status                    |
    71→| `collapsed_sections`                | `[]`                 | Which sections start collapsed (empty = all expanded)       |
    72→| `show_per_configuration_lock_cards` | `true`               | Show lock cards in per-config-entry views                   |
    73→| `show_all_lock_cards_view`          | `true`               | Add a "User Codes" view with cards showing all lock codes   |
    74→| `code_display`                      | `masked_with_reveal` | Code visibility mode for slot cards and lock codes cards    |
    75→
    76→Example dashboard configuration:
    77→
    78→```yaml
    79→strategy:
    80→  type: custom:lock-code-manager
    81→  show_all_lock_cards_view: true
    82→  show_per_configuration_lock_cards: true
    83→  code_display: masked_with_reveal
    84→  show_lock_sync: true
    85→```
    86→
    87→### View Strategy
    88→
    89→Use the view strategy when you want a single view for one config entry. If
    90→`show_lock_cards` is true, lock codes cards are appended below the slot
    91→cards within the same view (no extra view is created).
    92→
    93→| Option                     | Default              | Description                                                       |
    94→| -------------------------- | -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
    95→| `config_entry_id`          | -                    | Config entry ID to render                                         |
    96→| `config_entry_title`       | -                    | Config entry title to render (alternative to ID)                  |
    97→| `use_slot_cards`           | `true`               | Use streamlined slot cards instead of legacy entities cards       |
    98→| `show_code_sensors`        | `true`               | Show code sensors in lock status section                          |
    99→| `show_conditions`          | `true`               | Show conditions section in slot cards                             |
   100→| `show_lock_status`         | `true`               | Show lock status section in slot cards                            |
   101→| `show_lock_sync`           | `true`               | Show sync status per lock in lock status                          |
   102→| `collapsed_sections`       | `[]`                 | Which sections start collapsed (empty = all expanded)             |
   103→| `show_lock_cards`          | `true`               | Append lock codes cards below the slot cards                      |
   104→| `code_display`             | `masked_with_reveal` | Code visibility mode for slot cards and lock codes cards          |
   105→
   106→Example view configuration:
   107→
   108→```yaml
   109→strategy:
   110→  type: custom:lock-code-manager
   111→  config_entry_id: 1234567890abcdef
   112→  show_lock_cards: false
   113→  code_display: masked
   114→```
   115→
   116→### Section Strategies
   117→
   118→For advanced users building custom `sections`-type views, Lock Code Manager provides
   119→section strategies that generate cards when Home Assistant renders the section.
   120→
   121→> **Note:** Section strategies simply render a single card (`lcm-slot` or `lcm-lock-codes`)
   122→> within a grid section. You can use the cards directly in your dashboard without using
   123→> section strategies - see the [Slot Card](#slot-card) and [Lock Codes Card](#lock-codes-card)
   124→> sections below.
   125→
   126→#### Slot Section Strategy
   127→
   128→Use `custom:lock-code-manager-slot` to render a single slot section:
   129→
   130→| Option              | Required | Default              | Description                                                   |
   131→| ------------------- | -------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
   132→| `config_entry_id`   | Yes      | -                    | Config entry ID for the LCM instance                          |
   133→| `slot`              | Yes      | -                    | Slot number to display                                        |
   134→| `use_slot_cards`    | No       | `true`               | Use new lcm-slot card (`true`) or legacy entities card        |
   135→| `code_display`      | No       | `masked_with_reveal` | Code visibility mode                                          |
   136→| `show_conditions`   | No       | `true`               | Show conditions section                                       |
   137→| `show_lock_status`  | No       | `true`               | Show lock status section                                      |
   138→| `show_code_sensors` | No       | `true`               | Show code sensors in lock status                              |
   139→| `show_lock_sync`    | No       | `true`               | Show sync status per lock                                     |
   140→| `collapsed_sections`| No       | `[]`                 | Sections to collapse by default: `conditions`, `lock_status`  |
   141→
   142→```yaml
   143→views:
   144→  - type: sections
   145→    sections:
   146→      - strategy:
   147→          type: custom:lock-code-manager-slot
   148→          config_entry_id: 1234567890abcdef
   149→          slot: 1
   150→          code_display: masked_with_reveal
   151→      - strategy:
   152→          type: custom:lock-code-manager-slot
   153→          config_entry_id: 1234567890abcdef
   154→          slot: 2
   155→```
   156→
   157→#### Lock Section Strategy
   158→
   159→Use `custom:lock-code-manager-lock` to render a lock codes section:
   160→
   161→| Option           | Required | Default              | Description                           |
   162→| ---------------- | -------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
   163→| `lock_entity_id` | Yes      | -                    | The entity ID of the lock             |
   164→| `code_display`   | No       | `masked_with_reveal` | Code visibility mode                  |
   165→
   166→```yaml
   167→views:
   168→  - type: sections
   169→    sections:
   170→      - strategy:
   171→          type: custom:lock-code-manager-lock
   172→          lock_entity_id: lock.front_door
   173→          code_display: masked
   174→```
   175→
   176→### Slot Card
   177→
   178→The `lcm-slot` displays a single code slot with inline editing, real-time WebSocket
   179→updates, and collapsible sections for conditions and lock status. This is the default card
   180→used by the strategies when `use_slot_cards: true` (the default).
   181→
   182→| Option               | Required | Default              | Description                                                  |
   183→| -------------------- | -------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
   184→| `config_entry_id`    | Yes*     | -                    | Config entry ID for the LCM instance                         |
   185→| `config_entry_title` | Yes*     | -                    | Config entry title (alternative to ID)                       |
   186→| `slot`               | Yes      | -                    | Slot number to display                                       |
   187→| `code_display`       | No       | `masked_with_reveal` | How to display codes: see modes below                        |
   188→| `show_conditions`    | No       | `true`               | Show the conditions section                                  |
   189→| `show_lock_status`   | No       | `true`               | Show the lock status section                                 |
   190→| `show_code_sensors`  | No       | `true`               | Show code sensors in lock status                             |
   191→| `show_lock_sync`     | No       | `true`               | Show sync status per lock                                    |
   192→| `collapsed_sections` | No       | `[]`                 | Sections to collapse by default: `conditions`, `lock_status` |
   193→
   194→*Either `config_entry_id` or `config_entry_title` is required, but not both.
   195→
   196→Example card configuration:
   197→
   198→```yaml
   199→type: custom:lcm-slot
   200→config_entry_id: 1234567890abcdef
   201→slot: 1
   202→code_display: masked_with_reveal
   203→collapsed_sections:
   204→  - lock_status
   205→```
   206→
   207→### Lock Codes Card
   208→
   209→The `lcm-lock-codes` displays all code slots for a specific lock with status badges,
   210→inline editing for unmanaged slots, and click-to-navigate for LCM-managed slots.
   211→
   212→| Option           | Required | Default              | Description                                    |
   213→| ---------------- | -------- | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
   214→| `lock_entity_id` | Yes      | -                    | The entity ID of the lock to display codes for |
   215→| `title`          | No       | Lock name            | Custom title for the card                      |
   216→| `code_display`   | No       | `masked_with_reveal` | How to display codes: see modes below          |
   217→
   218→Example card configuration:
   219→
   220→```yaml
   221→type: custom:lcm-lock-codes
   222→lock_entity_id: lock.front_door
   223→title: Front Door Codes
   224→code_display: masked_with_reveal
   225→```
   226→
   227→**Code Display Modes:**
   228→
   229→- `masked` - Codes are always hidden (shown as bullets)
   230→- `unmasked` - Codes are always visible
   231→- `masked_with_reveal` - Codes are masked but can be revealed with a toggle button (default)
   232→
   233→## Inspiration
   234→
   235→I spent some time contributing to [keymaster](https://github.com/FutureTense/keymaster),
   236→and what I learned working on it, and the regular complaints users had about it generating
   237→too many automations, entities, etc. led me to take a different approach. This isn't a
   238→knock on `keymaster`, unfortunately a lot of what is built in this integration wasn't
   239→possible for most of `keymaster`'s life. I briefly considered implementing this into
   240→`keymaster` but:
   241→
   242→1. `keymaster` is still a great solution that works as is, and is more feature rich than
   243→   this integration will likely ever be.
   244→2. `keymaster` is surprisingly simple under the hood because it makes Home Assistant do a
   245→   lot of the heavy lifting for figuring out when to enable and disable a usercode. This
   246→   integration, on the other hand, attempts to do all of the heavy lifting internally in
   247→   code, which means it will generate less entities and automations but it is likely more
   248→   fragile to changes in HA Core or even changes in the codebase.
   249→3. It would be impossible to seamlessly migrate users from the current implementation of
   250→   `keymaster` to this integration's implementation. Rewriting `keymaster` to do this
   251→   would have been the equivalent of creating a new integration anyway, and since it's a
   252→   separate integration, users have a choice of what implementation they want to use.
   253→   Additionally, you can install the integrations side by side and slowly migrate your
   254→   locks over in either direction as needed.
   255→
   256→## Thanks
   257→
   258→A big thank you to the other `keymaster` maintainers:
   259→
   260→- @FutureTense
   261→- @firstof9
   262→
   263→As well as the person who created the base concept that `keymaster` evolved from:
   264→@ptdalen
   265→

   211→        if lock_state == clusters.DoorLock.Enums.DlLockState.kUnlatched:
   212→            self._attr_is_locked = False
   213→            self._attr_is_open = True
   214→        elif lock_state == clusters.DoorLock.Enums.DlLockState.kLocked:
   215→            self._attr_is_locked = True

   217→        elif lock_state in (

   219→            clusters.DoorLock.Enums.DlLockState.kNotFullyLocked,

   222→            self._attr_is_open = False
   223→        else:

   225→            # NOTE: A null state can happen during device startup.
   226→            self._attr_is_locked = None
   227→            self._attr_is_open = None

   229→    @callback
   230→    def _reset_optimistic_state(self, write_state: bool = True) -> None:
   231→        if self._optimistic_timer and not self._optimistic_timer.cancelled():
   232→            self._optimistic_timer.cancel()
   233→        self._optimistic_timer = None
   234→        self._attr_is_locking = False
   235→        self._attr_is_unlocking = False
   236→        self._attr_is_opening = False
   237→        if write_state:
   238→            self.async_write_ha_state()

   242→        self,

   245→        feature_map = int(

   248→        # NOTE: the featuremap can dynamically change, so we need to update the

   255→        if bool(feature_map & DoorLockFeature.kUnbolt):

   257→        self._attr_supported_features = supported_features

    31→        static_info = self._static_info
    32→        self._attr_assumed_state = static_info.assumed_state
    33→        self._attr_supported_features = LockEntityFeature(0)
    34→        if static_info.supports_open:

    36→        if static_info.requires_code:

  "new_string": "Locks from the following integrations are currently supported:\n\n- Z-Wave\n- [Virtual](https://github.com/twrecked/hass-virtual) custom integration. See the\n  [Wiki page on this integration](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki/Virtual-integration)\n  for more details on why it was built and how it works.\n\nThe code was written to make it (I think) easy to add support for locks in other\nintegrations. Check the [Wiki](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki) if you\nwant to learn more about that and take a stab at it. Contributors welcome!\n\n### Integrations That Cannot Be Supported\n\nSome integrations cannot support Lock Code Manager due to limitations in the underlying\nlibraries or protocols. The Home Assistant lock platform only requires lock/unlock\noperations - user code management is optional and many integrations don't expose it.\n\n| Integration | Reason |\n|-------------|--------|\n| **ESPHome** | The ESPHome lock component only supports lock/unlock/open commands. User code management would need to be implemented in ESPHome's firmware and API first. |\n| **Matter** | The Home Assistant Matter integration only exposes lock/unlock operations. While the Matter protocol includes a Door Lock cluster with user credential management, this functionality is not exposed in the HA integration or the `python-matter-server` library. |\n| **Yale/August** (`yale`, `yalexs_ble`, `yale_smart_alarm`) | The underlying libraries have limited support. The `yalexs` library can read PINs via `async_get_pins()` but has no methods to create, update, or delete them. The `yalexs-ble` and `yalesmartalarmclient` libraries don't expose any PIN management. Support would require upstream library changes. |\n\nIf you're interested in adding support for one of these integrations, the blocker is\ntypically the underlying Python library - not Lock Code Manager itself. Contributing user\ncode management features to those libraries would enable LCM support."
}

> AGENT

PR created: https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/pull/827

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The research revealed an interesting pattern in smart lock ecosystems:
1. **Protocol support ≠ library support ≠ HA integration support** - Matter has user credential management in the spec, but it's not exposed through the chain
2. **Cloud APIs often restrict write operations** - Yale's `yalexs` can read PINs but not manage them, likely a deliberate API limitation
3. **ESPHome's lock is minimal by design** - DIY focus means simple lock/unlock, no keypad code management
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

     1→Compared to integrations like [Keymaster](https://github.com/futuretense/keymaster), this integration may seem less powerful because it has a limited set of features in comparison. The philosophy with this integration is to avoid reinventing the wheel and trying to own support for features that could be enabled using other mechanisms, like automations.
     2→
     3→In my experience, the majority of additional features that Keymaster provides just reduce the number of automations you need to manually create, but they're also opinionated which means they won't work for every users needs and some users will have to create their own automations anyway. Almost everything (if not everything) that Keymaster natively supports but this integration doesn't can be built by you using automations. Eventually I hope to provide sample automations that you can modify to meet your needs while not having to start from scratch.
     4→
     5→If you identify a feature that can't be automated and would be useful to add to the integration, feel free to open an issue.

{
  "file_path": "/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager.wiki/Unsupported-Integrations.md",
  "content": "# Unsupported Integrations\n\nSome Home Assistant lock integrations cannot support Lock Code Manager due to limitations in\ntheir underlying libraries or protocols. The Home Assistant lock platform only requires\nlock/unlock operations - user code management is optional and many integrations don't\nexpose it.\n\n## ESPHome\n\n**Status:** Not possible\n\nThe ESPHome lock component only supports lock/unlock/open commands. There is no API for\nmanaging user codes on keypads.\n\n**What would need to change:** ESPHome would need to implement user code management in its\nfirmware and expose it through the ESPHome API. This would be a significant feature addition\nto the ESPHome project.\n\n## Matter\n\n**Status:** Not possible (currently)\n\nThe Matter protocol includes a Door Lock cluster with user credential management capabilities.\nHowever, the Home Assistant Matter integration and the underlying `python-matter-server`\nlibrary only expose basic lock/unlock operations - the credential management features are\nnot implemented.\n\n**What would need to change:** The `python-matter-server` library and the Home Assistant\nMatter integration would need to expose the Door Lock cluster's credential management\ncommands (SetCredential, GetCredential, ClearCredential, etc.).\n\n## Yale / August\n\n**Status:** Not possible\n\nThree integrations exist for Yale/August locks:\n\n| Integration | Library | Notes |\n| ----------- | ------- | ----- |\n| `yale` | `yalexs` | Can READ PINs but cannot create/update/delete them |\n| `yalexs_ble` | `yalexs-ble` | Only supports lock/unlock/securemode via Bluetooth |\n| `yale_smart_alarm` | `yalesmartalarmclient` | Can use PIN to unlock, but cannot manage PINs |\n\nThe `yalexs` library is the most promising - it has an `async_get_pins()` method that\nreturns full PIN information including slot numbers, codes, user names, and access schedules.\nHowever, there are no methods to create, update, or delete PINs.\n\n**What would need to change:** The `yalexs` library would need to add PIN management methods.\nThis likely requires reverse-engineering August's undocumented API endpoints for PIN\ncreation and deletion.\n\n## Want to Help?\n\nIf you're interested in adding support for one of these integrations, the blocker is\ntypically the underlying Python library - not Lock Code Manager itself. Contributing user\ncode management features to those upstream libraries would enable LCM support.\n\n- **ESPHome:** [esphome/esphome](https://github.com/esphome/esphome)\n- **Matter:** [home-assistant-libs/python-matter-server](https://github.com/home-assistant-libs/python-matter-server)\n- **Yale/August:** [bdraco/yalexs](https://github.com/bdraco/yalexs)\n"
}

     1→# Integrations That Cannot Currently Be Supported
     2→
     3→Many lock integrations don't yet have Lock Code Manager providers, but could potentially be
     4→added in the future (see [[Adding a Provider|Adding-a-Provider]]). The integrations listed
     5→on this page are different - they **cannot** be supported due to fundamental limitations in
     6→their underlying libraries or protocols.
     7→
     8→The Home Assistant lock platform only requires lock/unlock operations. User code management
     9→is optional, and these integrations don't expose it.
    10→
    11→## ESPHome
    12→
    13→**Status:** Not possible
    14→
    15→The ESPHome lock component only supports lock/unlock/open commands. There is no API for
    16→managing user codes on keypads.
    17→
    18→**What would need to change:** ESPHome would need to implement user code management in its
    19→firmware and expose it through the ESPHome API. This would be a significant feature addition
    20→to the ESPHome project.
    21→
    22→## Matter
    23→
    24→**Status:** Not possible (currently)
    25→
    26→The Matter protocol includes a Door Lock cluster with user credential management capabilities.
    27→However, the Home Assistant Matter integration and the underlying `python-matter-server`
    28→library only expose basic lock/unlock operations - the credential management features are
    29→not implemented.
    30→
    31→**What would need to change:** The `python-matter-server` library and the Home Assistant
    32→Matter integration would need to expose the Door Lock cluster's credential management
    33→commands (SetCredential, GetCredential, ClearCredential, etc.).
    34→
    35→## Yale / August
    36→
    37→**Status:** Not possible
    38→
    39→Three integrations exist for Yale/August locks:
    40→
    41→| Integration | Library | Notes |
    42→| ----------- | ------- | ----- |
    43→| `yale` | `yalexs` | Can READ PINs but cannot create/update/delete them |
    44→| `yalexs_ble` | `yalexs-ble` | Only supports lock/unlock/securemode via Bluetooth |
    45→| `yale_smart_alarm` | `yalesmartalarmclient` | Can use PIN to unlock, but cannot manage PINs |
    46→
    47→The `yalexs` library is the most promising - it has an `async_get_pins()` method that
    48→returns full PIN information including slot numbers, codes, user names, and access schedules.
    49→However, there are no methods to create, update, or delete PINs.
    50→
    51→**What would need to change:** The `yalexs` library would need to add PIN management methods.
    52→This likely requires reverse-engineering August's undocumented API endpoints for PIN
    53→creation and deletion.
    54→
    55→## Want to Help?
    56→
    57→If you're interested in adding support for one of these integrations, the blocker is
    58→typically the underlying Python library - not Lock Code Manager itself. Contributing user
    59→code management features to those upstream libraries would enable LCM support.
    60→
    61→- **ESPHome:** [esphome/esphome](https://github.com/esphome/esphome)
    62→- **Matter:** [home-assistant-libs/python-matter-server](https://github.com/home-assistant-libs/python-matter-server)
    63→- **Yale/August:** [bdraco/yalexs](https://github.com/bdraco/yalexs)
    64→

    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class _SlotState:
        active_state: str
        pin_state: str
        name_state: str | None
        code_state: str
        coordinator_code: int | str | None

    def _resolve_slot_state(
        self, event: Event[EventStateChangedData] | None
    ) -> _SlotState | None:
        """Resolve slot state while applying shared guards."""
        entity_id = event.data["entity_id"] if event else None
        to_state = event.data["new_state"] if event else None

        if not self.coordinator.last_update_success:
            return None

        if not self._build_entity_id_map():
            return None

        if self.is_on is None and int(self.slot_num) not in self.coordinator.data:
            _LOGGER.debug(
                "%s (%s): Slot %s not yet in coordinator data, skipping",
                self.config_entry.entry_id,
                self.config_entry.title,
                self.slot_num,
            )
            return None

        if entity_id is not None and entity_id not in self._tracked_entity_ids:
            return None

        if to_state and to_state.state in (STATE_UNAVAILABLE, STATE_UNKNOWN):
            return None

        if not self._ensure_entities_ready():
            return None

        active_state = self._get_entity_state(ATTR_ACTIVE)
        pin_state = self._get_entity_state(CONF_PIN)
        name_state = self._get_entity_state(CONF_NAME)
        code_state = self._get_entity_state(ATTR_CODE)

        if active_state is None or pin_state is None or code_state is None:
            return None

        coordinator_code = self.coordinator.data.get(int(self.slot_num))
        return self._SlotState(
            active_state=active_state,
            pin_state=pin_state,
            name_state=name_state,
            code_state=code_state,
            coordinator_code=coordinator_code,
        )

    async def _async_update_state(
        self, event: Event[EventStateChangedData] | None = None
    ) -> None:
        """Update binary sensor state by checking dependent entity states.

        On initial load (when is_on is None): Sets sync state without operations.
        On subsequent updates: Requests sync operations from coordinator when out of sync.
        The coordinator handles the actual operations and retry scheduling.
        """
        async with self._lock:
            slot_state = self._resolve_slot_state(event)
            if slot_state is None:
                return

            slot_num = int(self.slot_num)
            # Calculate expected sync state
            expected_in_sync = self._calculate_expected_sync(slot_state)

            # Initial load: Set sync state without performing operations (prevents startup flapping)
            if self.is_on is None:
                # Guard: Verify active state is valid
                if slot_state.active_state not in (STATE_ON, STATE_OFF):
                    _LOGGER.debug(
                        "%s (%s): Active entity for %s slot %s has invalid state '%s'",
                        self.config_entry.entry_id,
                        self.config_entry.title,
                        self.lock.lock.entity_id,
                        self.slot_num,
                        slot_state.active_state,
                    )
                    return

                # Mark initial sync state in coordinator (both synced and out-of-sync)
                if expected_in_sync:
                    self.coordinator.mark_synced(slot_num)
                else:
                    self.coordinator.mark_out_of_sync(slot_num)
                _LOGGER.debug(
                    "%s (%s): Initial state loaded for %s slot %s, in_sync=%s",
                    self.config_entry.entry_id,
                    self.config_entry.title,
                    self.lock.lock.entity_id,
                    self.slot_num,
                    expected_in_sync,
                )
                return

            # Normal operation: Request sync via coordinator if needed
            if not expected_in_sync:
                operation = "set" if slot_state.active_state == STATE_ON else "clear"
                await self.coordinator.async_request_sync(
                    slot_num=slot_num,
                    operation=operation,
                    usercode=slot_state.pin_state if operation == "set" else None,
                    name=slot_state.name_state if operation == "set" else None,
                )

            elif not self.is_on:
                # Was out of sync, now in sync - mark as synced
                self.coordinator.mark_synced(slot_num)

    async def async_added_to_hass(self) -> None:
        """Handle entity added to hass."""
        await BinarySensorEntity.async_added_to_hass(self)
        await BaseLockCodeManagerCodeSlotPerLockEntity.async_added_to_hass(self)
        await CoordinatorEntity.async_added_to_hass(self)

        if self._build_entity_id_map():
            self.async_on_remove(
                async_track_state_change_event(
                    self.hass, self._tracked_entity_ids, self._async_update_state
                )
            )
        else:
            self.async_on_remove(
                async_track_state_change_filtered(
                    self.hass, TrackStates(True, set(), set()), self._async_update_state
                ).async_remove
            )
        await self._async_update_state()

   116→        return None
   117→
   118→    def _get_client_state(self) -> tuple[bool, str]:
   119→        """Return whether the Z-Wave JS client is ready and a retry reason."""
   120→        if self.lock_config_entry.state != ConfigEntryState.LOADED:
   121→            return False, "config entry not loaded"
   122→

   126→        client: Client | None = (

   128→        )
   129→        if not client:

   131→
   132→        if not client.connected:
   133→            return False, "Z-Wave JS client not connected"
   134→
   135→        if client.driver is None:

   137→
   138→        return True, ""

   140→    def _resolve_pin_if_masked(self, value: str, code_slot: int) -> str | None:
   141→        """Resolve a PIN value, looking up expected PIN if masked.
   142→
   143→        Some locks return masked values (all asterisks) instead of the actual PIN.
   144→        This method returns the value as-is if not masked, or looks up the expected
   145→        PIN from LCM entities if masked.
   146→
   147→        Args:
   148→            value: The PIN value (may be masked like "****")
   149→            code_slot: The code slot number
   150→
   151→        Returns:
   152→            The PIN value if not masked, or expected PIN if masked and resolvable
   153→            None if masked but resolution fails
   154→
   155→        """
   156→        # If not masked, return as-is
   157→        if not value or value != "*" * len(value):
   158→            return value
   159→
   160→        # Masked - look up expected PIN from LCM entities
   161→        try:
   162→            config_entry = next(
   163→                entry
   164→                for entry in self.hass.config_entries.async_entries(DOMAIN)
   165→                if self.lock.entity_id in get_entry_data(entry, CONF_LOCKS, [])
   166→                and code_slot in (int(s) for s in get_entry_data(entry, CONF_SLOTS, {}))

   168→        except StopIteration:

   171→        # Use ATTR_ACTIVE binary sensor (not CONF_ENABLED switch) to match what
   172→        # sync logic expects. ATTR_ACTIVE considers conditions, so we only resolve
   173→        # masked codes when sync expects a PIN on the lock.
   174→        base_unique_id = f"{config_entry.entry_id}|{code_slot}"
   175→        active_entity_id = self.ent_reg.async_get_entity_id(
   176→            BINARY_SENSOR_DOMAIN, DOMAIN, f"{base_unique_id}|{ATTR_ACTIVE}"
   177→        )
   178→        pin_entity_id = self.ent_reg.async_get_entity_id(
   179→            TEXT_DOMAIN, DOMAIN, f"{base_unique_id}|{CONF_PIN}"
   180→        )
   181→
   182→        if not active_entity_id or not pin_entity_id:
   183→            return None
   184→
   185→        active_state = self.hass.states.get(active_entity_id)
   186→        pin_state = self.hass.states.get(pin_entity_id)
   187→
   188→        if not active_state or not pin_state:
   189→            return None
   190→
   191→        if active_state.state == STATE_ON and pin_state.state.isnumeric():

   193→                "PIN is masked for lock %s code slot %s, assuming value from PIN entity %s",
   194→                self.lock.entity_id,

   207→
   208→        ready, reason = self._get_client_state()

   218→        @callback
   219→        def on_value_updated(event: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   220→            """Handle value update events from Z-Wave JS."""
   221→            args: dict[str, Any] = event["args"]
   222→            # Filter for User Code CC - handle both userCode and userIdStatus
   223→            if args.get("commandClass") != CommandClass.USER_CODE:
   224→                return
   225→
   226→            property_name = args.get("property")
   227→            if property_name not in (
   228→                LOCK_USERCODE_PROPERTY,
   229→                LOCK_USERCODE_STATUS_PROPERTY,
   230→            ):
   231→                return
   232→
   233→            code_slot = int(args["propertyKey"])
   234→
   235→            # Slot 0 is not a valid user code slot (used for status/metadata)
   236→            if code_slot == 0:

   239→            # Handle userIdStatus updates - slot cleared is a fast path

   241→                status = args.get("newValue")

   244→                    if self.coordinator and self.coordinator.data.get(code_slot) != "":
   245→                        _LOGGER.debug(

   255→            new_value = args.get("newValue")

   257→            if not new_value or (

   272→                    code_slot,

   332→    @callback

   334→        """Filter out events."""
   335→        # Try to find the lock that we are getting an event for, skipping
   336→        # ones that don't match

   339→            event_data[ATTR_HOME_ID] == self.node.client.driver.controller.home_id

   348→            _LOGGER.debug(

   356→        code_slot = params.get("userId", 0)
   357→        self.async_fire_code_slot_event(
   358→            code_slot=code_slot,
   359→            to_locked=next(
   360→                (
   361→                    to_locked
   362→                    for to_locked, codes in ACCESS_CONTROL_NOTIFICATION_TO_LOCKED.items()
   363→                    if evt.data[ATTR_EVENT] in codes
   364→                ),
   365→                None,
   366→            ),
   367→            action_text=evt.data.get(ATTR_EVENT_LABEL),
   368→            source_data=evt,
   369→        )

   399→    async def async_hard_refresh_codes(self) -> dict[int, int | str]:
   400→        """
   401→        Perform hard refresh and return all codes.
   402→
   403→        Uses Z-Wave JS's refresh_cc_values which handles checksum optimization
   404→        internally - it will skip re-fetching codes if the checksum hasn't changed.
   405→        Returns codes in the same format as async_get_usercodes().

   410→    async def async_set_usercode(
   411→        self, code_slot: int, usercode: int | str, name: str | None = None
   412→    ) -> bool:
   413→        """
   414→        Set a usercode on a code slot.
   415→
   416→        Returns True if the value was changed, False if already set to this value.
   417→        """
   418→        # Check if the code is already set to this value (avoid unnecessary network call)
   419→        usercode = str(usercode)
   420→        try:
   421→            if (current := get_usercode(self.node, code_slot)).get("in_use"):
   422→                current_code = str(current.get("usercode", ""))
   423→                # Resolve masked codes and compare
   424→                if usercode == self._resolve_pin_if_masked(current_code, code_slot):
   425→                    _LOGGER.debug(
   426→                        "Lock %s slot %s already has this PIN, skipping set",
   427→                        self.lock.entity_id,
   428→                        code_slot,
   429→                    )
   430→                    return False
   431→        except Exception:
   432→            # If we can't check the cache, proceed with the set
   433→            pass
   434→
   435→        service_data = {
   436→            ATTR_ENTITY_ID: self.lock.entity_id,
   437→            ATTR_CODE_SLOT: code_slot,
   438→            ATTR_USERCODE: usercode,
   439→        }
   440→        await self.async_call_service(
   441→            ZWAVE_JS_DOMAIN, SERVICE_SET_LOCK_USERCODE, service_data
   442→        )
   443→        return True
   444→
   445→    async def async_clear_usercode(self, code_slot: int) -> bool:
   446→        """
   447→        Clear a usercode on a code slot.
   448→
   449→        Returns True if the value was changed, False if already cleared.
   450→        """
   451→        # Check if the slot is already cleared (avoid unnecessary network call)
   452→        try:
   453→            current = get_usercode(self.node, code_slot)
   454→            if not current.get("in_use"):
   455→                _LOGGER.debug(
   456→                    "Lock %s slot %s already cleared, skipping clear",
   457→                    self.lock.entity_id,
   458→                    code_slot,
   459→                )
   460→                return False
   461→        except Exception:
   462→            # If we can't check the cache, proceed with the clear
   463→            pass
   464→
   465→        service_data = {
   466→            ATTR_ENTITY_ID: self.lock.entity_id,
   467→            ATTR_CODE_SLOT: code_slot,
   468→        }
   469→        await self.async_call_service(
   470→            ZWAVE_JS_DOMAIN, SERVICE_CLEAR_LOCK_USERCODE, service_data
   471→        )
   472→        return True

   474→    def _get_usercodes_from_cache(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   475→        """Get usercodes from Z-Wave JS value DB cache."""
   476→        try:
   477→            return list(get_usercodes(self.node) or [])
   478→        except Exception as err:
   479→            raise LockDisconnected from err

   481→    async def _async_refresh_usercode_cache(self) -> None:
   482→        """Refresh usercode cache from the device."""
   483→        try:
   484→            await self.node.async_refresh_cc_values(CommandClass.USER_CODE)
   485→        except Exception as err:
   486→            raise LockDisconnected from err
   487→
   488→    async def async_get_usercodes(self) -> dict[int, int | str]:
   489→        """Get dictionary of code slots and usercodes."""
   490→        code_slots = {
   491→            int(code_slot)
   492→            for entry in self.hass.config_entries.async_entries(DOMAIN)
   493→            for code_slot in get_entry_data(entry, CONF_SLOTS, {})
   494→            if self.lock.entity_id in get_entry_data(entry, CONF_LOCKS, [])
   495→        }
   496→        data: dict[int, int | str] = {}
   497→
   498→        if not await self.async_is_connection_up():
   499→            raise LockDisconnected
   500→
   501→        slots = self._get_usercodes_from_cache()
   502→        slots_by_num = {int(slot["code_slot"]): slot for slot in slots}
   503→
   504→        # If any configured slot is missing or has unknown state, do one hard
   505→        # refresh to populate the cache. This is more efficient than fetching
   506→        # individual slots and uses Z-Wave JS's checksum optimization.
   507→        # Note: We call _async_refresh_usercode_cache directly here to avoid
   508→        # recursion since async_hard_refresh_codes calls async_get_usercodes.
   509→        if any(
   510→            slot_num not in slots_by_num or slots_by_num[slot_num].get("in_use") is None
   511→            for slot_num in code_slots
   512→        ):
   513→            _LOGGER.debug(
   514→                "Lock %s has missing/unknown slots, performing hard refresh",
   515→                self.lock.entity_id,
   516→            )
   517→            await self._async_refresh_usercode_cache()
   518→            slots = self._get_usercodes_from_cache()
   519→            slots_by_num = {int(slot["code_slot"]): slot for slot in slots}
   520→
   521→        for slot in slots:
   522→            code_slot = int(slot["code_slot"])
   523→            usercode: str = slot["usercode"] or ""
   524→            in_use: bool | None = slot["in_use"]
   525→
   526→            if not in_use:
   527→                data[code_slot] = ""
   528→            # Resolve PIN (handles masked codes), skip if unresolvable
   529→            elif resolved := self._resolve_pin_if_masked(usercode, code_slot):
   530→                data[code_slot] = resolved
   531→
   532→        slots_with_pin = [s for s, v in data.items() if v]
   533→        slots_not_enabled = [s for s, v in data.items() if not v]
   534→        _LOGGER.debug(
   535→            "Lock %s: %s slots with PIN %s, %s slots not enabled %s",
   536→            self.lock.entity_id,
   537→            len(slots_with_pin),
   538→            slots_with_pin,
   539→            len(slots_not_enabled),
   540→            slots_not_enabled,
   541→        )
   542→        return data
   543→

    51→@dataclass(repr=False, eq=False)
    52→class BaseLock:
    53→    """
    54→    Base class for lock provider implementations.
    55→
    56→    Data Fetching Modes
    57→    -------------------
    58→    The coordinator supports three update modes. All modes include an initial poll.
    59→
    60→    1. Poll for updates (default):
    61→       - Periodic calls to get_usercodes() at usercode_scan_interval
    62→       - Used when supports_push = False
    63→       - Suitable for integrations without real-time events
    64→
    65→    2. Push for updates:
    66→       - Real-time value updates via subscribe_push_updates()
    67→       - Enabled when supports_push = True
    68→       - Disables periodic polling (poll for updates)
    69→       - Updates pushed via coordinator.push_update({slot: value})
    70→
    71→    3. Poll for drift:
    72→       - Periodic hard_refresh_codes() at hard_refresh_interval
    73→       - Detects out-of-band changes (e.g., codes changed at keypad)
    74→       - Runs regardless of push/poll mode
    75→       - Set hard_refresh_interval = None to disable
    76→
    77→    4. Poll connection state:
    78→       - Periodic async_internal_is_connection_up() at connection_check_interval
    79→       - Helps detect reconnects for integrations without config entry state signals
    80→       - Set connection_check_interval = None to disable
    81→
    82→    Configuration Examples
    83→    ----------------------
    84→    Poll-only (default):
    85→        supports_push = False
    86→        usercode_scan_interval = timedelta(minutes=1)
    87→        hard_refresh_interval = None
    88→        connection_check_interval = timedelta(seconds=30)
    89→
    90→    Push with drift detection (recommended for Z-Wave JS):
    91→        supports_push = True
    92→        hard_refresh_interval = timedelta(hours=1)
    93→        connection_check_interval = None
    94→        # Override subscribe_push_updates() to handle value events
    95→
    96→    Poll with drift detection:
    97→        supports_push = False
    98→        usercode_scan_interval = timedelta(minutes=1)
    99→        hard_refresh_interval = timedelta(hours=1)
   100→        connection_check_interval = timedelta(seconds=30)
   101→
   102→    Exception Handling
   103→    ------------------
   104→    Provider implementations should raise LockCodeManagerError (or subclasses like
   105→    LockDisconnected) for lock communication failures. The coordinator catches
   106→    LockCodeManagerError and handles it appropriately (e.g., retrying, logging).
   107→
   108→    Do NOT raise generic exceptions or HomeAssistantError directly - always use
   109→    LCM-derived exceptions so the coordinator can distinguish lock failures from
   110→    other errors.

   112→

   132→        """Run a sync method in the executor."""

   139→    async def _execute_rate_limited(
   140→        self,
   141→        operation_type: Literal["get", "set", "clear", "refresh"],
   142→        func: Callable[..., Awaitable[Any]],
   143→        *args: Any,

### 2. Z-WAVE JS PROVIDER IMPLEMENTATION

**File: `/Users/raman/projects/keymaster/custom_components/keymaster/providers/zwave_js.py`**

**Class: `ZWaveJSLockProvider` (lines 44-402)** - Full Z-Wave JS implementation with advanced features

**Connection & State Management** (lines 78-186):
- `async_connect()`: Multi-step connection process
  1. Validates lock entity exists in registry
  2. Retrieves lock's config entry ID
  3. Accesses Z-Wave JS client from config entry runtime data
  4. Verifies client connectivity and controller availability
  5. Resolves device from device registry
  6. Extracts node ID from device identifiers
  7. Retrieves node from Z-Wave controller
  - Returns boolean success status

- `async_is_connected()`: Validates all components remain connected (client, driver, controller, node)

**Capabilities Declaration** (lines 58-66):
- `supports_push_updates = True`: Provides real-time events
- `supports_connection_status = True`: Reports connection status
- `domain = "zwave_js"`

**Usercode Operations** (lines 187-323):

1. **`async_get_usercodes()`** (lines 187-218)
   - Calls `get_usercodes(node)` from zwave_js_server
   - Converts Z-Wave JS CodeSlots to platform-agnostic CodeSlots
   - Handles FailedZWaveCommand exceptions
   - Returns list of CodeSlot objects

2. **`async_get_usercode(slot_num)`** (lines 220-239)
   - Get single slot (uses cached data)
   - Handles BaseZwaveJSServerError exceptions

3. **`async_refresh_usercode(slot_num)`** (lines 241-260)
   - Bypasses cache via `get_usercode_from_node()`
   - Forces device query for latest data
   - Used for cache invalidation

4. **`async_set_usercode(slot_num, code, name)`** (lines 262-283)
   - Calls `set_usercode(node, slot_num, code)` from zwave_js_server
   - No support for slot naming in Z-Wave

- Uses quick refresh cycles (configurable via `QUICK_REFRESH_SECONDS`) after sync operations

**Parent/Child Lock Support**:
- Parent locks can control child locks
- Child slots can override parent
- Settings propagate from parent to non-override child slots
- Prevents clearing parent PIN when child can't be updated

**Access Limiting**:
- Count-based limits (remaining access count)
- Date range limits (start/end dates)
- Day-of-week limits (specific days enabled/disabled)
- Time-based limits (include/exclude time windows)

**Async/Thread-Safe Operations**:
- All provider methods are async
- Coordinator uses async dataclass pattern
- JSON persistence in executor thread pool
- PIN encoding with salted base64 (coordinator.py:190-201)

Now I have a comprehensive view of both implementations. Let me provide a detailed comparison.

## Comparison: LCM vs Keymaster Lock Provider Models

### Architecture Overview

| Aspect | Keymaster | LCM |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base class | `BaseLockProvider` | `BaseLock` |
| Data format | `CodeSlot` dataclass (slot_num, code, in_use, name) | Simple dict `{slot: code}` |
| Connection | Explicit `async_connect()` returning bool | Implicit via `is_connection_up()` checks |
| Rate limiting | None | Built-in 2s minimum delay |
| Push updates | Lock events only | Full usercode value updates |

---

### Functionality Keymaster Has That LCM Lacks

**1. CodeSlot Structured Data**
```python
# Keymaster - richer metadata
@dataclass
class CodeSlot:
    slot_num: int
    code: str | None = None
    in_use: bool = False  # Explicit occupied state
    name: str | None = None  # Slot name from lock
```
LCM uses `dict[int, int | str]` which loses the `in_use` flag as separate state and slot names from the lock itself.

**2. Explicit Connection Method**
```python
# Keymaster
async def async_connect(self) -> bool:
    """Multi-step connection establishment"""
    
# LCM - no equivalent, just checks
async def async_is_connection_up(self) -> bool:
```
Keymaster's explicit connect allows lazy initialization and better connection lifecycle control.

**3. Single-Slot Refresh**
```python
# Keymaster
async def async_refresh_usercode(slot_num: int) -> CodeSlot
    """Bypass cache for one slot"""
    
# LCM - only bulk refresh
async def hard_refresh_codes(self) -> dict[int, int | str]:
    """Refresh ALL slots"""
```
Could be more efficient when only one slot needs verification.

**4. Connection Event Subscription**
```python
# Keymaster
ConnectionCallback = Callable[[bool], None]
def subscribe_connection_events(self, callback: ConnectionCallback) -> Callable[[], None]
```
LCM uses config entry state listener instead, which works for Z-Wave JS but may not work for all integrations.

**5. Diagnostic Data Method**
```python
# Keymaster
def get_platform_data(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Provider-specific diagnostic data"""
    return {
        "node_id": self.get_node_id(),
        "node_status": self.get_node_status(),
        ...
    }
```
LCM has no equivalent for exposing diagnostic info.

---

### Functionality LCM Has That Keymaster Lacks

**1. Built-in Rate Limiting** (`_base.py:139-172`)
```python
async def _execute_rate_limited(self, operation_type, func, *args, **kwargs):
    """Serialize operations with 2s delay"""
```
Prevents overwhelming Z-Wave network with rapid operations.

**2. Full Push Update Model** (`zwave_js.py:201-290`)
```python
@callback
def subscribe_push_updates(self) -> None:
    """Subscribe to User Code CC value updates"""
    self._value_update_unsub = self.node.on("value updated", on_value_updated)
```
LCM receives real-time usercode changes, not just lock/unlock events. Keymaster only gets events when lock is used.

**3. Change Detection Return Values** (`_base.py:463-543`)
```python
async def async_set_usercode(self, ...) -> bool:
    """Returns True if changed, False if already at target"""
```
Allows coordinator to skip refresh when no change occurred.

**4. Provider-Level Masked Code Resolution** (`zwave_js.py:140-199`)
```python
def _resolve_pin_if_masked(self, value: str, code_slot: int) -> str | None:
    """Resolve **** to expected PIN from LCM entities"""
```
Keymaster handles this in coordinator; LCM handles at provider level.

**5. Auto-Resubscription on Config Entry Reload** (`_base.py:369-400`)
```python
def _setup_config_entry_state_listener(self) -> None:
    """Resubscribe when provider integration reloads"""
```

**6. Connection Transition Tracking** (`_base.py:406-424`)
```python
async def async_internal_is_connection_up(self) -> bool:
    """Track connection transitions for auto-resubscription"""
    if self._last_connection_up is False and is_up:
        self.subscribe_push_updates()  # Reconnected
```

---

### Implementation Differences Worth Noting

**Z-Wave JS Usercode Retrieval:**
```python
# Keymaster - calls zwave_js_server directly
usercodes = get_usercodes(node)  # Returns CodeSlot list

# LCM - also uses zwave_js_server but via services for set/clear
await self.async_call_service(ZWAVE_JS_DOMAIN, SERVICE_SET_LOCK_USERCODE, ...)
```

**Event Handling:**
```python
# Keymaster - callback model
def subscribe_lock_events(self, kmlock, callback):
    """callback(code_slot_num, event_label, action_code)"""
    
# LCM - fires to HA event bus
self.async_fire_code_slot_event(code_slot, to_locked, action_text, source_data)
```

---

### Potential LCM Deficiencies to Consider

1. **Loss of `in_use` metadata**: The dict format loses explicit slot status. An empty string means "not in use" but some locks distinguish between "never programmed" vs "cleared".

2. **No single-slot refresh**: Could be inefficient when verifying just one slot changed.

3. **No explicit connect/disconnect**: Makes it harder for providers that need initialization steps.

4. **No diagnostic data export**: Harder to troubleshoot provider-specific issues.

5. **Tighter coupling**: `async_fire_code_slot_event()` in base class directly accesses LCM config entries and entities, which keymaster avoids by using callbacks.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
LCM's architecture prioritizes **real-time synchronization** (push updates, rate limiting, masked code resolution) while keymaster prioritizes **flexibility** (callbacks, structured data, explicit lifecycle). LCM's approach is more opinionated but handles edge cases like masked codes and rapid operations better out of the box.

   243→### Add Optional Flags to `get_config_entry_data` Websocket Command
   244→
   245→**Context:** PR #787 consolidated multiple websocket commands into a single
   246→`get_config_entry_data` command that returns `{config_entry, entities, locks, slots}`.
   247→However, not all callers need all the data:
   248→
   249→| Caller | config_entry | entities | locks | slots |
   250→| ------ | ------------ | -------- | ----- | ----- |
   251→| `view-strategy.ts` | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |
   252→| `generate-view.ts` | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
   253→| `slot-section-strategy.ts` (legacy) | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ |
   254→| `dashboard-strategy.ts` | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ |
   255→| `lock-codes-card-editor.ts` | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ |
   256→
   257→**Cost Analysis:**
   258→
   259→- `config_entry` - Very cheap (just `config_entry.as_json_fragment`)
   260→- `slots` - Very cheap (extracts calendar IDs from config)
   261→- `locks` - Moderate (iterates locks, gets friendly names via state lookups)
   262→- `entities` - Most expensive (queries entity registry, maps to `as_partial_dict`)
   263→
   264→**Proposed Change:** Add optional `include_entities` and `include_locks` flags
   265→(default `True` for backwards compatibility). Skip `config_entry` and `slots`
   266→flags since they're essentially free.
   267→
   268→```python
   269→vol.Optional("include_entities", default=True): bool,
   270→vol.Optional("include_locks", default=True): bool,
   271→```
   272→
   273→**Benefits:**
   274→
   275→- `view-strategy.ts` can skip both entities and locks
   276→- `dashboard-strategy.ts` and `lock-codes-card-editor.ts` can skip entities
   277→- Legacy `slot-section-strategy.ts` can skip locks
   278→
   279→**Estimated Effort:** Low (2-4 hours)
   280→**Priority:** Low
   281→**Status:** Not started

   304→| -------------- | -------- |
   305→| `calendar` | One-time events, external calendar sync (existing) |

   315→   - `entity`: EntitySelector filtered to `binary_sensor`, `input_boolean`
   316→
   317→2. **Binary Sensor Changes:**
   318→   - Update `_get_entity_state()` to handle different condition types

   323→   - Add `condition_type` field: `calendar | schedule | entity`
   324→   - Add `condition_entity` field (alternative to `calendar`)

   341→### Advanced Calendar Configuration
   342→
   343→**Feature Request:** Allow slot number and PIN to be configured directly in
   344→calendar event metadata, eliminating need for separate slot configuration.
   345→
   346→**Design Considerations:**
   347→
   348→**Current Behavior:**
   349→
   350→- Slot configured in config flow with fixed PIN
   351→- Calendar event (when present) only controls whether slot is active/inactive
   352→- PIN and slot number are static configuration
   353→
   354→**Proposed Behavior:**
   355→
   356→- Calendar event contains slot number and PIN in its metadata
   357→- User configures regex/pattern to extract slot number and PIN from:
   358→  - Event title (e.g., "Slot 3: 1234")
   359→  - Event description
   360→  - Event location
   361→  - Custom calendar properties
   362→
   363→**Implementation Requirements:**
   364→
   365→1. **Config Flow Changes:**
   366→   - Add "advanced calendar mode" toggle per slot
   367→   - When enabled, show pattern configuration UI
   368→   - Pattern fields: slot number regex, PIN regex, which field to parse
   369→     (title/description/location)
   370→2. **Entity Changes:**
   371→   - Calendar event listener needs to parse event metadata
   372→   - Extract slot number and PIN based on user-defined patterns
   373→   - Validate extracted values (numeric slot, PIN format)
   374→3. **Binary Sensor Changes:**
   375→   - Check if calendar event contains valid extracted values
   376→   - Use extracted PIN instead of configured PIN
   377→   - Handle multiple calendar events with different slots
   378→
   379→**Example Patterns:**
   380→
   381→- Title: "Guest Access: Slot 5, PIN 9876" -> Slot: `\d+`, PIN: `\d{4}$`
   382→- Description: "Code: 1234 for slot 3" -> Slot: `slot (\d+)`, PIN: `Code: (\d+)`
   383→- Location: "5:1234" -> Slot: `^(\d+):`, PIN: `:(\d+)$`
   384→
   385→**Challenges:**
   386→
   387→- Multiple calendar events with different slots
   388→- Error handling for invalid patterns
   389→- UI for testing patterns
   390→- Backward compatibility with existing simple calendar mode

**5. Explaining the coupling in `async_fire_code_slot_event()`:**

The issue is in `_base.py:638-740`. The base class method directly accesses LCM-specific data:

```python
# Lines 659-684 - Base class iterates LCM config entries
config_entry = next(
    config_entry
    for config_entry in self.hass.config_entries.async_entries(DOMAIN)
    if (
        self.lock.entity_id in get_entry_data(config_entry, CONF_LOCKS, [])
        and code_slot is not None
        and int(code_slot) in (
            int(slot) for slot in get_entry_data(config_entry, CONF_SLOTS, {})
        )
        and (
            name_entity_id := self.ent_reg.async_get_entity_id(
                TEXT_DOMAIN, DOMAIN, f"{config_entry.entry_id}|{code_slot}|{CONF_NAME}"
            )
        )
    )
)
```

**Current Design (coupled):**
- Provider calls `self.async_fire_code_slot_event(code_slot, to_locked, ...)`
- Base class finds matching LCM config entry, resolves slot name entity, builds event data
- Base class fires event to HA bus

**Keymaster Design (decoupled):**
- Provider calls `callback(code_slot_num, event_label, action_code)` 
- Coordinator/consumer receives callback, has all context to build event
- Provider doesn't know about keymaster internals

**Two possible changes:**

### Option A: Move to callback model (like keymaster)

```python
# In BaseLock - provider just notifies
@callback
def _notify_code_slot_used(
    self, code_slot: int, to_locked: bool | None, action_text: str | None, ...
) -> None:
    """Notify that a code slot was used."""
    if self._code_slot_callback:
        self._code_slot_callback(code_slot, to_locked, action_text, ...)

# Coordinator registers callback during setup
lock_provider.set_code_slot_callback(self._handle_code_slot_event)
```

**Pros:** Clean separation, base class has no LCM knowledge
**Cons:** More indirection, callback registration boilerplate

### Option B: Keep current design but document the contract

The current design is actually intentional - it centralizes event building so providers don't need to know about LCM entities. The base class acts as an "LCM-aware adapter" rather than a pure abstraction.

**Pros:** Simple for provider implementers, consistent event format
**Cons:** Base class is LCM-specific (but it's in the LCM codebase anyway)

---

**My recommendation:** Option B - keep current design. The base class is already LCM-specific (it imports from `..const`, `..data`, etc.). The coupling is intentional and provides a convenience for provider authors. A new provider just calls `self.async_fire_code_slot_event(code_slot, to_locked, action_text, source_data)` without knowing LCM internals.

If you wanted to make providers truly reusable across projects (like keymaster's model), Option A would be better. But since this is LCM's codebase, the current design seems pragmatic.

Does this answer your question, or would you like me to elaborate on either option?

should BaseLock be an ABC subclass? can a class be an ABC subclass and a dataclass?

> AGENT

Good questions. Let me check the current implementation and answer both.

**Can a class be both ABC and dataclass?**

Yes, they work together:

```python
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass
class MyBase(ABC):
    field: str
    
    @abstractmethod
    def required_method(self) -> str:
        pass
```

The `@dataclass` decorator adds `__init__`, `__repr__`, etc., while `ABC` with `ABCMeta` enforces abstract method implementation. No conflict.

**Should BaseLock be an ABC?**

> AGENT

Looking at the methods:

| Method | Current Behavior | Should be Abstract? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `domain` property | `raise NotImplementedError()` | Yes - always required |
| `is_connection_up()` | `raise NotImplementedError()` | Yes - always required |
| `get_usercodes()` | `_raise_not_implemented()` | Yes - core functionality |
| `set_usercode()` | `_raise_not_implemented()` | Yes - core functionality |
| `clear_usercode()` | `_raise_not_implemented()` | Yes - core functionality |
| `subscribe_push_updates()` | `_raise_not_implemented()` | No - only if `supports_push=True` |
| `unsubscribe_push_updates()` | `_raise_not_implemented()` | No - only if `supports_push=True` |
| `hard_refresh_codes()` | `_raise_not_implemented()` | No - only if `hard_refresh_interval` is set |

**Recommendation:** Make `BaseLock` an ABC with the core methods as abstract. The conditional methods (push, hard refresh) should stay as runtime errors since ABC doesn't support "conditionally abstract" methods.

```python
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod

@dataclass(repr=False, eq=False)
class BaseLock(ABC):
    ...
    
    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def domain(self) -> str:
        """Return integration domain."""
    
    @abstractmethod
    def is_connection_up(self) -> bool:
        """Return whether connection to lock is up."""
    
    @abstractmethod
    def get_usercodes(self) -> dict[int, int | str]:
        """Get dictionary of code slots and usercodes."""
    
    @abstractmethod
    def set_usercode(self, code_slot: int, usercode: int | str, name: str | None = None) -> bool:
        """Set a usercode on a code slot."""
    
    @abstractmethod
    def clear_usercode(self, code_slot: int) -> bool:
        """Clear a usercode on a code slot."""
```

**Benefits:**
- Catches missing implementations at class definition time, not runtime
- Better IDE support (shows required methods to implement)
- Clearer contract for provider authors

   369→    def _setup_config_entry_state_listener(self) -> None:
   370→        """Listen for provider config entry state changes to resubscribe."""
   371→        lock_entry = self.lock_config_entry

   375→        self._last_entry_state = lock_entry.state

   377→        @callback
   378→        def _handle_state_change() -> None:
   379→            to_state = lock_entry.state
   380→            if to_state == self._last_entry_state:
   381→                return
   382→
   383→            if to_state == ConfigEntryState.LOADED:
   384→                if self.coordinator:
   385→                    self.hass.async_create_task(
   386→                        self.coordinator.async_request_refresh(),
   387→                        f"Refresh coordinator for {self.lock.entity_id} after reload",
   388→                    )
   389→                if self.supports_push:
   390→                    self.subscribe_push_updates()
   391→            elif (
   392→                self.supports_push and self._last_entry_state == ConfigEntryState.LOADED
   393→            ):
   394→                self.unsubscribe_push_updates()
   395→
   396→            self._last_entry_state = to_state

   399→            _handle_state_change
   400→        )

   638→    @final

   641→        self,

   643→        to_locked: bool | None = None,
   644→        action_text: str | None = None,
   645→        source_data: Event | State | dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   646→    ) -> None:
   647→        """

   651→        include any data that is JSON serializable if the source is not a Home

   658→
   659→        try:
   660→            config_entry = next(
   661→                config_entry
   662→                for config_entry in self.hass.config_entries.async_entries(DOMAIN)
   663→                if (
   664→                    self.lock.entity_id in get_entry_data(config_entry, CONF_LOCKS, [])
   665→                    and code_slot is not None
   666→                    and int(code_slot)
   667→                    in (

   669→                        for slot in get_entry_data(config_entry, CONF_SLOTS, {})
   670→                    )

   673→                            TEXT_DOMAIN,
   674→                            DOMAIN,
   675→                            f"{config_entry.entry_id}|{code_slot}|{CONF_NAME}",
   676→                        )
   677→                    )
   678→                )
   679→            )

   693→            to_state = LockState.UNLOCKED

   709→            else:

   711→            extra_data = {

   713→                "state": source_data.state,
   714→                "attributes": source_data.attributes,
   715→                "last_changed": last_changed_isoformat,
   716→                "last_updated": last_updated_isoformat,

   718→        elif isinstance(source_data, dict):

   723→            ATTR_ENTITY_ID: lock_entity_id,
   724→            ATTR_DEVICE_ID: lock_device_id,
   725→            ATTR_LCM_CONFIG_ENTRY_ID: config_entry_id,
   726→            ATTR_STATE: (

> AGENT

I see the issue. Both VirtualLock and ZWaveJSLock only override the **async** versions, not the sync versions. The base class design allows either:
1. Implement sync → base async calls it via executor
2. Override async directly → sync never called

Both providers use approach 2, so making sync methods abstract breaks them.

**Two options:**

1. **Only make `domain` abstract** - safest, backward compatible
2. **Make all methods abstract + add stubs to providers** - more work, proper ABC

Let me revert the sync methods and only keep `domain` abstract for now, since that's the only truly universal requirement:

   211→async def test_rate_limiting_set_usercode(
   212→    hass: HomeAssistant,
   213→    mock_lock_config_entry,
   214→    lock_code_manager_config_entry,
   215→):
   216→    """Test that operations are rate limited with minimum delay between calls."""

   219→
   220→    # Set a smaller delay for testing
   221→    lock_provider._min_operation_delay = TEST_OPERATION_DELAY
   222→
   223→    # Reset the last operation time to ensure clean test
   224→    lock_provider._last_operation_time = 0.0
   225→
   226→    # First operation should execute immediately
   227→    start_time = time.monotonic()
   228→    await lock_provider.async_internal_set_usercode(1, "1111", "Test 1")
   229→    first_duration = time.monotonic() - start_time
   230→
   231→    # First operation should be fast (< 0.2 seconds without rate limiting delay)
   232→    assert first_duration < 0.2
   233→
   234→    # Second operation should be rate limited
   235→    start_time = time.monotonic()
   236→    await lock_provider.async_internal_set_usercode(2, "2222", "Test 2")
   237→    second_duration = time.monotonic() - start_time
   238→
   239→    # Second operation should take at least the rate limit time
   240→    assert second_duration >= TEST_OPERATION_DELAY
   241→
   242→    # Verify both operations completed
   243→    assert (
   244→        len(hass.data[LOCK_DATA][LOCK_1_ENTITY_ID]["service_calls"]["set_usercode"])
   245→        == 2
   246→    )

> AGENT

PR created: https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/pull/832

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
Python's `ABC` works seamlessly with `@dataclass` because they operate at different levels - ABC sets the metaclass for abstract method enforcement, while dataclass is a decorator that generates `__init__`, `__repr__`, etc. The key constraint with abstract methods in this codebase is the sync/async duality: since providers can implement either the sync method (for executor-based calls) or override the async method directly, only truly universal requirements like `domain` should be abstract.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

> DEVELOPER

we only have one abstract method which is a property. Is there any other benefit to ABC? If not we should probably just close this PR or clean up the docstrings in this PR and change the title/description

> AGENT

Good question. With only `domain` as abstract, the main benefits of ABC are:

1. **Prevents accidental instantiation** - `BaseLock(...)` fails immediately at instantiation, not later when `domain` is accessed
2. **Signals intent** - Documents that BaseLock is meant to be subclassed

For just one property, this might be overkill. Options:

1. **Keep ABC as-is** - The "cannot instantiate" benefit is real, even for one property
2. **Close PR** - If the overhead isn't worth it
3. **Keep ABC + clean up** - Update docstrings to explain why ABC with one abstract property, update PR title/description

What's your preference? If you want to keep it, I can clean up the docstrings to add a note explaining the design choice (ABC for instantiation prevention + future abstract methods as the sync/async pattern evolves).

A node supporting the Door Lock Command Class SHOULD reflect user code inputs in the door lock
status when relevant. (e.g. when the door becomes unlocked by a User Code input, the Door Lock
Mode is also updated to unlocked)
This Command Class can be used in conjunction with Schedule Entry Lock Command Class in order
to schedule access for users.

(B[mnew User ID Statuses, keypad modes and a Admin Code functionality.
2.2.116.1 Terminology
User Codes are configured on a supporting node for different User Identifiers. Each User Code is
associated to one User Identifier. An actual end user with several User Codes will also have several
User Identifiers (one for each User Code).
The entry of a user code can trigger different outcomes, such as opening a door, triggering a notification
or ignoring the code. This can be configured with the User ID status.
A supporting node may support one or several Keypad Modes. They allow configuring the keypad to
accept, ignore or treat differently keypad input.
A node may support the Admin Code functionality. The Admin Code is a separate unique code used
to get access to the node’s administrator functionalities, such as the network settings and/or User
Code management. A node may require the Admin Code to be always set and in this case advertise
that the Admin Code can be modified but cannot be deactivated using Z-Wave.
A node may support the User Code Checksum functionality. A controlling node can request a checksum representing all the user code set at the supporting node to ensure that the user code databases
are synchronized.
2.2.116.2 Compatibility Considerations
The User Code Command Class, version 2 is backwards compatible with User Code Command Class,
version 1.
CC:0063.02.00.21.001

All commands and fields not mentioned in this version MUST remain unchanged User Code Command
Class, version 1.
The Extended User Code Set Command permits to configure several user codes per command. The
following command has been extended to match the extended number of supported users:
• User Code Report Command
The following commands are also introduced to address the extended range of users:
• Extended User Code Set Command
• Extended User Code Get Command
• Extended User Code Report Command
Commands for advertising node capabilities, configuring the keypad mode and the Admin Code are
introduced:
• User Code Capabilities Get Command
• User Code Capabilities Report Command
• User Code Keypad Mode Get Command
• User Code Keypad Mode Report Command
• Admin Code Set Command
• Admin Code Get Command
• Admin Code Report Command

CC:0063.02.00.21.002

CC:0063.02.00.21.003

CC:0063.02.00.21.004

Application Work Group Z-Wave Specifications, Release 2023A

January 24, 2023

User Code Command Class, version 2 does not extend the existing User Code Set/Get/Report commands from version 1. The first 255 users that can be addressed by the User Code Set/Get Commands
MUST be identical to the first 255 users that can be addressed by the (version 2) Extended User Code
Set/Get Commands.
Addressing User Codes for extended User Identifiers (in the range 256..65535) MUST be done with
the (version 2) Extended User Code Set/Get Commands.
A version 1 node MAY advertise support for 0 User Codes in the Users Number Report Command.
A version 2 node MUST advertise support for at least 1 User Code.

CC:0063.02.00.21.005

The implemented User Identifier values MUST be in a sequence starting from 1, i.e. a node supporting
10 Users MUST accept User Identifier values in the range 1..10. However, a controlling node MAY
assign user codes non-continuously in the range of supported User Identifier.
2.2.116.3 Interoperability Considerations
This Command Class can be used in conjunction with the Entry Control Command Class to report
User Code input to a controlling application.

CC:0063.02.00.31.001

CC:0063.02.00.31.005

A node supporting the “Messaging” User ID Status MUST support the Entry Control Command
Class, version 1 or newer or the Notification Command Class, version 8 or newer.
A node supporting this Command Class MUST either:
• Support the Door Lock Command Class.
• Control the Door Lock Command Class via association groups.

CC:0063.02.00.31.003

CC:0063.02.00.33.001

A supporting node MUST reflect user code inputs in the door lock status when relevant. (e.g. when
the door becomes unsecured by a User Code input, the Door Lock Operation mode is updated to
unsecure with a timeout)
A node supporting this Command Class MAY have an Association group issuing the corresponding
Door Lock Operation Set Commands when valid User Codes are input in order to control several door
locks simultaneously.
This Command Class can be used in conjunction with Schedule Entry Lock Command Class to
schedule access for users.

CC:0063.02.00.31.004

A node receiving a User Code Get Command MUST advertise what User Code is set in the User Code
Report Command.
2.2.116.4 Security Considerations
A node identifies users on the background of User Code entry alone without User Identifier, the
following security measures should be taken into consideration:

CC:0063.02.00.42.001

CC:0063.02.00.42.002

CC:0063.02.00.42.003

• Users SHOULD NOT be allowed to choose their own user codes. Users tend to choose codes such
as birthdates and therefore the risk of having duplicate codes is high. A user may learn about
another User Code when trying to set his own User Code and receiving a duplicate/rejection
message. In such a case, User Codes SHOULD be generated randomly by the administrating
company, if applicable.
• If a node is configured with a large number of User Codes: (e.g. 500), it is RECOMMENDED
to increase the number of digits in each and every user code, making is less likely to randomly
guess an assigned user code.
• It is RECOMMENDED to implement mechanisms preventing brute force attacks, such as exponential increasing waiting time between attempts or lock out after a number of failed attempts.

Description
Normal Mode:
