Version
1

0x01

Vacation Mode:
This mode is used to disable/switch off the User Code functionalities for normal
users. When the Vacation mode is active, the supporting node:
• MUST ignore all input of assigned User Code (i.e. with Status ID different than 0x00 Available)
• MUST react according to Table 2.527 when being input unknown codes
(i.e. with Status ID 0x00 Available).
• MUST accept the Admin Code, if supported

2

0x02

Privacy Mode:
This mode is used to completely disable/switch off the User Code functionalities.
When the Privacy mode is active, the supporting node:
• MUST ignore any keypad input
• MUST ignore the Admin Code, if supported
This mode can be used e.g. to disallow User Code keypad use completely or
to rely only on Entry Control Notifications, if supported.
Locked Out Mode:
This mode is used as a security measure to prevent brute force attacks. This
mode is normally activated by the supporting node itself. If the node activates
the Locked Out mode, it MUST issue a User Code Keypad Mode Report
Command to the Lifeline destination.
When the Locked Out mode is active, the supporting node:
• MUST ignore any keypad input
• MUST ignore the Admin Code, if supported.
A supporting node MUST return to the last active mode automatically after
a defined timeout if it activated this mode.
A controlling node may unlock the keypad again by issuing this command with
a different mode.

Messaging:
The database entry represented by this User Identifier is in use.
The value is used to relay notifications to a controlling application.
E.g. A user may enter a messaging code for notifying that maintenance started
or an application should activate the alarm system.
When a user enters a code with this status, the node:
• SHOULD indicate that the code is accepted

0x04

Passage Mode:
The database entry represented by this User Identifier is in use.
The value is used to let the Door Lock permanently grant access.
Passage Mode can be activated and deactivated using the Door Lock Operation
Set (Unsecured without timeout/Secured) or via Passage Mode User Code
input.
E.g. A receptionist comes in the morning and enters a Passage Mode User
Code to allow anybody to subsequently enter the premises without entering a
code until Passage Mode is deactivated again.
When a user enters a code with this status, the node:
• MUST indicate that the code is accepted
• MUST toggle the Door Lock operation state between secured and unsecured without timeout (and also disable any auto-relock functionality)
If the node supports the Door Lock Command Class, it:
• MUST send a Door Lock Operation Report and Door Lock Configuration
Report via the Lifeline Association Group to advertise the new Door Lock
state

   198→    def _resolve_pin_if_masked(self, value: str, code_slot: int) -> str | None:
   199→        """
   200→        Resolve a PIN value, looking up expected PIN if masked.
   201→
   202→        Some locks return masked values (all asterisks) instead of the actual PIN.
   203→        This method returns the value as-is if not masked, or looks up the expected
   204→        PIN from LCM entities if masked.
   205→
   206→        """
   207→        slot_in_use = self.code_slot_in_use(code_slot)
   208→
   209→        if value == "0" * len(value) and slot_in_use is False:
   210→            # Some locks return all zeros instead of a blank value when cleared - treat
   211→            # as unmasked cleared value
   212→            return ""
   213→
   214→        # If not masked, return as-is
   215→        if not value or not (value == "*" * len(value) and slot_in_use):
   216→            return value
   217→
   218→        # Masked - look up expected PIN from LCM entities
   219→        # Use ATTR_ACTIVE binary sensor (not CONF_ENABLED switch) to match what
   220→        # sync logic expects. ATTR_ACTIVE considers conditions, so we only resolve
   221→        # masked codes when sync expects a PIN on the lock.
   222→        states = self._get_slot_entity_states(code_slot)
   223→        if states is None:
   224→            return None
   225→
   226→        active_state, pin_value, pin_entity_id = states
   227→
   228→        if active_state == STATE_ON:

   231→                self.lock.entity_id,
   232→                code_slot,
   233→                pin_entity_id,
   234→            )
   235→            return pin_value
   236→
   237→        # Fall back to returning masked value if active state is not ON (e.g. slot not
   238→        # enabled) - we don't care what the value is, just that there is one so that
   239→        # the sync logic treats this slot as having a PIN set on the lock
   240→        return value

   274→            code_slot = int(args["propertyKey"])

   276→            # Slot 0 is not a valid user code slot (used for status/metadata)
   277→            if code_slot == 0:
   278→                return
   279→
   280→            # Handle userIdStatus updates - slot cleared is a fast path
   281→            if property_name == LOCK_USERCODE_STATUS_PROPERTY:
   282→                status = args.get("newValue")
   283→                if status == CodeSlotStatus.AVAILABLE:
   284→                    # Ignore AVAILABLE status if LCM expects a PIN on this slot.
   285→                    # Some locks send stale AVAILABLE events after a code was set,
   286→                    # which would cause infinite sync loops.
   287→                    if self._slot_expects_pin(code_slot):
   288→                        _LOGGER.debug(
   289→                            "Lock %s: ignoring userIdStatus=AVAILABLE for slot %s "
   290→                            "(LCM expects PIN on this slot)",
   291→                            self.lock.entity_id,
   292→                            code_slot,
   293→                        )
   294→                        return
   295→
   296→                    # Slot was cleared - update coordinator if needed
   297→                    if self.coordinator and self.coordinator.data.get(code_slot) != "":
   298→                        _LOGGER.debug(
   299→                            "Lock %s: slot %s userIdStatus=AVAILABLE, marking cleared",
   300→                            self.lock.entity_id,
   301→                            code_slot,
   302→                        )
   303→                        self.coordinator.push_update({code_slot: ""})
   304→                return
   305→
   306→            # Handle userCode updates
   307→            # newValue is the raw PIN string (or None/empty/"0000" if cleared)
   308→            new_value = args.get("newValue")
   309→            # Treat empty, None, or all-zeros as cleared
   310→            if not new_value or (
   311→                isinstance(new_value, str) and new_value.strip("0") == ""
   312→            ):
   313→                value = ""
   314→            else:
   315→                value = str(new_value)
   316→
   317→            # Resolve masked codes (all asterisks) to expected PIN
   318→            # This prevents infinite sync loops when locks return masked values
   319→            resolved = self._resolve_pin_if_masked(value, code_slot)
   320→            if resolved is None:
   321→                _LOGGER.debug(
   322→                    "Lock %s: skipping masked code update for slot %s "
   323→                    "(unable to resolve)",
   324→                    self.lock.entity_id,
   325→                    code_slot,
   326→                )
   327→                return
   328→
   329→            # Skip if value hasn't changed (Z-Wave JS sends duplicate events)
   330→            if self.coordinator and self.coordinator.data.get(code_slot) == resolved:
   331→                return
   332→
   333→            _LOGGER.debug(
   334→                "Lock %s received push update for slot %s: %s",
   335→                self.lock.entity_id,
   336→                code_slot,
   337→                "****" if resolved else "(cleared)",
   338→            )
   339→
   340→            # Push update to coordinator
   341→            if self.coordinator:
   342→                self.coordinator.push_update({code_slot: resolved})
   343→
   344→        try:
   345→            self._value_update_unsub = self.node.on("value updated", on_value_updated)
   346→        except ValueError as err:
   347→            _LOGGER.debug(
   348→                "Lock %s push subscription deferred: %s", self.lock.entity_id, err
   349→            )
   350→            self._schedule_push_retry("node not ready")
   351→
   352→    def _schedule_push_retry(self, reason: str) -> None:
   353→        """Schedule a retry for push subscription if one isn't pending."""
   354→        if self._push_retry_cancel:
   355→            return
   356→
   357→        _LOGGER.debug(
   358→            "Lock %s: scheduling push subscription retry in %ss (%s)",
   359→            self.lock.entity_id,
   360→            PUSH_SUBSCRIBE_RETRY_DELAY,
   361→            reason,
   362→        )
   363→        self._push_retry_cancel = async_call_later(
   364→            self.hass, PUSH_SUBSCRIBE_RETRY_DELAY, self._handle_push_retry
   365→        )
   366→
   367→    @callback
   368→    def _handle_push_retry(self, _now: Any) -> None:
   369→        """Retry push subscription after delay."""
   370→        if self._push_retry_cancel:
   371→            self._push_retry_cancel()
   372→            self._push_retry_cancel = None
   373→        self.subscribe_push_updates()
   374→
   375→    @callback
   376→    def unsubscribe_push_updates(self) -> None:
   377→        """Unsubscribe from value update events."""
   378→        if self._push_retry_cancel:
   379→            self._push_retry_cancel()
   380→            self._push_retry_cancel = None
   381→        if self._value_update_unsub:
   382→            self._value_update_unsub()
   383→            self._value_update_unsub = None
   384→
   385→    @callback
   386→    def _zwave_js_event_filter(self, event_data: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
   387→        """Filter out events."""
   388→        # Try to find the lock that we are getting an event for, skipping
   389→        # ones that don't match
   390→        assert self.node.client.driver
   391→        return (
   392→            event_data[ATTR_HOME_ID] == self.node.client.driver.controller.home_id
   393→            and event_data[ATTR_NODE_ID] == self.node.node_id
   394→            and event_data[ATTR_DEVICE_ID] == self.lock.device_id
   395→        )
   396→
   397→    @callback
   398→    def _handle_zwave_js_event(self, evt: Event) -> None:
   399→        """Handle Z-Wave JS event."""
   400→        if evt.data[ATTR_TYPE] != NotificationType.ACCESS_CONTROL:
   401→            _LOGGER.debug(
   402→                "Lock %s received non Access Control event: %s",
   403→                self.lock.entity_id,
   404→                evt.as_dict(),
   405→            )
   406→            return
   407→
   408→        params = evt.data.get(ATTR_PARAMETERS) or {}
   409→        code_slot = params.get("userId", 0)
   410→        self.async_fire_code_slot_event(
   411→            code_slot=code_slot,
   412→            to_locked=next(
   413→                (
   414→                    to_locked
   415→                    for to_locked, codes in ACCESS_CONTROL_NOTIFICATION_TO_LOCKED.items()
   416→                    if evt.data[ATTR_EVENT] in codes
   417→                ),
   418→                None,
   419→            ),
   420→            action_text=evt.data.get(ATTR_EVENT_LABEL),
   421→            source_data=evt,
   422→        )
   423→
   424→    @property
   425→    def domain(self) -> str:
   426→        """Return integration domain."""
   427→        return ZWAVE_JS_DOMAIN
   428→
   429→    async def async_setup(self, config_entry: ConfigEntry) -> None:
   430→        """Set up lock."""
   431→        await super().async_setup(config_entry)
   432→        self._listeners.append(
   433→            self.hass.bus.async_listen(
   434→                ZWAVE_JS_NOTIFICATION_EVENT,
   435→                self._handle_zwave_js_event,
   436→                self._zwave_js_event_filter,
   437→            )
   438→        )
   439→
   440→    async def async_unload(self, remove_permanently: bool) -> None:
   441→        """Unload lock."""
   442→        for listener in self._listeners:
   443→            listener()
   444→        self._listeners.clear()
   445→        await super().async_unload(remove_permanently)
   446→
   447→    async def async_is_connection_up(self) -> bool:
   448→        """Return whether connection to lock is up."""
   449→        ready, _reason = self._get_client_state()
   450→        return ready
   451→
   452→    async def async_hard_refresh_codes(self) -> dict[int, int | str]:
   453→        """
   454→        Perform hard refresh and return all codes.
   455→
   456→        Uses Z-Wave JS's refresh_cc_values which handles checksum optimization
   457→        internally - it will skip re-fetching codes if the checksum hasn't changed.
   458→        Returns codes in the same format as async_get_usercodes().
   459→        """
   460→        await self._async_refresh_usercode_cache()
   461→        return await self.async_get_usercodes()
   462→
   463→    async def async_set_usercode(
   464→        self, code_slot: int, usercode: int | str, name: str | None = None
   465→    ) -> bool:
   466→        """
   467→        Set a usercode on a code slot.
   468→
   469→        Returns True if the value was changed, False if already set to this value.
   470→        """
   471→        # Check if the code is already set to this value (avoid unnecessary network call)
   472→        usercode = str(usercode)
   473→        try:
   474→            if (current := get_usercode(self.node, code_slot)).get("in_use"):
   475→                current_code = str(current.get("usercode", ""))
   476→                # Resolve masked codes and compare
   477→                if usercode == self._resolve_pin_if_masked(current_code, code_slot):
   478→                    _LOGGER.debug(
   479→                        "Lock %s slot %s already has this PIN, skipping set",
   480→                        self.lock.entity_id,
   481→                        code_slot,
   482→                    )
   483→                    return False
   484→        except Exception:
   485→            # If we can't check the cache, proceed with the set
   486→            pass
   487→
   488→        service_data = {
   489→            ATTR_ENTITY_ID: self.lock.entity_id,
   490→            ATTR_CODE_SLOT: code_slot,
   491→            ATTR_USERCODE: usercode,
   492→        }
   493→        await self.async_call_service(
   494→            ZWAVE_JS_DOMAIN, SERVICE_SET_LOCK_USERCODE, service_data
   495→        )
   496→        # Optimistic update: Z-Wave command succeeded (lock acknowledged), but the
   497→        # value cache updates asynchronously via push notification. Update coordinator
   498→        # immediately to prevent sync loops from reading stale cache data.
   499→        if self.coordinator:
   500→            self.coordinator.push_update({code_slot: usercode})
   501→        return True
   502→
   503→    async def async_clear_usercode(self, code_slot: int) -> bool:
   504→        """
   505→        Clear a usercode on a code slot.
   506→
   507→        Returns True if the value was changed, False if already cleared.
   508→        """
   509→        # Check if the slot is already cleared (avoid unnecessary network call)
   510→        try:
   511→            current = get_usercode(self.node, code_slot)
   512→            if not current.get("in_use"):
   513→                _LOGGER.debug(
   514→                    "Lock %s slot %s already cleared, skipping clear",
   515→                    self.lock.entity_id,
   516→                    code_slot,
   517→                )
   518→                return False
   519→        except Exception:
   520→            # If we can't check the cache, proceed with the clear
   521→            pass
   522→
   523→        service_data = {
   524→            ATTR_ENTITY_ID: self.lock.entity_id,
   525→            ATTR_CODE_SLOT: code_slot,
   526→        }
   527→        await self.async_call_service(
   528→            ZWAVE_JS_DOMAIN, SERVICE_CLEAR_LOCK_USERCODE, service_data
   529→        )
   530→        # Optimistic update: Z-Wave command succeeded (lock acknowledged), but the
   531→        # value cache updates asynchronously via push notification. Update coordinator
   532→        # immediately to prevent sync loops from reading stale cache data.
   533→        if self.coordinator:
   534→            self.coordinator.push_update({code_slot: ""})
   535→        return True
   536→
   537→    def _get_usercodes_from_cache(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   538→        """Get usercodes from Z-Wave JS value DB cache."""
   539→        try:
   540→            return list(get_usercodes(self.node) or [])
   541→        except Exception as err:
   542→            raise LockDisconnected from err
   543→
   544→    async def _async_refresh_usercode_cache(self) -> None:
   545→        """Refresh usercode cache from the device."""
   546→        try:
   547→            await self.node.async_refresh_cc_values(CommandClass.USER_CODE)
   548→        except Exception as err:
   549→            raise LockDisconnected from err
   550→
   551→    async def async_get_usercodes(self) -> dict[int, int | str]:
   552→        """Get dictionary of code slots and usercodes."""
   553→        code_slots = {
   554→            int(code_slot)
   555→            for entry in self.hass.config_entries.async_entries(DOMAIN)
   556→            for code_slot in get_entry_data(entry, CONF_SLOTS, {})
   557→            if self.lock.entity_id in get_entry_data(entry, CONF_LOCKS, [])
   558→        }
   559→        data: dict[int, int | str] = {}
   560→
   561→        if not await self.async_is_connection_up():
   562→            raise LockDisconnected
   563→
   564→        slots = self._get_usercodes_from_cache()
   565→        slots_by_num = {int(slot["code_slot"]): slot for slot in slots}
   566→
   567→        # If any configured slot is missing or has unknown state, do one hard
   568→        # refresh to populate the cache. This is more efficient than fetching
   569→        # individual slots and uses Z-Wave JS's checksum optimization.
   570→        # Note: We call _async_refresh_usercode_cache directly here to avoid
   571→        # recursion since async_hard_refresh_codes calls async_get_usercodes.
   572→        if any(
   573→            slot_num not in slots_by_num or slots_by_num[slot_num].get("in_use") is None
   574→            for slot_num in code_slots
   575→        ):
   576→            _LOGGER.debug(
   577→                "Lock %s has missing/unknown slots, performing hard refresh",
   578→                self.lock.entity_id,
   579→            )
   580→            await self._async_refresh_usercode_cache()
   581→            slots = self._get_usercodes_from_cache()
   582→            slots_by_num = {int(slot["code_slot"]): slot for slot in slots}
   583→
   584→        for slot in slots:
   585→            code_slot = int(slot["code_slot"])
   586→            usercode: str = slot["usercode"] or ""
   587→            in_use: bool | None = slot["in_use"]
   588→
   589→            if not in_use:
   590→                data[code_slot] = ""
   591→            # Resolve PIN (handles masked codes), skip if unresolvable
   592→            elif resolved := self._resolve_pin_if_masked(usercode, code_slot):
   593→                data[code_slot] = resolved
   594→
   595→        slots_with_pin = [s for s, v in data.items() if v]
   596→        slots_not_enabled = [s for s, v in data.items() if not v]
   597→        _LOGGER.debug(
   598→            "Lock %s: %s slots with PIN %s, %s slots not enabled %s",
   599→            self.lock.entity_id,
   600→            len(slots_with_pin),
   601→            slots_with_pin,
   602→            len(slots_not_enabled),
   603→            slots_not_enabled,
   604→        )
   605→        return data
   606→

def get_code_slot_value(node: Node, code_slot: int, property_name: str) -> Value:
    """Get a code slot value."""
    value = node.values.get(
        get_value_id_str(
            node,
            CommandClass.USER_CODE,
            property_name,
            endpoint=0,
            property_key=code_slot,
        )
    )

    if not value:
        raise NotFoundError(f"{property_name} for code slot {code_slot} not found")

    return value


=== _get_code_slots ===
def _get_code_slots(node: Node, include_usercode: bool = False) -> list[CodeSlot]:
    """Get all code slots on the lock and optionally include usercode."""
    code_slot = 1
    slots: list[CodeSlot] = []

    # Loop until we can't find a code slot
    while True:
        try:
            value = get_code_slot_value(node, code_slot, LOCK_USERCODE_PROPERTY)
            status_value = get_code_slot_value(
                node, code_slot, LOCK_USERCODE_STATUS_PROPERTY
            )
        except NotFoundError:
            return slots

        code_slot = int(value.property_key)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        in_use = (
            None
            if status_value.value is None
            else status_value.value == CodeSlotStatus.ENABLED
        )

        # we know that code slots will always have a property key
        # that is an int, so we can ignore mypy
        slot = {
            ATTR_CODE_SLOT: code_slot,
            ATTR_NAME: value.metadata.label,
            ATTR_IN_USE: in_use,
        }
        if include_usercode:
            slot[ATTR_USERCODE] = value.value

        slots.append(cast(CodeSlot, slot))
        code_slot += 1

# User Code CC Interview: V1 vs V2 Analysis

## Version Detection
The interview determines version through the `api.version` property, checked via conditional logic: `if (api.version >= 2)` handles V2-specific operations, while V1 flows to the else branch.

## V1 Interview Process

**Relevant code section:**
```typescript
} else {
    // V1
    if (userCodeAction === "delete") {
        await api.clear();
    } else if (userCodeAction === "query") {
        for (let userId = 1; userId <= supportedUsers; userId++) {
            await api.get(userId);
        }
    }
}
```

V1 interviews query user codes individually in a sequential loop, either deleting all codes initially or retrieving each one.

## Values Created in V1 vs V2

**Both versions create `userIdStatus` values:** The `setUserCodeMetadata` function runs for each user ID during interview setup, establishing metadata for status and code properties regardless of version.

**V1 User Code Report persistence:**
```typescript
persistUserCode.call(
    this,
    ctx,
    this.userId,
    this.userIdStatus,
    this.userCode,
);
```

The report handler stores three values per user: userId, userIdStatus, and userCode in the database.

## Key Differences

| Aspect | V1 | V2 |
|--------|----|----|
| **Capabilities** | Not queried | `getCapabilities()` called first |
| **Query method** | Individual `Get` commands | Bulk `ExtendedUserCodeGet` with pagination |
| **Admin code support** | Not available | Queried if supported |
| **Checksum support** | Not available | Used to optimize queries |

Both versions create identical `userIdStatus` and `userCode` values in the database through the same persistence mechanism.
```

# User Code CC Implementation Analysis

## 1. SET_VALUE Handler

```typescript
protected override get [SET_VALUE](): SetValueImplementation {
	return async function(
		this: UserCodeCCAPI,
		{ property, propertyKey },
		value,
	) {
		let result: SupervisionResult | undefined;
		if (property === "keypadMode") {
			if (typeof value !== "number") {
				throwWrongValueType(
					this.ccId,
					property,
					"number",
					typeof value,
				);
			}
			result = await this.setKeypadMode(value);
		} else if (
			property === "adminCode"
			|| property === "masterCode"
		) {
			if (typeof value !== "string") {
				throwWrongValueType(
					this.ccId,
					property,
					"string",
					typeof value,
				);
			}
			result = await this.setAdminCode(value);
		} else if (property === "userIdStatus") {
			if (propertyKey == undefined) {
				throwMissingPropertyKey(this.ccId, property);
			} else if (typeof propertyKey !== "number") {
				throwUnsupportedPropertyKey(
					this.ccId,
					property,
					propertyKey,
				);
			}
			if (typeof value !== "number") {
				throwWrongValueType(
					this.ccId,
					property,
					"number",
					typeof value,
				);
			}

			if (value === UserIDStatus.Available) {
				result = await this.clear(propertyKey);
			} else {
				const userCode = this.getValueDB().getValue<string>(
					UserCodeCCValues.userCode(propertyKey).endpoint(
						this.endpoint.index,
					),
				);
				result = await this.set(propertyKey, value, userCode!);
			}
		} else if (property === "userCode") {
			if (propertyKey == undefined) {
				throwMissingPropertyKey(this.ccId, property);
			} else if (typeof propertyKey !== "number") {
				throwUnsupportedPropertyKey(
					this.ccId,
					property,
					propertyKey,
				);
			}
			if (typeof value !== "string" && !isUint8Array(value)) {
				throwWrongValueType(
					this.ccId,
					property,
					"string or Buffer",
					typeof value,
				);
			}

			let userIdStatus = this.getValueDB().getValue<UserIDStatus>(
				UserCodeCCValues.userIdStatus(propertyKey).endpoint(
					this.endpoint.index,
				),
			);
			if (
				userIdStatus === UserIDStatus.Available
				|| userIdStatus == undefined
			) {
				userIdStatus = UserIDStatus.Enabled;
			}
			result = await this.set(
				propertyKey,
				userIdStatus as any,
				value,
			);
		} else {
			throwUnsupportedProperty(this.ccId, property);
		}

		// Verify the change after a short delay, unless 
		// the command was supervised and successful
		if (this.isSinglecast() && !supervisedCommandSucceeded(result)) {
			this.schedulePoll({ property, propertyKey }, value, {
				transition: "fast",
			});
		}

		return result;
	};
}
```

## 2. V1 vs V2 Set Command Selection

The logic in the `set()` method:

```typescript
public async set(
	userId: number,
	userIdStatus: Exclude<
		UserIDStatus,
		UserIDStatus.Available | UserIDStatus.StatusNotAvailable
	>,
	userCode: string | BytesView,
): Promise<SupervisionResult | undefined> {
	// CL:0063.01.31.02.1: V2+ nodes must use Extended User Code Set
	if (this.version >= 2 || userId > 255) {
		return this.setMany([{ userId, userIdStatus, userCode }]);
	}

	this.assertSupportsCommand(UserCodeCommand, UserCodeCommand.Set);
	// ... V1 UserCodeCCSet logic
}
```

**Key finding:** The driver routes to Extended (V2) for version ≥2 OR userId >255; otherwise uses V1.

## 3. Optimistic Cache Updates

The driver does **NOT** optimistically update the cache. Instead:

```typescript
// Verify the change after a short delay, unless the command 
// was supervised and successful
if (this.isSinglecast() && !supervisedCommandSucceeded(result)) {
	this.schedulePoll({ property, propertyKey }, value, {
		transition: "fast",
	});
}
```

For both V1 and V2, if the command is not supervised-successful, it schedules a poll verification.

## 4. persistUserCode Function

```typescript
function persistUserCode(
	this: UserCodeCC,
	ctx: GetValueDB & GetSupportedCCVersion,
	userId: number,
	userIdStatus: UserIDStatus,
	userCode: string | Bytes,
) {
	const statusValue = UserCodeCCValues.userIdStatus(userId);
	const codeValue = UserCodeCCValues.userCode(userId);

	// Check if this code is supported
	if (userIdStatus === UserIDStatus.StatusNotAvailable) {
		// It is not, remove all values if any exist
		this.removeValue(ctx, statusValue);
		this.removeValue(ctx, codeValue);
		this.removeMetadata(ctx, statusValue);
		this.removeMetadata(ctx, codeValue);
	} else {
		// Always create metadata in case it does not exist
		setUserCodeMetadata.call(this, ctx, userId, userCode);
		this.setValue(ctx, statusValue, userIdStatus);
		this.setValue(ctx, codeValue, userCode);
	}

	return true;
}
```

## 5. Refresh Values Implementation (V1 vs V2)

```typescript
public async refreshValues(
	ctx: RefreshValuesContext,
	queryAllUserCodes: boolean = false,
): Promise<void> {
	const node = this.getNode(ctx)!;
	const endpoint = this.getEndpoint(ctx)!;
	const api = CCAPI.create(
		CommandClasses["User Code"],
		ctx,
		endpoint,
	).withOptions({
		priority: MessagePriority.NodeQuery,
	});

	const supportsAdminCode: boolean = UserCodeCC.supportsAdminCodeCached(
		ctx,
		endpoint,
	);
	const supportsUserCodeChecksum: boolean = this.getValue(
		ctx,
		UserCodeCCValues.supportsUserCodeChecksum,
	) ?? false;
	const supportedKeypadModes: readonly KeypadMode[] =
		this.getValue(ctx, UserCodeCCValues.supportedKeypadModes)
			?? [];
	const supportedUsers: number =
		this.getValue(ctx, UserCodeCCValues.supportedUsers) ?? 0;
	const supportsMultipleUserCodeReport = !!this.getValue(
		ctx,
		UserCodeCCValues.supportsMultipleUserCodeReport,
	);

	// ... context logic ...

	// V2+
	if (api.version >= 2) {
		if (supportsAdminCode) {
			ctx.logNode(node.id, {
				message: "querying admin code...",
				direction: "outbound",
			});
			await api.getAdminCode();
		}
		if (supportedKeypadModes.length > 1) {
			ctx.logNode(node.id, {
				message: "querying active keypad mode...",
				direction: "outbound",
			});
			await api.getKeypadMode();
		}
		const storedUserCodeChecksum: number =
			this.getValue(ctx, UserCodeCCValues.userCodeChecksum) ?? 0;

		let currentUserCodeChecksum: number | undefined = 0;
		if (supportsUserCodeChecksum) {
			ctx.logNode(node.id, {
				message: "retrieving current user code checksum...",
				direction: "outbound",
			});
			currentUserCodeChecksum = await api.getUserCodeChecksum();
		}

		if (userCodeAction === "delete") {
			ctx.logNode(node.id, {
				message: "Initial interview, clearing all user codes...",
				direction: "outbound",
			});
			await api.clear();
		} else if (userCodeAction === "query") {
			if (
				!supportsUserCodeChecksum
				|| currentUserCodeChecksum !== storedUserCodeChecksum
			) {
				ctx.logNode(node.id, {
					message:
						"checksum changed or is not supported, querying all user codes...",
					direction: "outbound",
				});

				if (supportsMultipleUserCodeReport) {
					// Query the user codes in bulk
					let nextUserId = 1;
					while (nextUserId > 0 && nextUserId <= supportedUsers) {
						const response = await api.get(nextUserId, true);
						if (response) {
							nextUserId = response.nextUserId;
						} else {
							ctx.logNode(node.id, {
								endpoint: this.endpointIndex,
								message:
									`Querying user code #${nextUserId} timed out, skipping remaining...`,
								level: "warn",
							});
							break;
						}
					}
				} else {
					// Query one user code at a time
					for (
						let userId = 1;
						userId <= supportedUsers;
						userId++
					) {
						await api.get(userId);
					}
				}
			}
		}
	} else {
		// V1
		if (userCodeAction === "delete") {
			ctx.logNode(node.id, {
				message: "Initial interview, clearing all user codes...",
				direction: "outbound",
			});
			await api.clear();
		} else if (userCodeAction === "query") {
			ctx.logNode(node.id, {
				message: "querying all user codes...",
				direction: "outbound",
			});
			for (let userId = 1; userId <= supportedUsers; userId++) {
				await api.get(userId);
			}
		}
	}
}
```

**Key difference:** V2 uses checksum optimization and bulk retrieval; V1 always queries codes one-at-a-time.
```

Here's the comprehensive analysis of V1 vs V2 differences and their impact on our code:

---

## User Code CC V1 vs V2: Impact on LCM

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The Z-Wave JS driver treats V1 and V2 identically in terms of value structure (`userCode` + `userIdStatus` values per slot). The critical differences are in **cache management** and **verification behavior** after set/clear operations.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

### Key Finding: The Z-Wave JS Driver Does NOT Optimistically Update Cache

From the driver source:
```typescript
// Verify the change after a short delay, unless 
// the command was supervised and successful
if (this.isSinglecast() && !supervisedCommandSucceeded(result)) {
    this.schedulePoll({ property, propertyKey }, value, {
        transition: "fast",
    });
}
```

| Behavior | V2 (with Supervision CC) | V1 (no Supervision CC) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| After set/clear | If supervised-success → trusted, no poll | ALWAYS schedules verification poll |
| Hard refresh | Checksum optimization → skip if unchanged | Queries every slot one-by-one |
| Unsolicited reports | Required via Lifeline for local changes | Not required by spec |
| Masked codes | Should return actual codes | Known to return `"******"` |

### The Sync Loop Root Cause for V1

The critical bug is in `async_internal_set_usercode` (in `_base.py`):

```python
async def async_internal_set_usercode(self, code_slot, usercode, name=None):
    changed = await self._execute_rate_limited("set", self.async_set_usercode, ...)
    # ↑ Inside async_set_usercode:
    #   1. Sends Z-Wave command
    #   2. push_update({slot: "1234"})  ← OPTIMISTIC (correct)
    
    if changed and self.coordinator:
        await self.coordinator.async_request_refresh()
        # ↑ This calls async_get_usercodes() → reads Z-Wave JS cache
        # V2: Cache already updated (Supervision + fast report) → OK
        # V1: Cache is STALE (verification poll hasn't completed) → OVERWRITES optimistic push!
```

**For V1, the sequence is:**
1. Set code "1234" → Z-Wave command sent → lock ACKs
2. `push_update({3: "1234"})` → coordinator has correct data
3. `async_request_refresh()` reads Z-Wave JS cache → cache still has old value (AVAILABLE)
4. Coordinator data becomes `{3: ""}` → **overwrites the optimistic push**
5. Sync sees mismatch → retries set → infinite loop

### What Needs to Change

**1. Detect CC version** — so we can branch behavior:
```python
@property
def _usercode_cc_version(self) -> int:
    return next(
        (cc.version for cc in self.node.command_classes
         if cc.id == CommandClass.USER_CODE), 1
    )
```

**2. V1 nodes should not trigger coordinator refresh after set/clear** — the optimistic `push_update` is correct; the cache read overwrites it. Either:
- Skip `async_request_refresh()` when `push_update` was called (all push providers)
- Or have `async_set_usercode`/`async_clear_usercode` return a signal that the coordinator was already updated

**3. V1 hard refresh generates too many events** — every slot is queried individually. Consider:
- Longer `hard_refresh_interval` for V1
- Or suppressing push handler events during hard refresh

**4. V1 may need polling** — since V1 doesn't require unsolicited Lifeline reports, external changes (code entered at keypad) may not trigger `value updated` events. V1 may need `supports_push = False` or hybrid mode (push + periodic poll).

### Detection for CC Version

The version is available via:
```python
node.command_classes  # list[CommandClassInfo] with .id and .version
```

Would you like me to proceed with implementing these changes?

> DEVELOPER

yes. Remove request refresh entirely, defeats the purpose of optimistic updates alongside a polling period. Let's suppress push handler events during a hard refresh as long as its blocking and we can comfortably do so. We should poll for V1.

> AGENT

Great question. Let me think through the V1 vs V2 polling economics:

**V2 current strategy:**
- Push handles real-time updates (value updated events)
- Normal polling: DISABLED (push)
- Hard refresh: periodic, uses checksum → usually no Z-Wave traffic

**V1 reality:**
- `async_get_usercodes()` reads Z-Wave JS **cache** (no Z-Wave traffic)
- But V1 cache is only updated by: initial interview, our own verification polls, or hard refresh
- Normal cache poll DOES pick up our own set/clear changes (verification poll updates cache)
- Normal cache poll does NOT detect external changes (keypad entry, another controller)
- Hard refresh queries **every slot individually** → expensive (N Z-Wave commands for N slots)

So for V1:
- **Normal poll** (read cache): cheap, catches our own changes post-verification
- **Hard refresh** (re-query device): expensive, only way to detect external changes

> AGENT

## Design: User Code CC V1 Support

### 1. Remove `async_request_refresh()` after set/clear (base class)

Remove the two `async_request_refresh()` calls in `async_internal_set_usercode` and `async_internal_clear_usercode`. These defeat optimistic `push_update` by reading stale cache. The coordinator already gets updated data via:
- Optimistic `push_update()` (for push providers)
- Next poll cycle (for poll providers)

**Files:** `_base.py` lines 517-519, 567-569

Does this section look right?

### 2. Detect CC version and branch behavior in ZWaveJSLock

Add a `_usercode_cc_version` property:
```python
@cached_property
def _usercode_cc_version(self) -> int:
    return next(
        (cc.version for cc in self.node.command_classes
         if cc.id == CommandClass.USER_CODE), 1
    )
```

Then branch key properties:
- **V1:** `supports_push = False`, `usercode_scan_interval = ~2 min`, `hard_refresh_interval = ~30 min`, `connection_check_interval = 30s`
- **V2:** `supports_push = True`, `hard_refresh_interval = 1 hour` (current), `connection_check_interval = None` (current)

V1 still subscribes to notification events (lock/unlock with code slot) since those use the Notification CC, not User Code CC.

### 3. Suppress push handler events during hard refresh

Add a `_hard_refresh_in_progress` flag to ZWaveJSLock. Set it before `async_refresh_cc_values`, clear after. In `on_value_updated`, skip processing when the flag is set. This prevents the flood of stale value-updated events from V1's one-by-one re-query during drift detection.

This also benefits V2 — during hard refresh, the cache is being rebuilt and intermediate events are noise.

**Files:** `zwave_js.py` — `subscribe_push_updates` handler + `async_hard_refresh_codes`

### 4. TODO: configurable hard refresh interval

Add a TODO for making hard_refresh_interval a user-configurable option.

---

Does this design look right, or any adjustments needed?

> DEVELOPER

yes. We should also note that we may need to split hard refresh further between slots managed and unmanaged. Maybe managed slots get hard refreshed every 30 minutes but the rest once a day

> AGENT

Good point — managed slots need frequent verification (they're the ones we're syncing) while unmanaged slots just need occasional drift awareness. I'll add that as a TODO alongside the configurable interval.

Let me write the design doc and move to implementation planning.

  "content": "# User Code CC V1 Support\n\n## Problem\n\nThe Z-Wave JS provider is optimized for User Code Command Class V2. Locks using\nV1 experience sync loops because:\n\n1. V1 nodes lack Supervision CC, so the Z-Wave JS driver always schedules\n   verification polls after set/clear (no optimistic cache update).\n2. `async_internal_set_usercode` calls `coordinator.async_request_refresh()`\n   after the optimistic `push_update()`, reading stale cache and overwriting the\n   correct optimistic data.\n3. V1 hard refresh queries every slot individually (no checksum optimization),\n   flooding the push handler with stale value-updated events.\n4. V1 nodes are not required to send unsolicited User Code Reports via Lifeline,\n   making push-based updates unreliable for detecting external changes.\n\n## Changes\n\n### 1. Remove `async_request_refresh()` after set/clear\n\n**File:** `providers/_base.py`\n\nRemove the `coordinator.async_request_refresh()` calls in\n`async_internal_set_usercode` and `async_internal_clear_usercode`. These defeat\noptimistic `push_update()` by reading potentially stale cache. The coordinator\nalready receives correct data via:\n\n- Optimistic `push_update()` (push providers)\n- Next poll cycle (poll providers)\n\nThis change benefits all providers, not just V1.\n\n### 2. Detect CC version and branch behavior\n\n**File:** `providers/zwave_js.py`\n\nAdd a `_usercode_cc_version` cached property that reads the User Code CC version\nfrom the node's command class list.\n\nBranch key properties based on version:\n\n| Property | V1 | V2 |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `supports_push` | `False` | `True` |\n| `usercode_scan_interval` | 2 minutes | N/A (push) |\n| `hard_refresh_interval` | 30 minutes | 1 hour |\n| `connection_check_interval` | 30 seconds | `None` (config entry state) |\n\nV1 nodes still subscribe to Notification CC events (lock/unlock with code slot)\nsince those use a different command class than User Code CC.\n\n### 3. Suppress push handler events during hard refresh\n\n**File:** `providers/zwave_js.py`\n\nAdd a `_hard_refresh_in_progress` flag. Set it before\n`async_refresh_cc_values`, clear after. In `on_value_updated`, skip processing\nwhen the flag is set. This prevents stale value-updated events from V1's\none-by-one slot re-query during drift detection.\n\nThis also benefits V2 since intermediate events during cache rebuild are noise.\n\n### 4. TODOs for future work\n\n- Make `hard_refresh_interval` a user-configurable option.\n- Split hard refresh between managed and unmanaged slots. Managed slots (those\n  with LCM config) get refreshed at the normal interval (e.g., 30 min).\n  Unmanaged slots only need occasional drift awareness (e.g., once a day).\n"

    52→class BaseLock:
    53→    """
    54→    Base class for lock provider implementations.
    55→
    56→    Data Fetching Modes
    57→    -------------------
    58→    The coordinator supports three update modes. All modes include an initial poll.
    59→
    60→    1. Poll for updates (default):
    61→       - Periodic calls to get_usercodes() at usercode_scan_interval
    62→       - Used when supports_push = False
    63→       - Suitable for integrations without real-time events
    64→
    65→    2. Push for updates:
    66→       - Real-time value updates via subscribe_push_updates()
    67→       - Enabled when supports_push = True
    68→       - Disables periodic polling (poll for updates)
    69→       - Updates pushed via coordinator.push_update({slot: value})
    70→
    71→    3. Poll for drift:
    72→       - Periodic hard_refresh_codes() at hard_refresh_interval
    73→       - Detects out-of-band changes (e.g., codes changed at keypad)
    74→       - Runs regardless of push/poll mode
    75→       - Set hard_refresh_interval = None to disable
    76→
    77→    4. Poll connection state:
    78→       - Periodic async_internal_is_connection_up() at connection_check_interval
    79→       - Helps detect reconnects for integrations without config entry state signals
    80→       - Set connection_check_interval = None to disable
    81→
    82→    Configuration Examples
    83→    ----------------------
    84→    Poll-only (default):
    85→        supports_push = False
    86→        usercode_scan_interval = timedelta(minutes=1)
    87→        hard_refresh_interval = None
    88→        connection_check_interval = timedelta(seconds=30)
    89→
    90→    Push with drift detection (recommended for Z-Wave JS):
    91→        supports_push = True
    92→        hard_refresh_interval = timedelta(hours=1)
    93→        connection_check_interval = None
    94→        # Override subscribe_push_updates() to handle value events
    95→
    96→    Poll with drift detection:
    97→        supports_push = False
    98→        usercode_scan_interval = timedelta(minutes=1)
    99→        hard_refresh_interval = timedelta(hours=1)
   100→        connection_check_interval = timedelta(seconds=30)

   130→        self, func: Callable[..., Any], *args: Any, **kwargs: Any
   131→    ) -> Any:
   132→        """Run a sync method in the executor."""
   133→        if kwargs:
   134→            return await self.hass.async_add_executor_job(
   135→                functools.partial(func, *args, **kwargs)

   137→        return await self.hass.async_add_executor_job(func, *args)

   139→    async def _execute_rate_limited(
   140→        self,
   141→        operation_type: Literal["get", "set", "clear", "refresh"],
   142→        func: Callable[..., Awaitable[Any]],
   143→        *args: Any,
   144→        **kwargs: Any,
   145→    ) -> Any:
   146→        """Execute operation with connection check, serialization, and delay."""
   147→        if not await self.async_internal_is_connection_up():
   148→            raise LockDisconnected(
   149→                f"Cannot {_OPERATION_MESSAGES[operation_type]} {self.lock.entity_id} - lock not connected"
   150→            )
   151→
   152→        async with self._aio_lock:
   153→            elapsed = time.monotonic() - self._last_operation_time
   154→            if elapsed < self._min_operation_delay:
   155→                delay = self._min_operation_delay - elapsed
   156→                LOGGER.debug(
   157→                    "Rate limiting %s operation on %s, waiting %.1f seconds",
   158→                    operation_type,
   159→                    self.lock.entity_id,
   160→                    delay,
   161→                )
   162→                await asyncio.sleep(delay)
   163→
   164→            LOGGER.debug(
   165→                "Executing %s operation on %s",
   166→                operation_type,
   167→                self.lock.entity_id,
   168→            )
   169→
   170→            result = await func(*args, **kwargs)
   171→            self._last_operation_time = time.monotonic()
   172→            return result

   299→        await self.hass.async_add_executor_job(self.setup)

   369→    def _setup_config_entry_state_listener(self) -> None:
   370→        """Listen for provider config entry state changes to resubscribe."""
   371→        lock_entry = self.lock_config_entry
   372→        if not lock_entry or self._config_entry_state_unsub:
   373→            return
   374→
   375→        self._last_entry_state = lock_entry.state
   376→
   377→        @callback
   378→        def _handle_state_change() -> None:
   379→            to_state = lock_entry.state
   380→            if to_state == self._last_entry_state:
   381→                return
   382→
   383→            if to_state == ConfigEntryState.LOADED:
   384→                if self.coordinator:
   385→                    self.hass.async_create_task(
   386→                        self.coordinator.async_request_refresh(),
   387→                        f"Refresh coordinator for {self.lock.entity_id} after reload",
   388→                    )
   389→                if self.supports_push:
   390→                    self.subscribe_push_updates()
   391→            elif (
   392→                self.supports_push and self._last_entry_state == ConfigEntryState.LOADED
   393→            ):
   394→                self.unsubscribe_push_updates()
   395→
   396→            self._last_entry_state = to_state

   399→            _handle_state_change
   400→        )

   421→                elif self._last_connection_up is True and not is_up:
   422→                    self.unsubscribe_push_updates()

   463→    def set_usercode(
   464→        self, code_slot: int, usercode: int | str, name: str | None = None
   465→    ) -> bool:
   466→        """
   467→        Set a usercode on a code slot.
   468→
   469→        Returns True if the value was changed, False if already set to this value.
   470→        If the provider cannot determine whether a change occurred, return True
   471→        to ensure the coordinator refreshes and verifies the state.
   472→
   473→        Optimistic Updates
   474→        ------------------
   475→        For providers where the underlying integration's value cache updates
   476→        asynchronously (e.g., Z-Wave JS push notifications), the base class
   477→        coordinator refresh may read stale data, causing sync loops.
   478→
   479→        In these cases, call ``self.coordinator.push_update({code_slot: usercode})``
   480→        after a successful set operation to update coordinator data immediately.
   481→        This prevents the sync sensor from seeing a mismatch and retrying.
   482→
   483→        Providers with synchronous caches (like Virtual) don't need this as
   484→        get_usercodes() returns the updated value immediately.

   625→    @final
   626→    def call_service(
   627→        self,
   628→        domain: str,
   629→        service: str,
   630→        service_data: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   631→        blocking: bool = True,
   632→    ):
   633→        """Call a hass service and log a failure on an error."""
   634→        try:
   635→            self.hass.services.call(
   636→                domain, service, service_data=service_data, blocking=blocking
   637→            )
   638→        except Exception as err:
   639→            LOGGER.error(
   640→                "Error calling %s.%s service call: %s", domain, service, str(err)
   641→            )
   642→
   643→    @final
   644→    async def async_call_service(
   645→        self,
   646→        domain: str,
   647→        service: str,
   648→        service_data: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   649→        blocking: bool = True,
   650→    ):
   651→        """Call a hass service and re-raise failures as LockDisconnected."""
   652→        try:
   653→            await self.hass.services.async_call(
   654→                domain, service, service_data=service_data, blocking=blocking
   655→            )
   656→        except Exception as err:
   657→            LOGGER.error(
   658→                "Error calling %s.%s service call: %s", domain, service, str(err)
   659→            )
   660→            raise LockDisconnected(
   661→                f"Service call {domain}.{service} failed: {err}"
   662→            ) from err
   663→
   664→    @final
   665→    @callback
   666→    def async_fire_code_slot_event(
   667→        self,
   668→        code_slot: int | None = None,
   669→        to_locked: bool | None = None,
   670→        action_text: str | None = None,
   671→        source_data: Event | State | dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   672→    ) -> None:
   673→        """
   674→        Fire a code slot event.
   675→
   676→        Sub-classes should call this whenever a code slot is used. source_data can
   677→        include any data that is JSON serializable if the source is not a Home
   678→        Assistant event or state.
   679→        """
   680→        name_state: State | None = None
   681→        lock_entity_id = self.lock.entity_id
   682→        lock_device_id = self.lock.device_id
   683→        config_entry_id: str | None = None
   684→
   685→        try:
   686→            config_entry = next(
   687→                config_entry
   688→                for config_entry in self.hass.config_entries.async_entries(DOMAIN)
   689→                if (
   690→                    self.lock.entity_id in get_entry_data(config_entry, CONF_LOCKS, [])
   691→                    and code_slot is not None
   692→                    and int(code_slot)
   693→                    in (
   694→                        int(slot)
   695→                        for slot in get_entry_data(config_entry, CONF_SLOTS, {})
   696→                    )
   697→                    and (
   698→                        name_entity_id := self.ent_reg.async_get_entity_id(
   699→                            TEXT_DOMAIN,
   700→                            DOMAIN,
   701→                            f"{config_entry.entry_id}|{code_slot}|{CONF_NAME}",
   702→                        )
   703→                    )
   704→                )
   705→            )
   706→        except StopIteration:
   707→            pass
   708→        else:
   709→            config_entry_id = config_entry.entry_id
   710→            name_state = self.hass.states.get(name_entity_id)
   711→
   712→        from_state: str | None = None
   713→        to_state: str | None = None
   714→        if to_locked:
   715→            from_state = LockState.UNLOCKED
   716→            to_state = LockState.LOCKED
   717→        elif to_locked is False:
   718→            from_state = LockState.LOCKED
   719→            to_state = LockState.UNLOCKED
   720→
   721→        notification_source: Literal["event", "state"] | None = None
   722→        extra_data: dict[str, Any] | None = None
   723→        if isinstance(source_data, Event):
   724→            notification_source = "event"
   725→            extra_data = {
   726→                "event_type": source_data.event_type,
   727→                "data": source_data.data,
   728→                "time_fired": source_data.time_fired.isoformat(),
   729→            }
   730→        elif isinstance(source_data, State):
   731→            notification_source = "state"
   732→            last_changed_isoformat = source_data.last_changed.isoformat()
   733→            if source_data.last_changed == source_data.last_updated:
   734→                last_updated_isoformat = last_changed_isoformat
   735→            else:
   736→                last_updated_isoformat = source_data.last_updated.isoformat()
   737→            extra_data = {
   738→                "entity_id": source_data.entity_id,
   739→                "state": source_data.state,
   740→                "attributes": source_data.attributes,
   741→                "last_changed": last_changed_isoformat,
   742→                "last_updated": last_updated_isoformat,
   743→            }
   744→        elif isinstance(source_data, dict):
   745→            extra_data = source_data
   746→
   747→        event_data = {
   748→            ATTR_NOTIFICATION_SOURCE: notification_source,
   749→            ATTR_ENTITY_ID: lock_entity_id,
   750→            ATTR_DEVICE_ID: lock_device_id,
   751→            ATTR_LCM_CONFIG_ENTRY_ID: config_entry_id,
   752→            ATTR_STATE: (
   753→                state.state if (state := self.hass.states.get(lock_entity_id)) else ""
   754→            ),
   755→            ATTR_ACTION_TEXT: action_text,
   756→            ATTR_CODE_SLOT: code_slot or 0,
   757→            ATTR_CODE_SLOT_NAME: name_state.state if name_state else "",
   758→            ATTR_FROM: from_state,
   759→            ATTR_TO: to_state,
   760→            ATTR_EXTRA_DATA: extra_data,
   761→        }
   762→
   763→        if self.lock_config_entry:
   764→            event_data[ATTR_LOCK_CONFIG_ENTRY_ID] = self.lock_config_entry.entry_id
   765→
   766→        self.hass.bus.async_fire(EVENT_LOCK_STATE_CHANGED, event_data=event_data)
   767→

   198→    def _resolve_pin_if_masked(self, value: str, code_slot: int) -> str | None:
   199→        """
   200→        Resolve a PIN value, looking up expected PIN if masked.
   201→
   202→        Some locks return masked values (all asterisks) instead of the actual PIN.
   203→        This method returns the value as-is if not masked, or looks up the expected
   204→        PIN from LCM entities if masked.
   205→
   206→        """
   207→        slot_in_use = self.code_slot_in_use(code_slot)
   208→
   209→        if value == "0" * len(value) and slot_in_use is False:
   210→            # Some locks return all zeros instead of a blank value when cleared - treat
   211→            # as unmasked cleared value
   212→            return ""
   213→
   214→        # If not masked, return as-is
   215→        if not value or not (value == "*" * len(value) and slot_in_use):
   216→            return value
   217→
   218→        # Masked - look up expected PIN from LCM entities
   219→        # Use ATTR_ACTIVE binary sensor (not CONF_ENABLED switch) to match what
   220→        # sync logic expects. ATTR_ACTIVE considers conditions, so we only resolve
   221→        # masked codes when sync expects a PIN on the lock.
   222→        states = self._get_slot_entity_states(code_slot)
   223→        if states is None:
   224→            return None
   225→
   226→        active_state, pin_value, pin_entity_id = states
   227→
   228→        if active_state == STATE_ON:

   238→        # enabled) - we don't care what the value is, just that there is one so that
   239→        # the sync logic treats this slot as having a PIN set on the lock
   240→        return value

   259→        @callback
   260→        def on_value_updated(event: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   261→            """Handle value update events from Z-Wave JS."""
   262→            args: dict[str, Any] = event["args"]
   263→            # Filter for User Code CC - handle both userCode and userIdStatus
   264→            if args.get("commandClass") != CommandClass.USER_CODE:
   265→                return
   266→
   267→            property_name = args.get("property")
   268→            if property_name not in (
   269→                LOCK_USERCODE_PROPERTY,
   270→                LOCK_USERCODE_STATUS_PROPERTY,
   271→            ):
   272→                return
   273→
   274→            code_slot = int(args["propertyKey"])
   275→
   276→            # Slot 0 is not a valid user code slot (used for status/metadata)
   277→            if code_slot == 0:
   278→                return
   279→
   280→            # Handle userIdStatus updates - slot cleared is a fast path
   281→            if property_name == LOCK_USERCODE_STATUS_PROPERTY:
   282→                status = args.get("newValue")
   283→                if status == CodeSlotStatus.AVAILABLE:
   284→                    # Ignore AVAILABLE status if LCM expects a PIN on this slot.
   285→                    # Some locks send stale AVAILABLE events after a code was set,
   286→                    # which would cause infinite sync loops.
   287→                    if self._slot_expects_pin(code_slot):
   288→                        _LOGGER.debug(
   289→                            "Lock %s: ignoring userIdStatus=AVAILABLE for slot %s "
   290→                            "(LCM expects PIN on this slot)",
   291→                            self.lock.entity_id,
   292→                            code_slot,
   293→                        )
   294→                        return
   295→
   296→                    # Slot was cleared - update coordinator if needed
   297→                    if self.coordinator and self.coordinator.data.get(code_slot) != "":
   298→                        _LOGGER.debug(
   299→                            "Lock %s: slot %s userIdStatus=AVAILABLE, marking cleared",
   300→                            self.lock.entity_id,
   301→                            code_slot,
   302→                        )
   303→                        self.coordinator.push_update({code_slot: ""})
   304→                return
   305→
   306→            # Handle userCode updates
   307→            # newValue is the raw PIN string (or None/empty/"0000" if cleared)
   308→            new_value = args.get("newValue")
   309→            # Treat empty, None, or all-zeros as cleared
   310→            if not new_value or (
   311→                isinstance(new_value, str) and new_value.strip("0") == ""
   312→            ):
   313→                value = ""
   314→            else:
   315→                value = str(new_value)
   316→
   317→            # Resolve masked codes (all asterisks) to expected PIN
   318→            # This prevents infinite sync loops when locks return masked values
   319→            resolved = self._resolve_pin_if_masked(value, code_slot)
   320→            if resolved is None:
   321→                _LOGGER.debug(
   322→                    "Lock %s: skipping masked code update for slot %s "
   323→                    "(unable to resolve)",
   324→                    self.lock.entity_id,
   325→                    code_slot,
   326→                )
   327→                return
   328→
   329→            # Skip if value hasn't changed (Z-Wave JS sends duplicate events)
   330→            if self.coordinator and self.coordinator.data.get(code_slot) == resolved:
   331→                return
   332→
   333→            _LOGGER.debug(
   334→                "Lock %s received push update for slot %s: %s",
   335→                self.lock.entity_id,
   336→                code_slot,
   337→                "****" if resolved else "(cleared)",
   338→            )
   339→
   340→            # Push update to coordinator
   341→            if self.coordinator:
   342→                self.coordinator.push_update({code_slot: resolved})
   343→
   344→        try:
   345→            self._value_update_unsub = self.node.on("value updated", on_value_updated)
   346→        except ValueError as err:
   347→            _LOGGER.debug(
   348→                "Lock %s push subscription deferred: %s", self.lock.entity_id, err
   349→            )
   350→            self._schedule_push_retry("node not ready")
   351→
   352→    def _schedule_push_retry(self, reason: str) -> None:
   353→        """Schedule a retry for push subscription if one isn't pending."""
   354→        if self._push_retry_cancel:
   355→            return
   356→
   357→        _LOGGER.debug(
   358→            "Lock %s: scheduling push subscription retry in %ss (%s)",
   359→            self.lock.entity_id,
   360→            PUSH_SUBSCRIBE_RETRY_DELAY,
   361→            reason,
   362→        )
   363→        self._push_retry_cancel = async_call_later(
   364→            self.hass, PUSH_SUBSCRIBE_RETRY_DELAY, self._handle_push_retry
   365→        )
   366→
   367→    @callback
   368→    def _handle_push_retry(self, _now: Any) -> None:
   369→        """Retry push subscription after delay."""
   370→        if self._push_retry_cancel:
   371→            self._push_retry_cancel()
   372→            self._push_retry_cancel = None
   373→        self.subscribe_push_updates()
   374→
   375→    @callback
   376→    def unsubscribe_push_updates(self) -> None:
   377→        """Unsubscribe from value update events."""
   378→        if self._push_retry_cancel:
   379→            self._push_retry_cancel()
   380→            self._push_retry_cancel = None
   381→        if self._value_update_unsub:
   382→            self._value_update_unsub()
   383→            self._value_update_unsub = None
   384→
   385→    @callback
   386→    def _zwave_js_event_filter(self, event_data: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
   387→        """Filter out events."""
   388→        # Try to find the lock that we are getting an event for, skipping
   389→        # ones that don't match
   390→        assert self.node.client.driver
   391→        return (
   392→            event_data[ATTR_HOME_ID] == self.node.client.driver.controller.home_id
   393→            and event_data[ATTR_NODE_ID] == self.node.node_id
   394→            and event_data[ATTR_DEVICE_ID] == self.lock.device_id
   395→        )
   396→
   397→    @callback
   398→    def _handle_zwave_js_event(self, evt: Event) -> None:
   399→        """Handle Z-Wave JS event."""
   400→        if evt.data[ATTR_TYPE] != NotificationType.ACCESS_CONTROL:
   401→            _LOGGER.debug(
   402→                "Lock %s received non Access Control event: %s",
   403→                self.lock.entity_id,
   404→                evt.as_dict(),
   405→            )
   406→            return
   407→
   408→        params = evt.data.get(ATTR_PARAMETERS) or {}
   409→        code_slot = params.get("userId", 0)
   410→        self.async_fire_code_slot_event(
   411→            code_slot=code_slot,
   412→            to_locked=next(
   413→                (
   414→                    to_locked
   415→                    for to_locked, codes in ACCESS_CONTROL_NOTIFICATION_TO_LOCKED.items()
   416→                    if evt.data[ATTR_EVENT] in codes
   417→                ),
   418→                None,
   419→            ),
   420→            action_text=evt.data.get(ATTR_EVENT_LABEL),
   421→            source_data=evt,
   422→        )
   423→
   424→    @property
   425→    def domain(self) -> str:
   426→        """Return integration domain."""
   427→        return ZWAVE_JS_DOMAIN
   428→
   429→    async def async_setup(self, config_entry: ConfigEntry) -> None:
   430→        """Set up lock."""
   431→        await super().async_setup(config_entry)
   432→        self._listeners.append(
   433→            self.hass.bus.async_listen(
   434→                ZWAVE_JS_NOTIFICATION_EVENT,
   435→                self._handle_zwave_js_event,
   436→                self._zwave_js_event_filter,
   437→            )
   438→        )
   439→
   440→    async def async_unload(self, remove_permanently: bool) -> None:
   441→        """Unload lock."""
   442→        for listener in self._listeners:
   443→            listener()
   444→        self._listeners.clear()
   445→        await super().async_unload(remove_permanently)
   446→
   447→    async def async_is_connection_up(self) -> bool:
   448→        """Return whether connection to lock is up."""
   449→        ready, _reason = self._get_client_state()
   450→        return ready
   451→
   452→    async def async_hard_refresh_codes(self) -> dict[int, int | str]:
   453→        """
   454→        Perform hard refresh and return all codes.
   455→
   456→        Uses Z-Wave JS's refresh_cc_values which handles checksum optimization
   457→        internally - it will skip re-fetching codes if the checksum hasn't changed.
   458→        Returns codes in the same format as async_get_usercodes().
   459→        """
   460→        await self._async_refresh_usercode_cache()
   461→        return await self.async_get_usercodes()
   462→
   463→    async def async_set_usercode(
   464→        self, code_slot: int, usercode: int | str, name: str | None = None
   465→    ) -> bool:
   466→        """
   467→        Set a usercode on a code slot.
   468→
   469→        Returns True if the value was changed, False if already set to this value.
   470→        """
   471→        # Check if the code is already set to this value (avoid unnecessary network call)
   472→        usercode = str(usercode)
   473→        try:
   474→            if (current := get_usercode(self.node, code_slot)).get("in_use"):
   475→                current_code = str(current.get("usercode", ""))
   476→                # Resolve masked codes and compare
   477→                if usercode == self._resolve_pin_if_masked(current_code, code_slot):
   478→                    _LOGGER.debug(
   479→                        "Lock %s slot %s already has this PIN, skipping set",
   480→                        self.lock.entity_id,
   481→                        code_slot,
   482→                    )
   483→                    return False
   484→        except Exception:
   485→            # If we can't check the cache, proceed with the set
   486→            pass
   487→
   488→        service_data = {
   489→            ATTR_ENTITY_ID: self.lock.entity_id,
   490→            ATTR_CODE_SLOT: code_slot,
   491→            ATTR_USERCODE: usercode,
   492→        }
   493→        await self.async_call_service(
   494→            ZWAVE_JS_DOMAIN, SERVICE_SET_LOCK_USERCODE, service_data
   495→        )
   496→        # Optimistic update: Z-Wave command succeeded (lock acknowledged), but the
   497→        # value cache updates asynchronously via push notification. Update coordinator
   498→        # immediately to prevent sync loops from reading stale cache data.
   499→        if self.coordinator:
   500→            self.coordinator.push_update({code_slot: usercode})
   501→        return True
   502→
   503→    async def async_clear_usercode(self, code_slot: int) -> bool:
   504→        """
   505→        Clear a usercode on a code slot.
   506→
   507→        Returns True if the value was changed, False if already cleared.
   508→        """
   509→        # Check if the slot is already cleared (avoid unnecessary network call)
   510→        try:
   511→            current = get_usercode(self.node, code_slot)
   512→            if not current.get("in_use"):
   513→                _LOGGER.debug(
   514→                    "Lock %s slot %s already cleared, skipping clear",
   515→                    self.lock.entity_id,
   516→                    code_slot,
   517→                )
   518→                return False
   519→        except Exception:
   520→            # If we can't check the cache, proceed with the clear
   521→            pass
   522→
   523→        service_data = {
   524→            ATTR_ENTITY_ID: self.lock.entity_id,
   525→            ATTR_CODE_SLOT: code_slot,
   526→        }
   527→        await self.async_call_service(
   528→            ZWAVE_JS_DOMAIN, SERVICE_CLEAR_LOCK_USERCODE, service_data
   529→        )
   530→        # Optimistic update: Z-Wave command succeeded (lock acknowledged), but the
   531→        # value cache updates asynchronously via push notification. Update coordinator
   532→        # immediately to prevent sync loops from reading stale cache data.
   533→        if self.coordinator:
   534→            self.coordinator.push_update({code_slot: ""})
   535→        return True
   536→
   537→    def _get_usercodes_from_cache(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   538→        """Get usercodes from Z-Wave JS value DB cache."""
   539→        try:
   540→            return list(get_usercodes(self.node) or [])
   541→        except Exception as err:
   542→            raise LockDisconnected from err
   543→
   544→    async def _async_refresh_usercode_cache(self) -> None:
   545→        """Refresh usercode cache from the device."""
   546→        try:
   547→            await self.node.async_refresh_cc_values(CommandClass.USER_CODE)
   548→        except Exception as err:
   549→            raise LockDisconnected from err
   550→
   551→    async def async_get_usercodes(self) -> dict[int, int | str]:
   552→        """Get dictionary of code slots and usercodes."""
   553→        code_slots = {
   554→            int(code_slot)
   555→            for entry in self.hass.config_entries.async_entries(DOMAIN)
   556→            for code_slot in get_entry_data(entry, CONF_SLOTS, {})
   557→            if self.lock.entity_id in get_entry_data(entry, CONF_LOCKS, [])
   558→        }
   559→        data: dict[int, int | str] = {}
   560→
   561→        if not await self.async_is_connection_up():
   562→            raise LockDisconnected
   563→
   564→        slots = self._get_usercodes_from_cache()
   565→        slots_by_num = {int(slot["code_slot"]): slot for slot in slots}
   566→
   567→        # If any configured slot is missing or has unknown state, do one hard
   568→        # refresh to populate the cache. This is more efficient than fetching
   569→        # individual slots and uses Z-Wave JS's checksum optimization.
   570→        # Note: We call _async_refresh_usercode_cache directly here to avoid
   571→        # recursion since async_hard_refresh_codes calls async_get_usercodes.
   572→        if any(
   573→            slot_num not in slots_by_num or slots_by_num[slot_num].get("in_use") is None
   574→            for slot_num in code_slots
   575→        ):
   576→            _LOGGER.debug(
   577→                "Lock %s has missing/unknown slots, performing hard refresh",
   578→                self.lock.entity_id,
   579→            )
   580→            await self._async_refresh_usercode_cache()
   581→            slots = self._get_usercodes_from_cache()
   582→            slots_by_num = {int(slot["code_slot"]): slot for slot in slots}
   583→
   584→        for slot in slots:
   585→            code_slot = int(slot["code_slot"])
   586→            usercode: str = slot["usercode"] or ""
   587→            in_use: bool | None = slot["in_use"]
   588→
   589→            if not in_use:
   590→                data[code_slot] = ""
   591→            # Resolve PIN (handles masked codes), skip if unresolvable
   592→            elif resolved := self._resolve_pin_if_masked(usercode, code_slot):
   593→                data[code_slot] = resolved
   594→
   595→        slots_with_pin = [s for s, v in data.items() if v]
   596→        slots_not_enabled = [s for s, v in data.items() if not v]
   597→        _LOGGER.debug(
   598→            "Lock %s: %s slots with PIN %s, %s slots not enabled %s",
   599→            self.lock.entity_id,
   600→            len(slots_with_pin),
   601→            slots_with_pin,
   602→            len(slots_not_enabled),
   603→            slots_not_enabled,
   604→        )
   605→        return data
   606→

   193→async def test_set_usercode_skips_when_masked_code_matches(
   194→    hass: HomeAssistant,
   195→    zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock,
   196→    zwave_integration: MockConfigEntry,
   197→) -> None:
   198→    """Test that set_usercode returns False when masked code resolves to same PIN.
   199→
   200→    Some locks (like Yale) return masked PINs (****) instead of actual codes.
   201→    When the masked code resolves to the same PIN we're trying to set, we should
   202→    skip the set operation to prevent battery drain from repeated writes.
   203→    """
   204→    lcm_entry = MockConfigEntry(
   205→        domain=DOMAIN,
   206→        data={
   207→            CONF_LOCKS: [zwave_js_lock.lock.entity_id],
   208→            CONF_SLOTS: {"2": {}},
   209→        },
   210→    )
   211→    lcm_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
   212→    await zwave_js_lock.async_setup(lcm_entry)
   213→
   214→    # Mock the cache to return a masked code
   215→    masked_slot = {"code_slot": 2, "usercode": "****", "in_use": True}
   216→
   217→    with (
   218→        patch(
   219→            "custom_components.lock_code_manager.providers.zwave_js.get_usercode",
   220→            return_value=masked_slot,
   221→        ),
   222→        patch.object(
   223→            zwave_js_lock, "_resolve_pin_if_masked", return_value="5678"
   224→        ) as mock_resolve,
   225→        patch.object(
   226→            zwave_js_lock, "async_call_service", new_callable=AsyncMock
   227→        ) as mock_service,
   228→    ):
   229→        # Try to set the same PIN that the masked code resolves to
   230→        result = await zwave_js_lock.async_set_usercode(2, "5678", "Test User")
   231→
   232→        # Should skip the set operation
   233→        assert result is False
   234→        mock_resolve.assert_called_once_with("****", 2)
   235→        mock_service.assert_not_called()
   236→
   237→    await zwave_js_lock.async_unload(False)
   238→

   376→async def test_set_usercode_optimistic_update(
   377→    hass: HomeAssistant,
   378→    zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock,
   379→    zwave_integration: MockConfigEntry,
   380→) -> None:
   381→    """Test that set_usercode performs optimistic coordinator update.
   382→
   383→    When a set operation succeeds, the coordinator should be updated immediately
   384→    with the new value. This prevents sync loops where the binary sensor reads
   385→    stale cached data and triggers repeated sync attempts.
   386→
   387→    The Z-Wave command is acknowledged by the lock (via Supervision CC), but
   388→    the JS value cache updates asynchronously via push notifications. Without
   389→    the optimistic update, there's a race condition where coordinator refresh
   390→    reads stale cache data.
   391→    """
   392→    lcm_entry = MockConfigEntry(domain=DOMAIN, data={CONF_LOCKS: [], CONF_SLOTS: {}})
   393→    lcm_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
   394→    await zwave_js_lock.async_setup(lcm_entry)
   395→
   396→    # Set up a mock coordinator with stale data (simulating the race condition)
   397→    mock_coordinator = MagicMock()
   398→    mock_coordinator.data = {4: ""}  # Slot appears empty in stale cache
   399→    zwave_js_lock.coordinator = mock_coordinator
   400→
   401→    with patch.object(zwave_js_lock, "async_call_service", new_callable=AsyncMock):
   402→        result = await zwave_js_lock.async_set_usercode(4, "5678", "Test User")
   403→
   404→        assert result is True
   405→        # Verify optimistic update was called with new PIN
   406→        mock_coordinator.push_update.assert_called_once_with({4: "5678"})
   407→
   408→    await zwave_js_lock.async_unload(False)
   409→
   410→
   411→async def test_set_usercode_optimistic_update_prevents_stale_read(
   412→    hass: HomeAssistant,
   413→    zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock,
   414→    zwave_integration: MockConfigEntry,
   415→) -> None:
   416→    """Test that optimistic update prevents sync loops from stale cache reads.
   417→
   418→    This test verifies the fix for the reported issue where out-of-sync slots
   419→    cause constant lock activity. The scenario:
   420→    1. LCM sets a code on the lock
   421→    2. Z-Wave command succeeds (lock acknowledges)
   422→    3. Without optimistic update: coordinator.data still has old value
   423→    4. Binary sensor sees mismatch → triggers another sync → loop
   424→
   425→    With the fix, push_update immediately sets coordinator.data to the new value,
   426→    so the binary sensor sees the expected value and doesn't retry.
   427→    """
   428→    lcm_entry = MockConfigEntry(domain=DOMAIN, data={CONF_LOCKS: [], CONF_SLOTS: {}})
   429→    lcm_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
   430→    await zwave_js_lock.async_setup(lcm_entry)
   431→
   432→    # Simulate stale cache: coordinator thinks slot is empty
   433→    mock_coordinator = MagicMock()
   434→    mock_coordinator.data = {4: ""}
   435→    zwave_js_lock.coordinator = mock_coordinator
   436→
   437→    with patch.object(zwave_js_lock, "async_call_service", new_callable=AsyncMock):
   438→        await zwave_js_lock.async_set_usercode(4, "9999")
   439→
   440→        # The optimistic update should have been called
   441→        mock_coordinator.push_update.assert_called_once_with({4: "9999"})
   442→
   443→        # Simulate what push_update does - update coordinator data
   444→        # (In real code, push_update calls async_set_updated_data which does this)
   445→        mock_coordinator.data[4] = "9999"
   446→
   447→        # Now coordinator.data reflects the expected value
   448→        # Binary sensor would see coordinator.data[4] == "9999" == pin_state
   449→        # → expected_in_sync = True → no retry loop
   450→        assert mock_coordinator.data[4] == "9999"
   451→
   452→    await zwave_js_lock.async_unload(False)
   453→
   454→

   687→
   688→def async_capture_events(
   689→    hass: HomeAssistant, event_name: str
   690→) -> list[Event[dict[str, Any]]]:
   691→    """Create a helper that captures events."""
   692→    events: list[Event[dict[str, Any]]] = []
   693→
   694→    @callback
   695→    def capture_events(event: Event[dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
   696→        events.append(event)
   697→
   698→    hass.bus.async_listen(event_name, capture_events)
   699→    return events
