   793→
   794→async def test_get_usercodes_masked_pin_unmanaged_slot_returns_masked_value(
   795→    hass: HomeAssistant,
   796→    zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock,
   797→    zwave_integration: MockConfigEntry,
   798→) -> None:
   799→    """Test mixed slots: managed with real code vs unmanaged with masked code.
   800→
   801→    This test verifies behavior when the lock cache contains:
   802→    - Slot 1: Managed by LCM, has real code "9999" -> should be returned
   803→    - Slot 5: NOT managed by LCM, has masked code "****" -> returns masked value
   804→
   805→    Unmanaged slots with masked PINs return the masked value so sync logic
   806→    knows a PIN exists on the lock, even if we can't resolve the actual value.
   807→    """
   808→    # Configure LCM to only manage slot 1 (not slot 5)
   809→    lcm_entry = MockConfigEntry(
   810→        domain=DOMAIN,
   811→        data={
   812→            CONF_LOCKS: [zwave_js_lock.lock.entity_id],
   813→            CONF_SLOTS: {"1": {}},  # Only slot 1 is managed
   814→        },
   815→    )
   816→    lcm_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
   817→    await zwave_js_lock.async_setup(lcm_entry)
   818→
   819→    # Mock the cache to include a slot with a masked PIN that isn't managed by LCM
   820→    masked_slots = [
   821→        {"code_slot": 1, "usercode": "9999", "in_use": True},  # Managed by LCM
   822→        {"code_slot": 5, "usercode": "****", "in_use": True},  # NOT managed, masked
   823→    ]
   824→
   825→    with (
   826→        patch.object(
   827→            zwave_js_lock, "_get_usercodes_from_cache", return_value=masked_slots
   828→        ),
   829→        # Slot 5 not in Z-Wave node data, so code_slot_in_use returns None
   830→        patch.object(
   831→            zwave_js_lock,
   832→            "code_slot_in_use",
   833→            side_effect=lambda s: True if s == 1 else None,
   834→        ),
   835→    ):
   836→        codes = await zwave_js_lock.async_get_usercodes()
   837→
   838→        # Slot 1 should have its code
   839→        assert codes[1] == "9999"
   840→        # Slot 5 returns masked value (so sync logic knows a PIN exists)
   841→        assert codes[5] == "****"
   842→
   843→    await zwave_js_lock.async_unload(False)
   844→

   924→async def test_resolve_pin_if_masked_detection(zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock) -> None:
   925→    """Test _resolve_pin_if_masked returns value as-is when not masked."""
   926→    # Not masked - returns value as-is
   927→    assert zwave_js_lock._resolve_pin_if_masked("1234", 1) == "1234"
   928→    assert zwave_js_lock._resolve_pin_if_masked("5678", 2) == "5678"

   930→    # Partially masked - returns as-is (not all asterisks)
   931→    assert zwave_js_lock._resolve_pin_if_masked("***1", 1) == "***1"
   932→    assert zwave_js_lock._resolve_pin_if_masked("1***", 1) == "1***"

   935→async def test_push_update_masked_code_resolved(
   936→    hass: HomeAssistant,
   937→    zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock,
   938→    zwave_integration: MockConfigEntry,
   939→    lock_schlage_be469: Node,
   940→) -> None:
   941→    """Test that push updates with masked codes resolve and update coordinator.
   942→
   943→    When a push update arrives with a masked code and it can be resolved,
   944→    the resolved PIN should be pushed to the coordinator.
   945→    """
   946→    lcm_entry = MockConfigEntry(
   947→        domain=DOMAIN,
   948→        data={
   949→            CONF_LOCKS: [zwave_js_lock.lock.entity_id],
   950→            CONF_SLOTS: {"2": {}},
   951→        },
   952→    )
   953→    lcm_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
   954→    await zwave_js_lock.async_setup(lcm_entry)
   955→
   956→    # Set up a mock coordinator (push_update is synchronous)
   957→    mock_coordinator = MagicMock()
   958→    mock_coordinator.data = {}
   959→    zwave_js_lock.coordinator = mock_coordinator
   960→
   961→    # Subscribe to push updates
   962→    zwave_js_lock.subscribe_push_updates()
   963→
   964→    # Mock _resolve_pin_if_masked to return a PIN
   965→    with patch.object(zwave_js_lock, "_resolve_pin_if_masked", return_value="9876"):
   966→        # Simulate a value update event with masked code
   967→        event = ZwaveEvent(
   968→            type="value updated",
   969→            data={
   970→                "source": "node",
   971→                "event": "value updated",
   972→                "nodeId": lock_schlage_be469.node_id,
   973→                "args": {
   974→                    "commandClass": CommandClass.USER_CODE,
   975→                    "property": "userCode",
   976→                    "propertyKey": 2,
   977→                    "newValue": "****",
   978→                },
   979→            },
   980→        )
   981→        lock_schlage_be469.receive_event(event)
   982→        await hass.async_block_till_done()
   983→
   984→        # Coordinator should receive the resolved PIN, not the masked value
   985→        mock_coordinator.push_update.assert_called_once_with({2: "9876"})
   986→
   987→    zwave_js_lock.unsubscribe_push_updates()
   988→    await zwave_js_lock.async_unload(False)
   989→

   991→async def test_push_update_masked_code_skipped_when_unresolvable(
   992→    hass: HomeAssistant,
   993→    zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock,
   994→    zwave_integration: MockConfigEntry,
   995→    lock_schlage_be469: Node,
   996→) -> None:
   997→    """Test that push updates with unresolvable masked codes are skipped.
   998→
   999→    When a push update arrives with a masked code that cannot be resolved,
  1000→    the update should be skipped entirely to prevent infinite sync loops.
  1001→    """
  1002→    lcm_entry = MockConfigEntry(
  1003→        domain=DOMAIN,
  1004→        data={
  1005→            CONF_LOCKS: [zwave_js_lock.lock.entity_id],

  1010→    await zwave_js_lock.async_setup(lcm_entry)
  1011→
  1012→    # Set up a mock coordinator (push_update is synchronous)
  1013→    mock_coordinator = MagicMock()
  1014→    mock_coordinator.data = {}
  1015→    zwave_js_lock.coordinator = mock_coordinator
  1016→
  1017→    # Subscribe to push updates
  1018→    zwave_js_lock.subscribe_push_updates()
  1019→
  1020→    # Mock _resolve_pin_if_masked to return None (can't resolve)
  1021→    with patch.object(zwave_js_lock, "_resolve_pin_if_masked", return_value=None):
  1022→        # Simulate a value update event with masked code
  1023→        event = ZwaveEvent(
  1024→            type="value updated",
  1025→            data={
  1026→                "source": "node",
  1027→                "event": "value updated",
  1028→                "nodeId": lock_schlage_be469.node_id,
  1029→                "args": {
  1030→                    "commandClass": CommandClass.USER_CODE,
  1031→                    "property": "userCode",
  1032→                    "propertyKey": 2,
  1033→                    "newValue": "****",
  1034→                },
  1035→            },
  1036→        )
  1037→        lock_schlage_be469.receive_event(event)
  1038→        await hass.async_block_till_done()
  1039→
  1040→        # Coordinator should NOT receive any update
  1041→        mock_coordinator.push_update.assert_not_called()
  1042→
  1043→    zwave_js_lock.unsubscribe_push_updates()
  1044→    await zwave_js_lock.async_unload(False)

  1268→async def test_push_update_user_id_status_available_clears_slot(
  1269→    hass: HomeAssistant,
  1270→    zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock,
  1271→    zwave_integration: MockConfigEntry,
  1272→    lock_schlage_be469: Node,
  1273→) -> None:
  1274→    """Test that userIdStatus=AVAILABLE push update clears the slot.
  1275→
  1276→    When the lock sends a userIdStatus update with AVAILABLE status,
  1277→    it means the slot has been cleared. This should update the coordinator
  1278→    to mark the slot as empty.
  1279→    """
  1280→    lcm_entry = MockConfigEntry(
  1281→        domain=DOMAIN,
  1282→        data={
  1283→            CONF_LOCKS: [zwave_js_lock.lock.entity_id],
  1284→            CONF_SLOTS: {"2": {}},
  1285→        },
  1286→    )
  1287→    lcm_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
  1288→    await zwave_js_lock.async_setup(lcm_entry)
  1289→
  1290→    # Set up a mock coordinator with existing data
  1291→    mock_coordinator = MagicMock()
  1292→    mock_coordinator.data = {2: "1234"}  # Slot has a PIN
  1293→    zwave_js_lock.coordinator = mock_coordinator
  1294→
  1295→    # Subscribe to push updates
  1296→    zwave_js_lock.subscribe_push_updates()
  1297→
  1298→    # Simulate userIdStatus=AVAILABLE event (slot cleared)
  1299→    event = ZwaveEvent(
  1300→        type="value updated",
  1301→        data={
  1302→            "args": {
  1303→                "commandClass": CommandClass.USER_CODE,
  1304→                "property": LOCK_USERCODE_STATUS_PROPERTY,
  1305→                "propertyKey": 2,
  1306→                "newValue": CodeSlotStatus.AVAILABLE,
  1307→            },
  1308→        },
  1309→    )
  1310→    lock_schlage_be469.emit("value updated", event.data)
  1311→    await hass.async_block_till_done()
  1312→
  1313→    # Coordinator should be updated with empty string
  1314→    mock_coordinator.push_update.assert_called_once_with({2: ""})
  1315→
  1316→    zwave_js_lock.unsubscribe_push_updates()
  1317→    await zwave_js_lock.async_unload(False)
  1318→

  1482→    a slot is cleared. When the slot is confirmed not in use, these should

  1488→        assert zwave_js_lock._resolve_pin_if_masked("000000", 1) == ""
  1489→        assert zwave_js_lock._resolve_pin_if_masked("00", 1) == ""

  1645→async def test_push_update_user_id_status_available_ignored_when_slot_expects_pin(
  1646→    hass: HomeAssistant,
  1647→    zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock,
  1648→    zwave_integration: MockConfigEntry,
  1649→    lock_schlage_be469: Node,
  1650→) -> None:
  1651→    """Test that userIdStatus=AVAILABLE is ignored when slot expects a PIN.
  1652→
  1653→    This prevents sync loops where the lock sends stale AVAILABLE status
  1654→    after a code was successfully set.
  1655→    """
  1656→    lcm_entry = MockConfigEntry(
  1657→        domain=DOMAIN,
  1658→        data={
  1659→            CONF_LOCKS: [zwave_js_lock.lock.entity_id],
  1660→            CONF_SLOTS: {"2": {}},
  1661→        },
  1662→    )
  1663→    lcm_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
  1664→    await zwave_js_lock.async_setup(lcm_entry)
  1665→
  1666→    # Set up a mock coordinator with existing PIN
  1667→    mock_coordinator = MagicMock()
  1668→    mock_coordinator.data = {2: "1234"}  # Slot has a PIN
  1669→    zwave_js_lock.coordinator = mock_coordinator
  1670→
  1671→    # Subscribe to push updates
  1672→    zwave_js_lock.subscribe_push_updates()
  1673→
  1674→    # Mock _slot_expects_pin to return True (LCM expects a PIN on this slot)
  1675→    with patch.object(zwave_js_lock, "_slot_expects_pin", return_value=True):
  1676→        # Simulate userIdStatus=AVAILABLE event (stale status from lock)
  1677→        event = ZwaveEvent(
  1678→            type="value updated",
  1679→            data={
  1680→                "args": {
  1681→                    "commandClass": CommandClass.USER_CODE,
  1682→                    "property": LOCK_USERCODE_STATUS_PROPERTY,
  1683→                    "propertyKey": 2,
  1684→                    "newValue": CodeSlotStatus.AVAILABLE,
  1685→                },
  1686→            },
  1687→        )
  1688→        lock_schlage_be469.emit("value updated", event.data)
  1689→        await hass.async_block_till_done()
  1690→
  1691→        # Coordinator should NOT be updated (AVAILABLE ignored)
  1692→        mock_coordinator.push_update.assert_not_called()
  1693→
  1694→    zwave_js_lock.unsubscribe_push_updates()
  1695→    await zwave_js_lock.async_unload(False)

   102→            "hard_refresh_codes"

   105→    def set_usercode(
   106→        self, code_slot: int, usercode: int | str, name: str | None = None
   107→    ) -> bool:
   108→        """Set a usercode on a code slot.
   109→
   110→        Returns True if the value was changed, False if already set to this value.
   111→        """
   112→        lock_data = self.hass.data.get(LOCK_DATA, {}).get(self.lock.entity_id)
   113→        if lock_data:
   114→            # Check if value already matches
   115→            if lock_data["codes"].get(code_slot) == usercode:
   116→                return False
   117→            lock_data["codes"][code_slot] = usercode
   118→            lock_data["service_calls"]["set_usercode"].append(
   119→                (code_slot, usercode, name)
   120→            )
   121→            return True
   122→        return True
   123→
   124→    def clear_usercode(self, code_slot: int) -> bool:
   125→        """Clear a usercode on a code slot.
   126→
   127→        Returns True if the value was changed, False if already cleared.
   128→        """
   129→        lock_data = self.hass.data.get(LOCK_DATA, {}).get(self.lock.entity_id)
   130→        if lock_data:
   131→            if code_slot not in lock_data["codes"]:
   132→                return False
   133→            lock_data["codes"].pop(code_slot, None)
   134→            lock_data["service_calls"]["clear_usercode"].append((code_slot,))

    84→- Current guard uses `_attr_is_on is None` to avoid initial sync operations
    85→
    86→**Proposed Solution:**
    87→Move sync logic entirely into the coordinator:
    88→
    89→- Coordinator already has access to both desired state (from config) and actual
    90→  state (from lock)
    91→- Coordinator performs sync operations during its `_async_update_data()` cycle
    92→- Binary sensor becomes read-only, just displays coordinator's computed in-sync
    93→  status
    94→- Text/number/switch entities remain as config views
    95→
    96→**Example Implementation:**
    97→
    98→```python
    99→# In coordinator._async_update_data()
   100→actual_code = await self.provider.get_usercodes()
   101→desired_code = self.config_entry.data[slot]["pin"]
   102→
   103→if actual_code != desired_code and slot_enabled:
   104→    await self.provider.set_usercode(slot, desired_code)
   105→
   106→return {"in_sync": actual_code == desired_code, "actual_code": actual_code}
   107→```
   108→
   109→**Benefits:**
   110→
   111→- Eliminates cross-entity state reading
   112→- Removes `_initial_state_loaded` flag and startup detection logic
   113→- No race conditions during startup
   114→- Simpler, more centralized sync logic
   115→- Coordinator is single source of truth
   116→
   117→**Considerations:**
   118→
   119→- Major architectural change
   120→- Would need to update binary sensor to be read-only
   121→- Config updates still flow through text/switch entities
   122→- Need to ensure coordinator runs sync on config changes
   123→
   124→**Estimated Effort:** High (16-24 hours)
   125→**Priority:** Medium
   126→**Status:** Not started
   127→
   128→### Convert Config and Internal Dicts to Dataclasses
   129→
   130→Convert config entry data to typed dataclasses with `from_dict`/`from_entry`
   131→class methods. Use object instances internally instead of iterating through raw
   132→config dicts. Audit codebase for other complex dicts that would benefit from
   133→dataclass conversion (e.g., slot data, lock state, coordinator data). This
   134→improves type safety, IDE autocompletion, and code readability.
   135→
   136→**Why not Voluptuous?** Voluptuous is for validation, not object instantiation.
   137→Other options like `dacite` or Pydantic add dependencies.
   138→
   139→**Example implementation:**
   140→
   141→```python
   142→@dataclass
   143→class SlotConfig:
   144→    name: str
   145→    pin: str
   146→    enabled: bool = True
   147→    calendar: str | None = None
   148→    number_of_uses: int | None = None
   149→
   150→    @classmethod
   151→    def from_dict(cls, data: dict) -> SlotConfig:
   152→        return cls(
   153→            name=data[CONF_NAME],
   154→            pin=data[CONF_PIN],
   155→            enabled=data.get(CONF_ENABLED, True),
   156→            calendar=data.get(CONF_CALENDAR),
   157→            number_of_uses=data.get(CONF_NUMBER_OF_USES),
   158→        )
   159→
   160→@dataclass
   161→class LCMConfig:
   162→    locks: list[str]
   163→    slots: dict[int, SlotConfig]
   164→
   165→    @classmethod
   166→    def from_entry(cls, entry: ConfigEntry) -> LCMConfig:
   167→        return cls(
   168→            locks=get_entry_data(entry, CONF_LOCKS, []),
   169→            slots={
   170→                int(k): SlotConfig.from_dict(v)
   171→                for k, v in get_entry_data(entry, CONF_SLOTS, {}).items()
   172→            },
   173→        )
   174→```
   175→
   176→**Places to audit for dict-to-dataclass conversion:**
   177→
   178→- `config_entry.data` / `config_entry.options` access patterns
   179→- `get_entry_data()` / `get_slot_data()` return values
   180→- Coordinator `self.data` structure
   181→- Lock provider internal state
   182→
   183→### Handle Disabled Lock Slots
   184→
   185→**Context:** Z-Wave locks have `userIdStatus` which can be `Enabled`, `Available`,
   186→or `Disabled`. Currently the coordinator only stores the code value, not the status.
   187→
   188→**Investigation Needed:**
   189→
   190→1. Test what happens when LCM tries to set a user code on a slot with
   191→   `userIdStatus=Disabled`
   192→2. Determine if we need to explicitly enable the slot before setting a code
   193→3. Check if different lock brands handle disabled slots differently
   194→
   195→**Related:** See "Enhance Coordinator Data Model" below.
   196→
   197→**Estimated Effort:** Medium (4-8 hours)
   198→**Priority:** Medium
   199→**Status:** Not started
   200→
   201→### Enhance Coordinator Data Model with Slot Status
   202→
   203→**Current State:** Coordinator stores `{slot: code}` mapping only.
   204→
   205→**Proposed Change:** Store `{slot: {code, status}}` where status is a generic
   206→LCM enum that providers map to.
   207→
   208→**Generic Status Enum:**
   209→
   210→```python
   211→class SlotStatus(StrEnum):
   212→    ENABLED = "enabled"    # Slot has active code
   213→    AVAILABLE = "available"  # Slot can be used but is empty
   214→    DISABLED = "disabled"  # Slot cannot be used (locked out)
   215→```
   216→
   217→**Provider Mapping:**
   218→
   219→- Z-Wave JS: Maps `userIdStatus` (Enabled/Available/Disabled) → `SlotStatus`
   220→- Other providers: Map their equivalent states to the generic enum
   221→
   222→**Benefits:**
   223→
   224→- Frontend can distinguish between "slot is empty" vs "slot is disabled"
   225→- Better handling of disabled slots in sync logic
   226→- More accurate representation of lock state
   227→- Provider-agnostic data model
   228→
   229→**Implementation:**
   230→
   231→1. Define `SlotStatus` enum in `const.py`
   232→2. Update Z-Wave JS provider to track userIdStatus and map to `SlotStatus`
   233→   (currently filtered out in `on_value_updated`)
   234→3. Change coordinator data schema from `dict[int, str]` to
   235→   `dict[int, SlotData]` where `SlotData` includes code and status
   236→4. Update all consumers of coordinator data (binary_sensor, sensor, websocket)
   237→5. Update frontend types and rendering
   238→
   239→**Estimated Effort:** High (12-16 hours)
   240→**Priority:** Medium
   241→**Status:** Not started
   242→
   243→### Add Optional Flags to `get_config_entry_data` Websocket Command
   244→
   245→**Context:** PR #787 consolidated multiple websocket commands into a single
   246→`get_config_entry_data` command that returns `{config_entry, entities, locks, slots}`.
   247→However, not all callers need all the data:
   248→
   249→| Caller | config_entry | entities | locks | slots |
   250→| ------ | ------------ | -------- | ----- | ----- |
   251→| `view-strategy.ts` | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |
   252→| `generate-view.ts` | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
   253→| `slot-section-strategy.ts` (legacy) | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ |
   254→| `dashboard-strategy.ts` | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ |
   255→| `lock-codes-card-editor.ts` | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ |
   256→
   257→**Cost Analysis:**
   258→
   259→- `config_entry` - Very cheap (just `config_entry.as_json_fragment`)
   260→- `slots` - Very cheap (extracts calendar IDs from config)
   261→- `locks` - Moderate (iterates locks, gets friendly names via state lookups)
   262→- `entities` - Most expensive (queries entity registry, maps to `as_partial_dict`)
   263→
   264→**Proposed Change:** Add optional `include_entities` and `include_locks` flags
   265→(default `True` for backwards compatibility). Skip `config_entry` and `slots`
   266→flags since they're essentially free.
   267→
   268→```python
   269→vol.Optional("include_entities", default=True): bool,
   270→vol.Optional("include_locks", default=True): bool,
   271→```
   272→
   273→**Benefits:**
   274→
   275→- `view-strategy.ts` can skip both entities and locks
   276→- `dashboard-strategy.ts` and `lock-codes-card-editor.ts` can skip entities
   277→- Legacy `slot-section-strategy.ts` can skip locks
   278→
   279→**Estimated Effort:** Low (2-4 hours)
   280→**Priority:** Low
   281→**Status:** Not started

   328→### Add Schedule and Entity Condition Types
   329→
   330→**Problem:** Users report that managing calendars in HA is too painful for simple
   331→recurring schedules. Calendars are overkill for "weekdays 9-5" patterns.
   332→
   333→**Proposed Solution:** Add alternative condition types alongside `calendar`:
   334→
   335→| Condition Type | Use Case |
   336→| -------------- | -------- |
   337→| `calendar` | One-time events, external calendar sync (existing) |
   338→| `schedule` | Recurring weekly patterns via HA schedule helper |
   339→| `entity` | Custom logic via any binary sensor/input_boolean |
   340→
   341→**Implementation:**
   342→
   343→1. **Config Flow Changes:**
   344→   - Add condition type selector (calendar/schedule/entity)
   345→   - Show appropriate entity selector based on type
   346→   - `schedule`: EntitySelector filtered to `schedule` domain
   347→   - `entity`: EntitySelector filtered to `binary_sensor`, `input_boolean`
   348→
   349→2. **Binary Sensor Changes:**
   350→   - Update `_get_entity_state()` to handle different condition types
   351→   - Schedule entities: check if current time is within schedule (state = "on")
   352→   - Entity conditions: directly use entity state
   353→
   354→3. **Slot Data Model:**
   355→   - Add `condition_type` field: `calendar | schedule | entity`
   356→   - Add `condition_entity` field (alternative to `calendar`)
   357→   - Maintain backward compatibility with existing `calendar` field
   358→
   359→4. **Frontend Updates:**
   360→   - Update slot card to show condition type
   361→   - Show appropriate icon/label for each type
   362→
   363→**Benefits:**
   364→
   365→- Schedule helper is much simpler for recurring patterns
   366→- Entity condition allows maximum flexibility (templates, automations)
   367→- Calendar remains available for complex/one-time events
   368→
   369→**Estimated Effort:** Medium (8-12 hours)
   370→**Priority:** Medium-High

   373→### Advanced Calendar Configuration
   374→
   375→**Feature Request:** Allow slot number and PIN to be configured directly in
   376→calendar event metadata, eliminating need for separate slot configuration.
   377→
   378→**Design Considerations:**
   379→
   380→**Current Behavior:**
   381→
   382→- Slot configured in config flow with fixed PIN
   383→- Calendar event (when present) only controls whether slot is active/inactive
   384→- PIN and slot number are static configuration
   385→
   386→**Proposed Behavior:**
   387→
   388→- Calendar event contains slot number and PIN in its metadata
   389→- User configures regex/pattern to extract slot number and PIN from:
   390→  - Event title (e.g., "Slot 3: 1234")
   391→  - Event description
   392→  - Event location
   393→  - Custom calendar properties
   394→
   395→**Implementation Requirements:**
   396→
   397→1. **Config Flow Changes:**
   398→   - Add "advanced calendar mode" toggle per slot
   399→   - When enabled, show pattern configuration UI
   400→   - Pattern fields: slot number regex, PIN regex, which field to parse
   401→     (title/description/location)
   402→2. **Entity Changes:**
   403→   - Calendar event listener needs to parse event metadata
   404→   - Extract slot number and PIN based on user-defined patterns
   405→   - Validate extracted values (numeric slot, PIN format)
   406→3. **Binary Sensor Changes:**
   407→   - Check if calendar event contains valid extracted values
   408→   - Use extracted PIN instead of configured PIN
   409→   - Handle multiple calendar events with different slots
   410→
   411→**Example Patterns:**
   412→
   413→- Title: "Guest Access: Slot 5, PIN 9876" -> Slot: `\d+`, PIN: `\d{4}$`
   414→- Description: "Code: 1234 for slot 3" -> Slot: `slot (\d+)`, PIN: `Code: (\d+)`
   415→- Location: "5:1234" -> Slot: `^(\d+):`, PIN: `:(\d+)$`
   416→
   417→**Challenges:**
   418→
   419→- Multiple calendar events with different slots
   420→- Error handling for invalid patterns
   421→- UI for testing patterns
   422→- Backward compatibility with existing simple calendar mode
   423→
   424→**Estimated Effort:** Very High (40+ hours)
   425→**Priority:** Medium
   426→**Status:** Not started

## Summary: Reading Z-Wave Command Class Version from a Node

Based on my analysis of the `zwave_js_server` package in your project, here's how to read the User Code CC (id=99) version from a `zwave_js_server.model.node.Node` object:

### Package Location
The zwave_js_server package is installed at:
- `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/zwave_js_server/`

### How It Works

#### 1. **Node.command_classes Property**
The `Node` class exposes a `command_classes` property that returns a list of `CommandClassInfo` objects:

**File:** `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/zwave_js_server/model/node/__init__.py` (line 329-331)
```python
@property
def command_classes(self) -> list[CommandClassInfo]:
    """Return all CommandClasses supported on this node."""
    return self.endpoints[0].command_classes
```

This delegates to the first endpoint's command_classes, which in turn creates `CommandClassInfo` objects from the raw data.

#### 2. **CommandClassInfo Model**
The `CommandClassInfo` class provides properties to access command class information:

**File:** `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/zwave_js_server/model/command_class.py` (lines 23-58)

```python
class CommandClassInfo:
    """Model for a Zwave CommandClass Info."""

    def __init__(self, data: CommandClassInfoDataType) -> None:
        """Initialize."""
        self.data = data

    @property
    def id(self) -> int:
        """Return CommandClass ID."""
        return self.data["id"]

    @property
    def version(self) -> int:
        """Return the CommandClass version used on this node/endpoint."""
        return self.data["version"]

    @property
    def is_secure(self) -> bool:
        """Return if the CommandClass is used securely on this node/endpoint."""
        return self.data["isSecure"]

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        """Return friendly name for CommandClass."""
        return self.data["name"]
```

#### 3. **User Code CC ID**
The User Code command class has ID `99`, defined in:

**File:** `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/zwave_js_server/const/__init__.py` (line 181)
```python
USER_CODE = 99
```

### How to Get the User Code CC Version

**Option 1: Using the CommandClass enum (Recommended)**
```python
from zwave_js_server.const import CommandClass
from zwave_js_server.model.node import Node

node: Node = ...  # Your node instance

# Get the User Code CC info
user_code_cc = next(
    (cc for cc in node.command_classes if cc.id == CommandClass.USER_CODE.value),
    None
)

if user_code_cc:
    version = user_code_cc.version
    print(f"User Code CC version: {version}")
    print(f"Is secure: {user_code_cc.is_secure}")
    print(f"Name: {user_code_cc.name}")
```

**Option 2: Direct ID comparison**
```python
# If you don't want to import CommandClass
user_code_cc = next(
    (cc for cc in node.command_classes if cc.id == 99),
    None
)

if user_code_cc:
    version = user_code_cc.version
```

**Option 3: Search through endpoints (if needed for a specific endpoint)**
```python
# Access all endpoints and their command classes
for endpoint in node.endpoints:
    for cc in endpoint.command_classes:
        if cc.id == 99:  # User Code CC
            print(f"Endpoint {endpoint.index}: User Code v{cc.version}")
```

### Data Structure

The underlying data structure is defined as:

**File:** `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/zwave_js_server/model/command_class.py` (lines 14-21)
```python
class CommandClassInfoDataType(TypedDict):
    """Represent a command class info data dict type."""

    id: int
    name: str
    version: int
    isSecure: bool
```

### Practical Example from Your Code

In your `zwave_js.py` provider file, you're already working with the `node` object. You could add a helper method like:

```python
def get_usercode_cc_version(self) -> int | None:
    """Get the User Code command class version from the node."""
    try:
        user_code_cc = next(
            (cc for cc in self.node.command_classes if cc.id == CommandClass.USER_CODE.value),
            None
        )
        return user_code_cc.version if user_code_cc else None
    except Exception:
        return None

     1→# User Code CC V1 Support
     2→
     3→## Problem
     4→
     5→The Z-Wave JS provider is optimized for User Code Command Class V2. Locks using
     6→V1 experience sync loops because:
     7→
     8→1. V1 nodes lack Supervision CC, so the Z-Wave JS driver always schedules
     9→   verification polls after set/clear (no optimistic cache update).
    10→2. `async_internal_set_usercode` calls `coordinator.async_request_refresh()`
    11→   after the optimistic `push_update()`, reading stale cache and overwriting the
    12→   correct optimistic data.
    13→3. V1 hard refresh queries every slot individually (no checksum optimization),
    14→   flooding the push handler with stale value-updated events.
    15→4. V1 nodes are not required to send unsolicited User Code Reports via Lifeline,
    16→   making push-based updates unreliable for detecting external changes.
    17→
    18→## Changes
    19→
    20→### 1. Remove `async_request_refresh()` after set/clear
    21→
    22→**File:** `providers/_base.py`
    23→
    24→Remove the `coordinator.async_request_refresh()` calls in
    25→`async_internal_set_usercode` and `async_internal_clear_usercode`. These defeat
    26→optimistic `push_update()` by reading potentially stale cache. The coordinator
    27→already receives correct data via:
    28→
    29→- Optimistic `push_update()` (push providers)
    30→- Next poll cycle (poll providers)
    31→
    32→This change benefits all providers, not just V1.
    33→
    34→### 2. Detect CC version and branch behavior
    35→
    36→**File:** `providers/zwave_js.py`
    37→
    38→Add a `_usercode_cc_version` cached property that reads the User Code CC version
    39→from the node's command class list.
    40→
    41→Branch key properties based on version:
    42→
    43→| Property | V1 | V2 |
    44→| --- | --- | --- |
    45→| `supports_push` | `False` | `True` |
    46→| `usercode_scan_interval` | 2 minutes | N/A (push) |
    47→| `hard_refresh_interval` | 30 minutes | 1 hour |
    48→| `connection_check_interval` | 30 seconds | `None` (config entry state) |
    49→
    50→V1 nodes still subscribe to Notification CC events (lock/unlock with code slot)
    51→since those use a different command class than User Code CC.
    52→
    53→### 3. Suppress push handler events during hard refresh
    54→
    55→**File:** `providers/zwave_js.py`
    56→
    57→Add a `_hard_refresh_in_progress` flag. Set it before
    58→`async_refresh_cc_values`, clear after. In `on_value_updated`, skip processing
    59→when the flag is set. This prevents stale value-updated events from V1's
    60→one-by-one slot re-query during drift detection.
    61→
    62→This also benefits V2 since intermediate events during cache rebuild are noise.
    63→
    64→### 4. TODOs for future work
    65→
    66→- Make `hard_refresh_interval` a user-configurable option.
    67→- Split hard refresh between managed and unmanaged slots. Managed slots (those
    68→  with LCM config) get refreshed at the normal interval (e.g., 30 min).
    69→  Unmanaged slots only need occasional drift awareness (e.g., once a day).
    70→
```

{

  "content": "# User Code CC V1 Support Implementation Plan\n\n> **For Claude:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task.\n\n**Goal:** Fix sync loops for Z-Wave locks using User Code CC V1 by removing stale\ncache reads, detecting CC version, branching provider behavior, and suppressing\npush events during hard refresh.\n\n**Architecture:** Remove `async_request_refresh()` after set/clear in the base\nclass (benefits all providers). Add CC version detection to `ZWaveJSLock` and\nbranch `supports_push`, polling intervals, and hard refresh intervals by version.\nAdd a `_hard_refresh_in_progress` flag to suppress stale value-updated events\nduring cache rebuild.\n\n**Tech Stack:** Python, Home Assistant custom component, zwave_js_server library,\npytest\n\n---\n\n### Task 1: Remove `async_request_refresh()` after set/clear\n\n**Files:**\n- Modify: `custom_components/lock_code_manager/providers/_base.py:509-519,561-569`\n- Modify: `tests/providers/test_base.py:394-452`\n\n**Step 1: Write the failing tests**\n\nReplace the two tests that assert `async_request_refresh` is called with tests\nthat verify it is NOT called. The set/clear methods should rely on optimistic\n`push_update()` (push providers) or the next poll cycle (poll providers), not\nan immediate refresh.\n\nIn `tests/providers/test_base.py`, replace\n`test_set_usercode_refreshes_coordinator_on_change` (line 394) with:\n\n```python\nasync def test_set_usercode_does_not_refresh_coordinator(\n    hass: HomeAssistant,\n    mock_lock_config_entry,\n    lock_code_manager_config_entry,\n):\n    \"\"\"Test that async_internal_set_usercode does not call async_request_refresh.\n\n    Set/clear rely on optimistic push_update() (push providers) or the next poll\n    cycle (poll providers). Calling async_request_refresh after set/clear defeats\n    optimistic updates by reading potentially stale cache.\n    \"\"\"\n    lock_provider = lock_code_manager_config_entry.runtime_data.locks[LOCK_1_ENTITY_ID]\n    coordinator = lock_provider.coordinator\n    assert coordinator is not None\n\n    refresh_count = 0\n    original_refresh = coordinator.async_request_refresh\n\n    async def track_refresh():\n        nonlocal refresh_count\n        refresh_count += 1\n        return await original_refresh()\n\n    with patch.object(coordinator, \"async_request_refresh\", track_refresh):\n        await lock_provider.async_internal_set_usercode(3, \"3333\", \"Test 3\")\n        assert refresh_count == 0\n```\n\nReplace `test_clear_usercode_refreshes_coordinator_on_change` (line 423) with:\n\n```python\nasync def test_clear_usercode_does_not_refresh_coordinator(\n    hass: HomeAssistant,\n nonlocal refresh_count\n        refresh_count += 1\n        return await original_refresh()\n\n    with patch.object(coordinator, \"async_request_refresh\", track_refresh):\n        await 0)\n\n**Step 3: Implement the change**\n\nIn `custom_components/lock_code_manager/providers/_base.py`, remove the\n`async_request_refresh` calls and their comments from both methods:\n\n`async_internal_set_usercode` becomes:\n```python\n@final\nasync def async_internal_set_usercode(\n    self, code_slot: int, usercode: int | str, name: str | None = None\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Set a usercode on a code slot.\"\"\"\n    await self._execute_rate_limited(\n        \"set\", self.async_set_usercode, code_slot, usercode, name=name\n ent_reg=ent_reg,\n        lock_config_entry=zwave_integration,\n        lock=lock_entity,\n    )\n    return lock\n```\n\nThen add these tests:\n\n```python\n# CC version detection tests\n\n\nasync def test_usercode_cc_version_v1(zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Test that V1 lock reports correct CC version.\"\"\"\n    assert zwave_js_lock._usercode_cc_version == 1\n\n\nasync def test_usercode_cc_version_v2(zwave_js_lock_v2: ZWaveJSLock) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Test that V2 lock reports correct CC version.\"\"\"\n    assert zwave_js_lock_v2._usercode_cc_version == 2\n\n\n# V1 property tests\n\n\nasync def test_v1_does_not_support_push(zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Test that V1 locks do not support push updates.\"\"\"\n    assert zwave_js_lock.supports_push is False\n\n\nasync def test_v1_usercode_scan_interval(zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Test that V1 locks poll every 2 minutes.\"\"\"\n    assert zwave_js_lock.usercode_scan_interval == timedelta(minutes=2)\n\n\nasync def test_v1_hard_refresh_interval(zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Test that V1 locks hard refresh every 30 minutes.\"\"\"\n    assert zwave_js_lock.hard_refresh_interval == timedelta(minutes=30)\n\n\nasync def test_v1_connection_check_interval(zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Test that V1 test_v2_supports_push(zwave_js_lock_v2: ZWaveJSLock) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Test that V2 locks support push updates.\"\"\"\n    assert zwave_js_lock_v2.supports_push is True\n\n\nasync def test_v2_hard_refresh_interval(zwave_js_lock_v2: ZWaveJSLock) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Test that V2 locks hard refresh every hour.\"\"\"\n    assert zwave_js_lock_v2.hard_refresh_interval == exist yet, supports_push returns True)\n\n**Step 5: Implement CC version detection and property branching**\n\nIn `custom_components/lock_code_manager/providers/zwave_js.py`:\n\nAdd `functools` import at the top:\n```python\nimport functools\n```\n\nAdd `_usercode_cc_version` cached property after the `node` property:\n\n```python\n@functools.cached_property\ndef _usercode_cc_version(self) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the User Code CC version supported by this node.\"\"\"\n    for cc in self.node.command_classes:\n        if cc.id == CommandClass.USER_CODE:\n            return cc.version\n    return 1  # Default to V1 if not found\n```\n\nUpdate `supports_push` to branch on version:\n\n```python\n@property\ndef supports_push(self) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Return whether this lock supports push-based updates.\n\n    V2 nodes emit reliable value-updated events via Lifeline.\n    V1 nodes don't reliably send unsolicited User Code Reports,\n    so we use polling instead.\n    \"\"\"\n    return self._usercode_cc_version >= 2\n```\n\nAdd `usercode_scan_interval` property:\n\n```python\n@property\ndef usercode_scan_interval(self) -> timedelta:\n    \"\"\"Return scan interval for usercodes.\n\n    V1 only - reads from Z-Wave JS cache (cheap, no Z-Wave traffic).\n    \"\"\"\n    return timedelta(minutes=2)\n```\n\nAdd `hard_refresh_interval` property:\n\n```python\n@property\ndef hard_refresh_interval(self) -> timedelta:\n    \"\"\"Return interval between hard refreshes.\n\n    V1: 30 minutes (queries each slot individually, expensive).\n    V2: 1 hour (uses checksum optimization, usually no traffic).\n    \"\"\"\n    if self._usercode_cc_version >= 2:\n        return timedelta(hours=1)\n    return timedelta(minutes=30)\n```\n\nUpdate `connection_check_interval`:\n\n```python\n@property\ndef connection_check_interval(self) -> timedelta | None:\n    \"\"\"Return interval for connection state checks.\n\n    V2 uses config entry state changes. These events carry intermediate\n    cache state and should be ignored to prevent stale data from overwriting\n    the final refresh result.\n    \"\"\"\n    lcm_entry = MockConfigEntry(\n        domain=DOMAIN,\n        data={\n            CONF_LOCKS: [zwave_js_lock_v2.lock.entity_id],\n            CONF_SLOTS: {\"1\": {}, \"2\": {}},\n        },\n    )\n    lcm_entry.add_to_hass(hass)\n    await zwave_js_lock_v2.async_setup(lcm_entry)\n\n    mock_coordinator = MagicMock()\n    mock_coordinator.data = {1: \"1111\", 2: \"2222\"}\n    zwave_js_lock_v2.coordinator = mock_coordinator\n\n    # Subscribe to push updates\n    zwave_js_lock_v2.subscribe_push_updates()\n\n    # Simulate a hard refresh that emits value-updated events mid-refresh\n    original_refresh = zwave_js_lock_v2._async_refresh_usercode_cache\n\n    async def refresh_with_event():\n        \"\"\"Simulate refresh that triggers value-updated events.\"\"\"\n        # Emit a value-updated event while refresh is in progress\n        lock_schlage_be469_v2.emit(\n            \"value updated\",\n            {\n                \"args\": {\n                    \"commandClass\": CommandClass.USER_CODE,\n                    \"property\": \"userCode\",\n                    \"propertyKey\": 1,\n                    \"newValue\": \"stale_value\",\n                },\n            },\n        )\n        await original_refresh()\n\n    with patch.object(\n        zwave_js_lock_v2,\n        \"_async_refresh_usercode_cache\",\n        side_effect=refresh_with_event,\n    ):\n        await zwave_js_lock_v2.async_hard_refresh_codes()\n\n    # The stale event should have been suppressed\n    mock_coordinator.push_update.assert_not_called()\n\n    # After refresh completes, events should work again\n    lock_schlage_be469_v2.emit(\n        \"value updated\",\n        {\n            \"args\": {\n                \"commandClass\": CommandClass.USER_CODE,\n                \"property\": \"userCode\",\n                \"propertyKey\": 1,\n                \"newValue\": \"9999\",\n            },\n        },\n    )\n    await hass.async_block_till_done()\n\n    mock_coordinator.push_update.assert_called_once_with({1: \"9999\"})\n\n    zwave_js_lock_v2.unsubscribe_push_updates()\n    await zwave_js_lock_v2.async_unload(False)\n```\n\n**Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**\n\nRun: `pytest tests/providers/test_zwave_js.py::test_push_events_suppressed_during_hard_refresh -v`\nExpected: FAIL (stale event is not suppressed)\n\n**Step 3: Implement hard refresh suppression**\n\nIn `custom_components/lock_code_manager/providers/zwave_js.py`:\n\nAdd field to the dataclass:\n\n```python\n_hard_refresh_in_progress: bool = field(init=False, default=False)\n```\n\nIn `async_hard_refresh_codes`, wrap with the flag:\n\n```python\nasync def async_hard_refresh_codes(self) -> dict[int, int | str]:\n    \"\"\"Perform hard refresh and return all codes.\n\n    Sets _hard_refresh_in_progress flag to suppress push handler events\n    during the refresh. The driver emits value-updated events as it\n    re-queries each slot, which carry intermediate cache state.\n    \"\"\"\n    self._hard_refresh_in_progress = True\n    try:\n        await self._async_refresh_usercode_cache()\n        return await self.async_get_usercodes()\n    finally:\n        self._hard_refresh_in_progress = False\n```\n\nIn `subscribe_push_updates`, add a guard at the top of `on_value_updated`:\n\n```python\n@callback\ndef on_value_updated(event: dict[str, Any]) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Handle value update events from Z-Wave JS.\"\"\"\n    if self._hard_refresh_in_progress:\n        return\n\n    # ... rest of existing handler\n```\n\n**Step 4: Run tests to verify they pass**\n\nRun: `pytest tests/providers/test_zwave_js.py -v`\nExpected: ALL PASS\n\n**Step 5: Run full test suite**\n\nRun: `pytest tests/ -v`\nExpected: ALL PASS\n\n**Step 6: Commit**\n\n```bash\ngit add custom_components/lock_code_manager/providers/zwave_js.py \\\n    tests/providers/test_zwave_js.py\ngit commit -m \"Suppress push handler events during hard refresh\n\nThe Z-Wave JS driver emits value-updated events as it re-queries each\nslot during refresh. These carry intermediate cache state and should\nbe ignored to prevent stale data overwriting the refresh result.\"\n```\n\n---\n\n### Task 4: Add TODOs for future work\n\n**Files:**\n- Modify: `TODO.md`\n\n**Step 1: Add TODO entries**\n\nUnder `## Refactors and Maintenance`, add a new section:\n\n```markdown\n### Configurable Hard Refresh Interval\n\nMake `hard_refresh_interval` a user-configurable option in the config flow.\nCurrently hardcoded to 30 minutes (V1) and 1 hour (V2).\n\n**Estimated Effort:** Low (2-4 hours)\n**Priority:** Low\n**Status:** Not started\n\n### Split Hard Refresh Between Managed and Unmanaged Slots\n\nManaged slots (those with LCM config) should be hard refreshed at the normal\ninterval (e.g., 30 min). Unmanaged slots only need occasional drift awareness\n(e.g., once a day) since they're not actively synced by LCM.\n\n**Estimated Effort:** Medium (4-8 hours)\n**Priority:** Low\n**Status:** Not started\n```\n\n**Step 2: Commit**\n\n```bash\ngit add TODO.md\ngit commit -m \"Add TODOs for configurable hard refresh and slot splitting\"\n```\n\n---\n\n### Task 5: Final verification and cleanup\n\n**Step 1: Run full test suite**\n\nRun: `pytest tests/ -v`\nExpected: ALL PASS, under 10 seconds\n\n**Step 2: Run pre-commit checks**\n\nRun: `pre-commit run --all-files`\nExpected: ALL PASS\n\n**Step 3: Fix any issues from pre-commit**\n\nIf any linting/formatting issues, fix and re-run.\n\n**Step 4: Commit any pre-commit fixes**\n\nOnly if step 3 required changes.\n"

## Tests Added

Three scenario-based regression tests were added to `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/tests/providers/test_base.py`:

### 1. `test_set_usercode_preserves_optimistic_update` (line ~641)

Verifies that after `async_internal_set_usercode` completes, a subsequent poll (`async_internal_get_usercodes`) returns the newly set value rather than stale data. This proves that no intermediate refresh overwrites the set operation's effect.

```python
await lock_provider.async_internal_set_usercode(3, "9999", "Test")
fresh_data = await lock_provider.async_internal_get_usercodes()
assert fresh_data[3] == "9999"
```

### 2. `test_clear_usercode_preserves_optimistic_update` (line ~670)

Same pattern for clear operations: sets a code on slot 4, clears it, then verifies the next poll sees the slot as cleared.

```python
await lock_provider.async_internal_set_usercode(4, "4444", "Test")
await lock_provider.async_internal_clear_usercode(4)
fresh_data = await lock_provider.async_internal_get_usercodes()
assert 4 not in fresh_data or fresh_data.get(4) == ""
```

### 3. `test_no_coordinator_refresh_between_set_and_poll` (line ~686)

The most critical test. Patches `coordinator.async_set_updated_data` with a tracking wrapper and then calls `async_internal_set_usercode`. For a poll-based provider (`MockLCMLock` with `supports_push=False`), there should be zero `async_set_updated_data` calls during the set operation -- no sneaky refresh that could read stale cache data.

```python
with patch.object(coordinator, "async_set_updated_data", track_data_updates):
    await lock_provider.async_internal_set_usercode(3, "9999", "Test")

assert data_snapshots == [], (
    f"Expected no async_set_updated_data calls during set_usercode, "
    f"but got {len(data_snapshots)} call(s): {data_snapshots}"
)
```

These three tests complement the existing `test_set_usercode_does_not_refresh_coordinator` and `test_clear_usercode_does_not_refresh_coordinator` (which verify `async_request_refresh` isn't called) by testing the end-to-end data flow consequences of that fix.

   152→    def _get_client_state(self) -> tuple[bool, str]:
   153→        """Return whether the Z-Wave JS client is ready and a retry reason."""
   154→        if self.lock_config_entry.state != ConfigEntryState.LOADED:
   155→            return False, "config entry not loaded"
   156→
   157→        runtime_data: ZwaveJSData | None = getattr(
   158→            self.lock_config_entry, "runtime_data", None
   159→        )
   160→        client: Client | None = (
   161→            getattr(runtime_data, "client", None) if runtime_data else None
   162→        )
   163→        if not client:
   164→            return False, "Z-Wave JS client not ready"
   165→
   166→        if not client.connected:
   167→            return False, "Z-Wave JS client not connected"
   168→
   169→        if client.driver is None:
   170→            return False, "Z-Wave JS driver not ready"
   171→
   172→        return True, ""

   174→    def code_slot_in_use(self, code_slot: int) -> bool | None:

   181→    def _get_slot_entity_states(self, code_slot: int) -> tuple[str, str, str] | None:
   182→        """
   183→        Get active state, PIN value, and PIN entity ID for a managed slot.
   184→
   185→        Returns tuple of (active_state, pin_value, pin_entity_id) if the slot is
   186→        managed by LCM and entities exist, None otherwise.
   187→        """
   188→        try:
   189→            config_entry = next(
   190→                entry
   191→                for entry in self.hass.config_entries.async_entries(DOMAIN)
   192→                if self.lock.entity_id in get_entry_data(entry, CONF_LOCKS, [])
   193→                and code_slot in (int(s) for s in get_entry_data(entry, CONF_SLOTS, {}))
   194→            )
   195→        except StopIteration:
   196→            return None
   197→
   198→        base_unique_id = f"{config_entry.entry_id}|{code_slot}"
   199→        active_entity_id = self.ent_reg.async_get_entity_id(
   200→            BINARY_SENSOR_DOMAIN, DOMAIN, f"{base_unique_id}|{ATTR_ACTIVE}"
   201→        )
   202→        pin_entity_id = self.ent_reg.async_get_entity_id(
   203→            TEXT_DOMAIN, DOMAIN, f"{base_unique_id}|{CONF_PIN}"
   204→        )
   205→
   206→        if not active_entity_id or not pin_entity_id:
   207→            return None
   208→
   209→        active_state = self.hass.states.get(active_entity_id)
   210→        pin_state = self.hass.states.get(pin_entity_id)
   211→
   212→        if not active_state or not pin_state:
   213→            return None
   214→
   215→        return (active_state.state, pin_state.state, pin_entity_id)

   217→    def _slot_expects_pin(self, code_slot: int) -> bool:
   218→        """
   219→        Check if LCM expects a PIN on this slot (active=ON with PIN set).
   220→
   221→        Used to ignore stale userIdStatus=AVAILABLE events from locks that report
   222→        old status after a code was successfully set.
   223→        """
   224→        states = self._get_slot_entity_states(code_slot)
   225→        if states is None:
   226→            return False
   227→
   228→        active_state, pin_value, _ = states
   229→        return active_state == STATE_ON and bool(pin_value)
   230→
   231→    def _resolve_pin_if_masked(self, value: str, code_slot: int) -> str | None:
   232→        """
   233→        Resolve a PIN value, looking up expected PIN if masked.
   234→
   235→        Some locks return masked values (all asterisks) instead of the actual PIN.
   236→        This method returns the value as-is if not masked, or looks up the expected
   237→        PIN from LCM entities if masked.
   238→
   239→        """
   240→        slot_in_use = self.code_slot_in_use(code_slot)
   241→
   242→        if value == "0" * len(value) and slot_in_use is False:
   243→            # Some locks return all zeros instead of a blank value when cleared - treat
   244→            # as unmasked cleared value
   245→            return ""
   246→
   247→        # If not masked, return as-is
   248→        if not value or not (value == "*" * len(value) and slot_in_use):
   249→            return value
   250→
   251→        # Masked - look up expected PIN from LCM entities
   252→        # Use ATTR_ACTIVE binary sensor (not CONF_ENABLED switch) to match what
   253→        # sync logic expects. ATTR_ACTIVE considers conditions, so we only resolve
   254→        # masked codes when sync expects a PIN on the lock.
   255→        states = self._get_slot_entity_states(code_slot)
   256→        if states is None:
   257→            return None
   258→
   259→        active_state, pin_value, pin_entity_id = states
   260→
   261→        if active_state == STATE_ON:
   262→            _LOGGER.debug(
   263→                "PIN is masked for lock %s code slot %s, assuming value from PIN entity %s",
   264→                self.lock.entity_id,
   265→                code_slot,
   266→                pin_entity_id,
   267→            )
   268→            return pin_value
   269→
   270→        # Fall back to returning masked value if active state is not ON (e.g. slot not
   271→        # enabled) - we don't care what the value is, just that there is one so that
   272→        # the sync logic treats this slot as having a PIN set on the lock
   273→        return value

   275→    @callback
   276→    def subscribe_push_updates(self) -> None:
   277→        """Subscribe to User Code CC value update events."""
   278→        # Idempotent - skip if already subscribed
   279→        if self._value_update_unsub is not None:
   280→            return
   281→
   282→        ready, reason = self._get_client_state()
   283→        if not ready:
   284→            _LOGGER.debug(
   285→                "Lock %s: push subscription deferred (%s)",
   286→                self.lock.entity_id,
   287→                reason,
   288→            )
   289→            self._schedule_push_retry(reason)

   292→        @callback
   293→        def on_value_updated(event: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   294→            """Handle value update events from Z-Wave JS."""
   295→            args: dict[str, Any] = event["args"]
   296→            # Filter for User Code CC - handle both userCode and userIdStatus
   297→            if args.get("commandClass") != CommandClass.USER_CODE:
   298→                return
   299→
   300→            property_name = args.get("property")
   301→            if property_name not in (
   302→                LOCK_USERCODE_PROPERTY,
   303→                LOCK_USERCODE_STATUS_PROPERTY,
   304→            ):
   305→                return
   306→
   307→            code_slot = int(args["propertyKey"])
   308→
   309→            # Slot 0 is not a valid user code slot (used for status/metadata)
   310→            if code_slot == 0:
   311→                return
   312→
   313→            # Handle userIdStatus updates - slot cleared is a fast path
   314→            if property_name == LOCK_USERCODE_STATUS_PROPERTY:
   315→                status = args.get("newValue")
   316→                if status == CodeSlotStatus.AVAILABLE:
   317→                    # Ignore AVAILABLE status if LCM expects a PIN on this slot.
   318→                    # Some locks send stale AVAILABLE events after a code was set,
   319→                    # which would cause infinite sync loops.
   320→                    if self._slot_expects_pin(code_slot):
   321→                        _LOGGER.debug(
   322→                            "Lock %s: ignoring userIdStatus=AVAILABLE for slot %s "
   323→                            "(LCM expects PIN on this slot)",
   324→                            self.lock.entity_id,
   325→                            code_slot,
   326→                        )
   327→                        return
   328→
   329→                    # Slot was cleared - update coordinator if needed
   330→                    if self.coordinator and self.coordinator.data.get(code_slot) != "":
   331→                        _LOGGER.debug(
   332→                            "Lock %s: slot %s userIdStatus=AVAILABLE, marking cleared",
   333→                            self.lock.entity_id,
   334→                            code_slot,
   335→                        )
   336→                        self.coordinator.push_update({code_slot: ""})
   337→                return
   338→
   339→            # Handle userCode updates
   340→            # newValue is the raw PIN string (or None/empty/"0000" if cleared)
   341→            new_value = args.get("newValue")
   342→            # Treat empty, None, or all-zeros as cleared
   343→            if not new_value or (
   344→                isinstance(new_value, str) and new_value.strip("0") == ""
   345→            ):
   346→                value = ""
   347→            else:
   348→                value = str(new_value)
   349→
   350→            # Resolve masked codes (all asterisks) to expected PIN
   351→            # This prevents infinite sync loops when locks return masked values
   352→            resolved = self._resolve_pin_if_masked(value, code_slot)
   353→            if resolved is None:
   354→                _LOGGER.debug(
   355→                    "Lock %s: skipping masked code update for slot %s "
   356→                    "(unable to resolve)",
   357→                    self.lock.entity_id,
   358→                    code_slot,
   359→                )
   360→                return
   361→
   362→            # Skip if value hasn't changed (Z-Wave JS sends duplicate events)
   363→            if self.coordinator and self.coordinator.data.get(code_slot) == resolved:
   364→                return
   365→
   366→            _LOGGER.debug(
   367→                "Lock %s received push update for slot %s: %s",
   368→                self.lock.entity_id,
   369→                code_slot,
   370→                "****" if resolved else "(cleared)",
   371→            )
   372→
   373→            # Push update to coordinator
   374→            if self.coordinator:
   375→                self.coordinator.push_update({code_slot: resolved})
   376→
   377→        try:
   378→            self._value_update_unsub = self.node.on("value updated", on_value_updated)
   379→        except ValueError as err:
   380→            _LOGGER.debug(
   381→                "Lock %s push subscription deferred: %s", self.lock.entity_id, err
   382→            )
   383→            self._schedule_push_retry("node not ready")
   384→
   385→    def _schedule_push_retry(self, reason: str) -> None:
   386→        """Schedule a retry for push subscription if one isn't pending."""
   387→        if self._push_retry_cancel:
   388→            return
   389→
   390→        _LOGGER.debug(
   391→            "Lock %s: scheduling push subscription retry in %ss (%s)",
   392→            self.lock.entity_id,
   393→            PUSH_SUBSCRIBE_RETRY_DELAY,
   394→            reason,
   395→        )
   396→        self._push_retry_cancel = async_call_later(
   397→            self.hass, PUSH_SUBSCRIBE_RETRY_DELAY, self._handle_push_retry
   398→        )
   399→
   400→    @callback
   401→    def _handle_push_retry(self, _now: Any) -> None:
   402→        """Retry push subscription after delay."""
   403→        if self._push_retry_cancel:
   404→            self._push_retry_cancel()
   405→            self._push_retry_cancel = None
   406→        self.subscribe_push_updates()
   407→
   408→    @callback
   409→    def unsubscribe_push_updates(self) -> None:
   410→        """Unsubscribe from value update events."""
   411→        if self._push_retry_cancel:
   412→            self._push_retry_cancel()
   413→            self._push_retry_cancel = None
   414→        if self._value_update_unsub:
   415→            self._value_update_unsub()
   416→            self._value_update_unsub = None
   417→
   418→    @callback
   419→    def _zwave_js_event_filter(self, event_data: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
   420→        """Filter out events."""
   421→        # Try to find the lock that we are getting an event for, skipping
   422→        # ones that don't match
   423→        assert self.node.client.driver
   424→        return (
   425→            event_data[ATTR_HOME_ID] == self.node.client.driver.controller.home_id
   426→            and event_data[ATTR_NODE_ID] == self.node.node_id
   427→            and event_data[ATTR_DEVICE_ID] == self.lock.device_id
   428→        )
   429→
   430→    @callback
   431→    def _handle_zwave_js_event(self, evt: Event) -> None:
   432→        """Handle Z-Wave JS event."""
   433→        if evt.data[ATTR_TYPE] != NotificationType.ACCESS_CONTROL:
   434→            _LOGGER.debug(
   435→                "Lock %s received non Access Control event: %s",
   436→                self.lock.entity_id,
   437→                evt.as_dict(),
   438→            )
   439→            return
   440→
   441→        params = evt.data.get(ATTR_PARAMETERS) or {}
   442→        code_slot = params.get("userId", 0)
   443→        self.async_fire_code_slot_event(
   444→            code_slot=code_slot,
   445→            to_locked=next(
   446→                (
   447→                    to_locked
   448→                    for to_locked, codes in ACCESS_CONTROL_NOTIFICATION_TO_LOCKED.items()
   449→                    if evt.data[ATTR_EVENT] in codes
   450→                ),
   451→                None,
   452→            ),
   453→            action_text=evt.data.get(ATTR_EVENT_LABEL),
   454→            source_data=evt,
   455→        )
   456→
   457→    @property
   458→    def domain(self) -> str:
   459→        """Return integration domain."""
   460→        return ZWAVE_JS_DOMAIN
   461→
   462→    async def async_setup(self, config_entry: ConfigEntry) -> None:
   463→        """Set up lock."""
   464→        await super().async_setup(config_entry)
   465→        self._listeners.append(
   466→            self.hass.bus.async_listen(
   467→                ZWAVE_JS_NOTIFICATION_EVENT,
   468→                self._handle_zwave_js_event,
   469→                self._zwave_js_event_filter,
   470→            )
   471→        )
   472→
   473→    async def async_unload(self, remove_permanently: bool) -> None:
   474→        """Unload lock."""
   475→        for listener in self._listeners:
   476→            listener()
   477→        self._listeners.clear()
   478→        # Always clean up push subscriptions regardless of supports_push,
   479→        # in case subscribe_push_updates() was called explicitly.
   480→        self.unsubscribe_push_updates()
   481→        await super().async_unload(remove_permanently)
   482→
   483→    async def async_is_connection_up(self) -> bool:
   484→        """Return whether connection to lock is up."""
   485→        ready, _reason = self._get_client_state()
   486→        return ready
   487→
   488→    async def async_hard_refresh_codes(self) -> dict[int, int | str]:
   489→        """
   490→        Perform hard refresh and return all codes.
   491→
   492→        Uses Z-Wave JS's refresh_cc_values which handles checksum optimization
   493→        internally - it will skip re-fetching codes if the checksum hasn't changed.
   494→        Returns codes in the same format as async_get_usercodes().
   495→        """
   496→        await self._async_refresh_usercode_cache()
   497→        return await self.async_get_usercodes()
   498→
   499→    async def async_set_usercode(
   500→        self, code_slot: int, usercode: int | str, name: str | None = None
   501→    ) -> bool:
   502→        """
   503→        Set a usercode on a code slot.
   504→
   505→        Returns True if the value was changed, False if already set to this value.
   506→        """
   507→        # Check if the code is already set to this value (avoid unnecessary network call)
   508→        usercode = str(usercode)
   509→        try:
   510→            if (current := get_usercode(self.node, code_slot)).get("in_use"):
   511→                current_code = str(current.get("usercode", ""))
   512→                # Resolve masked codes and compare
   513→                if usercode == self._resolve_pin_if_masked(current_code, code_slot):
   514→                    _LOGGER.debug(
   515→                        "Lock %s slot %s already has this PIN, skipping set",
   516→                        self.lock.entity_id,
   517→                        code_slot,
   518→                    )
   519→                    return False
   520→        except Exception:
   521→            # If we can't check the cache, proceed with the set
   522→            pass
   523→
   524→        service_data = {
   525→            ATTR_ENTITY_ID: self.lock.entity_id,
   526→            ATTR_CODE_SLOT: code_slot,
   527→            ATTR_USERCODE: usercode,
   528→        }
   529→        await self.async_call_service(
   530→            ZWAVE_JS_DOMAIN, SERVICE_SET_LOCK_USERCODE, service_data
   531→        )
   532→        # Optimistic update: Z-Wave command succeeded (lock acknowledged), but the
   533→        # value cache updates asynchronously via push notification. Update coordinator
   534→        # immediately to prevent sync loops from reading stale cache data.
   535→        if self.coordinator:
   536→            self.coordinator.push_update({code_slot: usercode})
   537→        return True
   538→
   539→    async def async_clear_usercode(self, code_slot: int) -> bool:
   540→        """
   541→        Clear a usercode on a code slot.
   542→
   543→        Returns True if the value was changed, False if already cleared.
   544→        """
   545→        # Check if the slot is already cleared (avoid unnecessary network call)
   546→        try:
   547→            current = get_usercode(self.node, code_slot)
   548→            if not current.get("in_use"):
   549→                _LOGGER.debug(
   550→                    "Lock %s slot %s already cleared, skipping clear",
   551→                    self.lock.entity_id,
   552→                    code_slot,
   553→                )
   554→                return False
   555→        except Exception:
   556→            # If we can't check the cache, proceed with the clear
   557→            pass
   558→
   559→        service_data = {
   560→            ATTR_ENTITY_ID: self.lock.entity_id,
   561→            ATTR_CODE_SLOT: code_slot,
   562→        }
   563→        await self.async_call_service(
   564→            ZWAVE_JS_DOMAIN, SERVICE_CLEAR_LOCK_USERCODE, service_data
   565→        )
   566→        # Optimistic update: Z-Wave command succeeded (lock acknowledged), but the
   567→        # value cache updates asynchronously via push notification. Update coordinator
   568→        # immediately to prevent sync loops from reading stale cache data.
   569→        if self.coordinator:
   570→            self.coordinator.push_update({code_slot: ""})
   571→        return True
   572→
   573→    def _get_usercodes_from_cache(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   574→        """Get usercodes from Z-Wave JS value DB cache."""
   575→        try:
   576→            return list(get_usercodes(self.node) or [])
   577→        except Exception as err:
   578→            raise LockDisconnected from err
   579→
   580→    async def _async_refresh_usercode_cache(self) -> None:
   581→        """Refresh usercode cache from the device."""
   582→        try:
   583→            await self.node.async_refresh_cc_values(CommandClass.USER_CODE)
   584→        except Exception as err:
   585→            raise LockDisconnected from err
   586→
   587→    async def async_get_usercodes(self) -> dict[int, int | str]:
   588→        """Get dictionary of code slots and usercodes."""
   589→        code_slots = {
   590→            int(code_slot)
   591→            for entry in self.hass.config_entries.async_entries(DOMAIN)
   592→            for code_slot in get_entry_data(entry, CONF_SLOTS, {})
   593→            if self.lock.entity_id in get_entry_data(entry, CONF_LOCKS, [])
   594→        }
   595→        data: dict[int, int | str] = {}
   596→
   597→        if not await self.async_is_connection_up():
   598→            raise LockDisconnected
   599→
   600→        slots = self._get_usercodes_from_cache()
   601→        slots_by_num = {int(slot["code_slot"]): slot for slot in slots}
   602→
   603→        # If any configured slot is missing or has unknown state, do one hard
   604→        # refresh to populate the cache. This is more efficient than fetching
   605→        # individual slots and uses Z-Wave JS's checksum optimization.
   606→        # Note: We call _async_refresh_usercode_cache directly here to avoid
   607→        # recursion since async_hard_refresh_codes calls async_get_usercodes.
   608→        if any(
   609→            slot_num not in slots_by_num or slots_by_num[slot_num].get("in_use") is None
   610→            for slot_num in code_slots
   611→        ):
   612→            _LOGGER.debug(
   613→                "Lock %s has missing/unknown slots, performing hard refresh",
   614→                self.lock.entity_id,
   615→            )
   616→            await self._async_refresh_usercode_cache()
   617→            slots = self._get_usercodes_from_cache()
   618→            slots_by_num = {int(slot["code_slot"]): slot for slot in slots}
   619→
   620→        for slot in slots:
   621→            code_slot = int(slot["code_slot"])
   622→            usercode: str = slot["usercode"] or ""
   623→            in_use: bool | None = slot["in_use"]
   624→
   625→            if not in_use:
   626→                data[code_slot] = ""
   627→            # Resolve PIN (handles masked codes), skip if unresolvable
   628→            elif resolved := self._resolve_pin_if_masked(usercode, code_slot):
   629→                data[code_slot] = resolved
   630→
   631→        slots_with_pin = [s for s, v in data.items() if v]
   632→        slots_not_enabled = [s for s, v in data.items() if not v]
   633→        _LOGGER.debug(
   634→            "Lock %s: %s slots with PIN %s, %s slots not enabled %s",
   635→            self.lock.entity_id,
   636→            len(slots_with_pin),
   637→            slots_with_pin,
   638→            len(slots_not_enabled),
   639→            slots_not_enabled,
   640→        )
   641→        return data
   642→

   273→) -> None:
   274→    """Test that set_usercode returns False when masked code resolves to same PIN.
   275→
   276→    Some locks (like Yale) return masked PINs (****) instead of actual codes.
   277→    When the masked code resolves to the same PIN we're trying to set, we should
   278→    skip the set operation to prevent battery drain from repeated writes.
   279→    """
   280→    lcm_entry = MockConfigEntry(
   281→        domain=DOMAIN,
   282→        data={
   283→            CONF_LOCKS: [zwave_js_lock.lock.entity_id],

   289→
   290→    # Mock the cache to return a masked code
   291→    masked_slot = {"code_slot": 2, "usercode": "****", "in_use": True}
   292→
   293→    with (
   294→        patch(
   295→            "custom_components.lock_code_manager.providers.zwave_js.get_usercode",
   296→            return_value=masked_slot,
   297→        ),
   298→        patch.object(
   299→            zwave_js_lock, "_resolve_pin_if_masked", return_value="5678"
   300→        ) as mock_resolve,
   301→        patch.object(
   302→            zwave_js_lock, "async_call_service", new_callable=AsyncMock
   303→        ) as mock_service,
   304→    ):
   305→        # Try to set the same PIN that the masked code resolves to
   306→        result = await zwave_js_lock.async_set_usercode(2, "5678", "Test User")
   307→
   308→        # Should skip the set operation

   310→        mock_resolve.assert_called_once_with("****", 2)
   311→        mock_service.assert_not_called()

   313→    await zwave_js_lock.async_unload(False)

   452→async def test_set_usercode_optimistic_update(
   453→    hass: HomeAssistant,
   454→    zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock,
   455→    zwave_integration: MockConfigEntry,
   456→) -> None:
   457→    """Test that set_usercode performs optimistic coordinator update.
   458→
   459→    When a set operation succeeds, the coordinator should be updated immediately
   460→    with the new value. This prevents sync loops where the binary sensor reads
   461→    stale cached data and triggers repeated sync attempts.
   462→
   463→    The Z-Wave command is acknowledged by the lock (via Supervision CC), but
   464→    the JS value cache updates asynchronously via push notifications. Without
   465→    the optimistic update, there's a race condition where coordinator refresh
   466→    reads stale cache data.
   467→    """
   468→    lcm_entry = MockConfigEntry(domain=DOMAIN, data={CONF_LOCKS: [], CONF_SLOTS: {}})
   469→    lcm_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
   470→    await zwave_js_lock.async_setup(lcm_entry)
   471→
   472→    # Set up a mock coordinator with stale data (simulating the race condition)
   473→    mock_coordinator = MagicMock()
   474→    mock_coordinator.data = {4: ""}  # Slot appears empty in stale cache
   475→    zwave_js_lock.coordinator = mock_coordinator
   476→
   477→    with patch.object(zwave_js_lock, "async_call_service", new_callable=AsyncMock):
   478→        result = await zwave_js_lock.async_set_usercode(4, "5678", "Test User")
   479→
   480→        assert result is True
   481→        # Verify optimistic update was called with new PIN
   482→        mock_coordinator.push_update.assert_called_once_with({4: "5678"})
   483→
   484→    await zwave_js_lock.async_unload(False)
   485→
   486→
   487→async def test_set_usercode_optimistic_update_prevents_stale_read(
   488→    hass: HomeAssistant,
   489→    zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock,
   490→    zwave_integration: MockConfigEntry,
   491→) -> None:
   492→    """Test that optimistic update prevents sync loops from stale cache reads.
   493→
   494→    This test verifies the fix for the reported issue where out-of-sync slots
   495→    cause constant lock activity. The scenario:
   496→    1. LCM sets a code on the lock
   497→    2. Z-Wave command succeeds (lock acknowledges)
   498→    3. Without optimistic update: coordinator.data still has old value
   499→    4. Binary sensor sees mismatch → triggers another sync → loop
   500→
   501→    With the fix, push_update immediately sets coordinator.data to the new value,
   502→    so the binary sensor sees the expected value and doesn't retry.
   503→    """
   504→    lcm_entry = MockConfigEntry(domain=DOMAIN, data={CONF_LOCKS: [], CONF_SLOTS: {}})
   505→    lcm_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
   506→    await zwave_js_lock.async_setup(lcm_entry)
   507→
   508→    # Simulate stale cache: coordinator thinks slot is empty
   509→    mock_coordinator = MagicMock()
   510→    mock_coordinator.data = {4: ""}
   511→    zwave_js_lock.coordinator = mock_coordinator
   512→
   513→    with patch.object(zwave_js_lock, "async_call_service", new_callable=AsyncMock):
   514→        await zwave_js_lock.async_set_usercode(4, "9999")
   515→
   516→        # The optimistic update should have been called
   517→        mock_coordinator.push_update.assert_called_once_with({4: "9999"})
   518→
   519→        # Simulate what push_update does - update coordinator data
   520→        # (In real code, push_update calls async_set_updated_data which does this)
   521→        mock_coordinator.data[4] = "9999"
   522→
   523→        # Now coordinator.data reflects the expected value
   524→        # Binary sensor would see coordinator.data[4] == "9999" == pin_state
   525→        # → expected_in_sync = True → no retry loop
   526→        assert mock_coordinator.data[4] == "9999"
   527→
   528→    await zwave_js_lock.async_unload(False)
   529→
   530→

   764→def async_capture_events(
   765→    hass: HomeAssistant, event_name: str
   766→) -> list[Event[dict[str, Any]]]:
   767→    """Create a helper that captures events."""
   768→    events: list[Event[dict[str, Any]]] = []
   769→
   770→    @callback
   771→    def capture_events(event: Event[dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
   772→        events.append(event)
   773→
   774→    hass.bus.async_listen(event_name, capture_events)
   775→    return events

   870→async def test_get_usercodes_masked_pin_unmanaged_slot_returns_masked_value(
   871→    hass: HomeAssistant,
   872→    zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock,
   873→    zwave_integration: MockConfigEntry,
   874→) -> None:
   875→    """Test mixed slots: managed with real code vs unmanaged with masked code.
   876→
   877→    This test verifies behavior when the lock cache contains:
   878→    - Slot 1: Managed by LCM, has real code "9999" -> should be returned
   879→    - Slot 5: NOT managed by LCM, has masked code "****" -> returns masked value
   880→
   881→    Unmanaged slots with masked PINs return the masked value so sync logic
   882→    knows a PIN exists on the lock, even if we can't resolve the actual value.
   883→    """
   884→    # Configure LCM to only manage slot 1 (not slot 5)
   885→    lcm_entry = MockConfigEntry(
   886→        domain=DOMAIN,
   887→        data={
   888→            CONF_LOCKS: [zwave_js_lock.lock.entity_id],
   889→            CONF_SLOTS: {"1": {}},  # Only slot 1 is managed
   890→        },
   891→    )
   892→    lcm_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
   893→    await zwave_js_lock.async_setup(lcm_entry)
   894→
   895→    # Mock the cache to include a slot with a masked PIN that isn't managed by LCM
   896→    masked_slots = [
   897→        {"code_slot": 1, "usercode": "9999", "in_use": True},  # Managed by LCM
   898→        {"code_slot": 5, "usercode": "****", "in_use": True},  # NOT managed, masked
   899→    ]
   900→
   901→    with (
   902→        patch.object(
   903→            zwave_js_lock, "_get_usercodes_from_cache", return_value=masked_slots
   904→        ),
   905→        # Slot 5 not in Z-Wave node data, so code_slot_in_use returns None
   906→        patch.object(
   907→            zwave_js_lock,
   908→            "code_slot_in_use",
   909→            side_effect=lambda s: True if s == 1 else None,
   910→        ),
   911→    ):
   912→        codes = await zwave_js_lock.async_get_usercodes()
   913→
   914→        # Slot 1 should have its code
   915→        assert codes[1] == "9999"
   916→        # Slot 5 returns masked value (so sync logic knows a PIN exists)
   917→        assert codes[5] == "****"
   918→
   919→    await zwave_js_lock.async_unload(False)
   920→
   921→

  1000→async def test_resolve_pin_if_masked_detection(zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock) -> None:
  1001→    """Test _resolve_pin_if_masked returns value as-is when not masked."""
  1002→    # Not masked - returns value as-is
  1003→    assert zwave_js_lock._resolve_pin_if_masked("1234", 1) == "1234"
  1004→    assert zwave_js_lock._resolve_pin_if_masked("5678", 2) == "5678"
  1005→    assert zwave_js_lock._resolve_pin_if_masked("", 1) == ""
  1006→    # Partially masked - returns as-is (not all asterisks)
  1007→    assert zwave_js_lock._resolve_pin_if_masked("***1", 1) == "***1"
  1008→    assert zwave_js_lock._resolve_pin_if_masked("1***", 1) == "1***"
  1009→
