     5→This repository holds the Z-Wave JS driver library, a TypeScript implementation of a Z-Wave controller software stack and supporting tools.
     6→
     7→## Project structure
     8→
     9→- The `packages/` directory contains all of the packages in this monorepo.
    10→  - `packages/zwave-js`: The main driver library (name: `zwave-js`)
    11→  - `packages/shared`: Internal utilities shared between packages (name: `@zwave-js/shared`)
    12→  - `packages/core`: Core definitions, utilities and types used by other packages and applications (name: `@zwave-js/core`)
    13→  - `packages/cc`: Command Class definitions and implementations (name: `@zwave-js/cc`)
    14→  - `packages/config`: Functionality related to device configuration and all configuration files (name: `@zwave-js/config`)
    15→  - `packages/eslint-plugin`: A custom ESLint plugin, used internally throughout the project (name: `@zwave-js/eslint-plugin`)
    16→  - `packages/flash`: Command-line based Z-Wave firmware flashing tool (name: `@zwave-js/flash`)
    17→  - `packages/host`: Host abstractions layer for integration tests (name: `@zwave-js/host`)
    18→  - `packages/nvmedit`: Utilities and a command-line tool for editing the contents of Z-Wave controller memory/NVM (name: `@zwave-js/nvmedit`)
    19→  - `packages/serial`: Serial port abstraction and Serial API message implementation (name: `@zwave-js/serial`)
    20→  - `packages/testing`: Utilities for testing (name: `@zwave-js/testing`)
    21→  - `packages/transformers`: Plugins for the TypeScript compiler used to auto-generate code at build time (name: `@zwave-js/transformers`)
    22→- Device configuration files are located in `packages/config/config/devices` and have a `.json` extension.
    23→
    24→## Tools and Tasks
    25→
    26→- Build the entire project: `yarn build`
    27→- Build a specific package: `yarn build <package-name>`, e.g. `yarn build zwave-js` or `yarn build @zwave-js/cc`
    28→- Run tests: `yarn test:ts`
    29→- Run tests for a specific file: `yarn test:ts <file>`
    30→- Format all code: `yarn fmt`
    31→- Check configuration files for semantic errors: `yarn lint:zwave`
    32→- Detect and fix linting issues in TypeScript code: `yarn lint:ts:fix`
    33→- Prefer built-in tools for finding files (e.g. `Grep`) over shell commands like `find`, `ls`, `grep`, `xargs`, to ensure cross-platform compatibility.
    34→
    35→## Common Guidelines
    36→
    37→- All code and comments and other text are written in American English
    38→- Follow existing code style patterns as much as possible
    39→- Prefer `async`/`await` over callbacks and Promises wherever possible
    40→- After making code changes, always run `yarn fmt` to fix the formatting
    41→- Do not preserve backwards compatibility (e.g., keeping unused methods, re-exporting removed types, renaming to `_unused`) unless explicitly asked. When refactoring or iterating on new features, remove unused code completely.
    42→- In comments, never mention things you replaced or removed
    43→
    44→## Commenting Style
    45→
    46→Comments should explain the WHY, not the WHAT. The code itself shows what happens; comments should explain why that approach was chosen or what it achieves in context.
    47→
    48→**When to write comments:**
    49→
    50→- Non-obvious algorithmic decisions or workarounds
    51→- Protocol-specific behavior or constraints (e.g., "These fields are only available for Z-Wave LR")
    52→- References to specifications (e.g., "Implementation based on SDS13782")
    53→- Edge cases, gotchas, or assumptions that aren't evident from code
    54→- Complex conditional logic where the reasoning matters
    55→
    56→**When NOT to write comments:**
    57→
    58→- Self-explanatory code (prefer clear naming over comments)
    59→- Describing what the next line does
    60→- Documenting parameters or types (use JSDoc for public APIs instead)
    61→- Basic control flow or straightforward operations
    62→
    63→**Good comment examples:**
    64→
    65→```typescript
    66→// When requesting a non-existing parameter, a node SHOULD respond with the
    67→// first available parameter. We use this for the first param only,
    68→// because delayed responses might otherwise confuse the interview process
    69→allowUnexpectedResponse: param === 1,
    70→
    71→// For multicast and broadcast CCs, just use the highest implemented version to serialize
    72→// Older nodes will ignore the additional fields
    73→if (typeof cc.nodeId !== "number") {
    74→```
    75→
    76→**Avoid comments like:**
    77→
    78→```typescript
    79→// Set the value to 5
    80→const timeout = 5;
    81→
    82→// Check if the node is awake
    83→if (node.isAwake) {
    84→```
    85→
    86→Keep comments concise (1-3 sentences), use professional technical tone, and assume the reader understands Z-Wave domain terminology.
    87→
    88→## Testing
    89→
    90→- Use `vitest` for testing.
    91→- Unit tests must be located next to the code they test, but with a `.test.ts` extension instead of `.ts`.
    92→- Do not create tests for functionality that interacts with (mock) devices, unless specifically instructed to do so.
    93→- Do not create tests when you are assigned a Github issue to fix, unless specifically instructed to do so.
    94→
    95→## Reviewing Pull Requests
    96→
    97→The rules to apply for reviewing pull requests depend on which files were changed:
    98→
    99→- If the PR changes device configuration files (`*.json` files in `packages/config/config/devices`), follow the [review-config-pr](prompts/review-config-pr.prompt.md) prompt to review the changes.

> AGENT

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
There are two ways to get CC version:
1. **`node.command_classes`** (sync, cached) — iterates local `CommandClassInfo` list, no network call
2. **`node.async_get_cc_version(cc)`** (async, network) — sends a command to the Z-Wave JS server

Our current approach using `node.command_classes` is already the simpler one — it's synchronous and reads from cached data. The async `get_cc_version` makes an unnecessary server roundtrip.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

The current implementation could be slightly more concise with `next()`:

```python
return next(
    (cc.version for cc in self.node.command_classes if cc.id == CommandClass.USER_CODE),
    1,
)
```

But it's the same logic. There's no simpler built-in helper in the library — `node.command_classes` is the canonical way to access CC metadata locally.

Let me also check if HA core's zwave_js integration has any CC version helper we could reuse.

    56→#### Clarify Config Entry Data vs Options Usage
    57→
    58→Document and standardize when to read from `config_entry.data` vs
    59→`config_entry.options`. Current understanding: prefer `options` only within the
    60→config entry update listener during options updates; elsewhere use `data` to
    61→avoid mid-update inconsistencies. Add helper(s) or guidance to reduce ambiguity
    62→and prevent regressions.

    74→
    75→#### Move Sync Logic to Coordinator
    76→
    77→**Current Architecture Issues:**
    78→
    79→- In-sync binary sensor reads PIN config from text entities via
    80→  `_get_entity_state()`
    81→- Reads lock state from coordinator data
    82→- Compares them and triggers sync operations (set_usercode/clear_usercode)
    83→- Cross-entity dependencies create race conditions during startup
    84→- Current guard uses `_attr_is_on is None` to avoid initial sync operations
    85→
    86→**Proposed Solution:**
    87→Move sync logic entirely into the coordinator:
    88→
    89→- Coordinator already has access to both desired state (from config) and actual
    90→  state (from lock)
    91→- Coordinator performs sync operations during its `_async_update_data()` cycle
    92→- Binary sensor becomes read-only, just displays coordinator's computed in-sync
    93→  status
    94→- Text/number/switch entities remain as config views
    95→
    96→**Example Implementation:**
    97→
    98→```python
    99→# In coordinator._async_update_data()
   100→actual_code = await self.provider.get_usercodes()
   101→desired_code = self.config_entry.data[slot]["pin"]
   102→
   103→if actual_code != desired_code and slot_enabled:
   104→    await self.provider.set_usercode(slot, desired_code)
   105→
   106→return {"in_sync": actual_code == desired_code, "actual_code": actual_code}
   107→```
   108→
   109→**Benefits:**
   110→
   111→- Eliminates cross-entity state reading
   112→- Removes `_initial_state_loaded` flag and startup detection logic
   113→- No race conditions during startup
   114→- Simpler, more centralized sync logic
   115→- Coordinator is single source of truth
   116→
   117→**Considerations:**
   118→
   119→- Major architectural change
   120→- Would need to update binary sensor to be read-only
   121→- Config updates still flow through text/switch entities
   122→- Need to ensure coordinator runs sync on config changes
   123→
   124→**Estimated Effort:** High (16-24 hours)
   125→**Priority:** Medium
   126→**Status:** Not started
   127→
   128→### Convert Config and Internal Dicts to Dataclasses
   129→
   130→Convert config entry data to typed dataclasses with `from_dict`/`from_entry`
   131→class methods. Use object instances internally instead of iterating through raw
   132→config dicts. Audit codebase for other complex dicts that would benefit from
   133→dataclass conversion (e.g., slot data, lock state, coordinator data). This
   134→improves type safety, IDE autocompletion, and code readability.
   135→
   136→**Why not Voluptuous?** Voluptuous is for validation, not object instantiation.
   137→Other options like `dacite` or Pydantic add dependencies.
   138→
   139→**Example implementation:**
   140→
   141→```python
   142→@dataclass
   143→class SlotConfig:
   144→    name: str
   145→    pin: str
   146→    enabled: bool = True
   147→    calendar: str | None = None
   148→    number_of_uses: int | None = None
   149→
   150→    @classmethod
   151→    def from_dict(cls, data: dict) -> SlotConfig:
   152→        return cls(
   153→            name=data[CONF_NAME],
   154→            pin=data[CONF_PIN],
   155→            enabled=data.get(CONF_ENABLED, True),
   156→            calendar=data.get(CONF_CALENDAR),
   157→            number_of_uses=data.get(CONF_NUMBER_OF_USES),
   158→        )
   159→
   160→@dataclass
   161→class LCMConfig:
   162→    locks: list[str]
   163→    slots: dict[int, SlotConfig]
   164→
   165→    @classmethod
   166→    def from_entry(cls, entry: ConfigEntry) -> LCMConfig:
   167→        return cls(
   168→            locks=get_entry_data(entry, CONF_LOCKS, []),
   169→            slots={
   170→                int(k): SlotConfig.from_dict(v)
   171→                for k, v in get_entry_data(entry, CONF_SLOTS, {}).items()
   172→            },
   173→        )
   174→```
   175→
   176→**Places to audit for dict-to-dataclass conversion:**
   177→
   178→- `config_entry.data` / `config_entry.options` access patterns
   179→- `get_entry_data()` / `get_slot_data()` return values
   180→- Coordinator `self.data` structure
   181→- Lock provider internal state
   182→
   183→### Handle Disabled Lock Slots
   184→
   185→**Context:** Z-Wave locks have `userIdStatus` which can be `Enabled`, `Available`,
   186→or `Disabled`. Currently the coordinator only stores the code value, not the status.
   187→
   188→**Investigation Needed:**
   189→
   190→1. Test what happens when LCM tries to set a user code on a slot with
   191→   `userIdStatus=Disabled`
   192→2. Determine if we need to explicitly enable the slot before setting a code
   193→3. Check if different lock brands handle disabled slots differently
   194→
   195→**Related:** See "Enhance Coordinator Data Model" below.
   196→
   197→**Estimated Effort:** Medium (4-8 hours)
   198→**Priority:** Medium
   199→**Status:** Not started
   200→
   201→### Enhance Coordinator Data Model with Slot Status
   202→
   203→**Current State:** Coordinator stores `{slot: code}` mapping only.
   204→
   205→**Proposed Change:** Store `{slot: {code, status}}` where status is a generic
   206→LCM enum that providers map to.
   207→
   208→**Generic Status Enum:**
   209→
   210→```python
   211→class SlotStatus(StrEnum):
   212→    ENABLED = "enabled"    # Slot has active code
   213→    AVAILABLE = "available"  # Slot can be used but is empty
   214→    DISABLED = "disabled"  # Slot cannot be used (locked out)
   215→```
   216→
   217→**Provider Mapping:**
   218→
   219→- Z-Wave JS: Maps `userIdStatus` (Enabled/Available/Disabled) → `SlotStatus`
   220→- Other providers: Map their equivalent states to the generic enum
   221→
   222→**Benefits:**
   223→
   224→- Frontend can distinguish between "slot is empty" vs "slot is disabled"
   225→- Better handling of disabled slots in sync logic
   226→- More accurate representation of lock state
   227→- Provider-agnostic data model
   228→
   229→**Implementation:**
   230→
   231→1. Define `SlotStatus` enum in `const.py`
   232→2. Update Z-Wave JS provider to track userIdStatus and map to `SlotStatus`
   233→   (currently filtered out in `on_value_updated`)
   234→3. Change coordinator data schema from `dict[int, str]` to
   235→   `dict[int, SlotData]` where `SlotData` includes code and status
   236→4. Update all consumers of coordinator data (binary_sensor, sensor, websocket)
   237→5. Update frontend types and rendering
   238→
   239→**Estimated Effort:** High (12-16 hours)
   240→**Priority:** Medium
   241→**Status:** Not started
   242→
   243→### Add Optional Flags to `get_config_entry_data` Websocket Command
   244→
   245→**Context:** PR #787 consolidated multiple websocket commands into a single
   246→`get_config_entry_data` command that returns `{config_entry, entities, locks, slots}`.
   247→However, not all callers need all the data:
   248→
   249→| Caller | config_entry | entities | locks | slots |
   250→| ------ | ------------ | -------- | ----- | ----- |
   251→| `view-strategy.ts` | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |
   252→| `generate-view.ts` | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
   253→| `slot-section-strategy.ts` (legacy) | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ |
   254→| `dashboard-strategy.ts` | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ |
   255→| `lock-codes-card-editor.ts` | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ |
   256→
   257→**Cost Analysis:**
   258→
   259→- `config_entry` - Very cheap (just `config_entry.as_json_fragment`)
   260→- `slots` - Very cheap (extracts calendar IDs from config)
   261→- `locks` - Moderate (iterates locks, gets friendly names via state lookups)
   262→- `entities` - Most expensive (queries entity registry, maps to `as_partial_dict`)
   263→
   264→**Proposed Change:** Add optional `include_entities` and `include_locks` flags
   265→(default `True` for backwards compatibility). Skip `config_entry` and `slots`
   266→flags since they're essentially free.
   267→
   268→```python
   269→vol.Optional("include_entities", default=True): bool,
   270→vol.Optional("include_locks", default=True): bool,
   271→```
   272→
   273→**Benefits:**
   274→
   275→- `view-strategy.ts` can skip both entities and locks
   276→- `dashboard-strategy.ts` and `lock-codes-card-editor.ts` can skip entities
   277→- Legacy `slot-section-strategy.ts` can skip locks
   278→
   279→**Estimated Effort:** Low (2-4 hours)
   280→**Priority:** Low
   281→**Status:** Not started
   282→
   283→### Entity Registry Change Detection
   284→
   285→Track entity registry updates and warn if LCM entities change entity IDs (reload
   286→required).
   287→
   288→### Add Provider Diagnostic Data Method
   289→
   290→Add `get_diagnostic_data()` method to `BaseLock` for exposing provider-specific
   291→diagnostic information. Keymaster has this pattern with `get_platform_data()`.
   292→
   293→**Example Implementation:**
   294→
   295→```python
   296→# In BaseLock
   297→def get_diagnostic_data(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
   298→    """Return provider-specific diagnostic data."""
   299→    return {}
   300→
   301→# In ZWaveJSLock
   302→def get_diagnostic_data(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
   303→    return {
   304→        "node_id": self.node.node_id,
   305→        "home_id": self.node.client.driver.controller.home_id,
   306→        "client_connected": self.node.client.connected,
   307→        "config_entry_state": self.lock_config_entry.state.value,
   308→    }
   309→```
   310→
   311→**Benefits:**
   312→
   313→- Easier troubleshooting of provider-specific issues
   314→- Can be exposed via diagnostics platform or websocket
   315→
   316→**Estimated Effort:** Low (2-4 hours)
   317→**Priority:** Low
   318→**Status:** Not started
   319→
   320→### Drift Detection Failure Alerting
   321→
   322→Add mechanism to alert users when drift detection consistently fails over
   323→extended periods (e.g., lock offline). Currently failures are logged but there is
   324→no visibility to users or entities.
   325→
   326→### Configurable Hard Refresh Interval
   327→
   328→Make `hard_refresh_interval` a user-configurable option in the config flow.
   329→Currently hardcoded to 30 minutes (V1) and 1 hour (V2).
   330→
   331→**Estimated Effort:** Low (2-4 hours)
   332→**Priority:** Low
   333→**Status:** Not started
   334→
   335→### Split Hard Refresh Between Managed and Unmanaged Slots
   336→
   337→Managed slots (those with LCM config) should be hard refreshed at the normal
   338→interval (e.g., 30 min). Unmanaged slots only need occasional drift awareness
   339→(e.g., once a day) since they're not actively synced by LCM.
   340→
   341→**Estimated Effort:** Medium (4-8 hours)
   342→**Priority:** Low
   343→**Status:** Not started
   344→
   345→## Features
   346→
   347→### Add Schedule and Entity Condition Types
   348→
   349→**Problem:** Users report that managing calendars in HA is too painful for simple
   350→recurring schedules. Calendars are overkill for "weekdays 9-5" patterns.
   351→
   352→**Proposed Solution:** Add alternative condition types alongside `calendar`:
   353→
   354→| Condition Type | Use Case |
   355→| -------------- | -------- |
   356→| `calendar` | One-time events, external calendar sync (existing) |
   357→| `schedule` | Recurring weekly patterns via HA schedule helper |
   358→| `entity` | Custom logic via any binary sensor/input_boolean |
   359→
   360→**Implementation:**
   361→
   362→1. **Config Flow Changes:**
   363→   - Add condition type selector (calendar/schedule/entity)
   364→   - Show appropriate entity selector based on type
   365→   - `schedule`: EntitySelector filtered to `schedule` domain
   366→   - `entity`: EntitySelector filtered to `binary_sensor`, `input_boolean`
   367→
   368→2. **Binary Sensor Changes:**
   369→   - Update `_get_entity_state()` to handle different condition types
   370→   - Schedule entities: check if current time is within schedule (state = "on")
   371→   - Entity conditions: directly use entity state
   372→
   373→3. **Slot Data Model:**
   374→   - Add `condition_type` field: `calendar | schedule | entity`
   375→   - Add `condition_entity` field (alternative to `calendar`)
   376→   - Maintain backward compatibility with existing `calendar` field
   377→
   378→4. **Frontend Updates:**
   379→   - Update slot card to show condition type
   380→   - Show appropriate icon/label for each type
   381→
   382→**Benefits:**
   383→
   384→- Schedule helper is much simpler for recurring patterns
   385→- Entity condition allows maximum flexibility (templates, automations)
   386→- Calendar remains available for complex/one-time events
   387→
   388→**Estimated Effort:** Medium (8-12 hours)
   389→**Priority:** Medium-High
   390→**Status:** Not started
   391→
   392→### Advanced Calendar Configuration
   393→
   394→**Feature Request:** Allow slot number and PIN to be configured directly in
   395→calendar event metadata, eliminating need for separate slot configuration.
   396→
   397→**Design Considerations:**
   398→
   399→**Current Behavior:**
   400→
   401→- Slot configured in config flow with fixed PIN
   402→- Calendar event (when present) only controls whether slot is active/inactive
   403→- PIN and slot number are static configuration
   404→
   405→**Proposed Behavior:**
   406→
   407→- Calendar event contains slot number and PIN in its metadata
   408→- User configures regex/pattern to extract slot number and PIN from:
   409→  - Event title (e.g., "Slot 3: 1234")
   410→  - Event description
   411→  - Event location
   412→  - Custom calendar properties
   413→
   414→**Implementation Requirements:**
   415→
   416→1. **Config Flow Changes:**
   417→   - Add "advanced calendar mode" toggle per slot
   418→   - When enabled, show pattern configuration UI
   419→   - Pattern fields: slot number regex, PIN regex, which field to parse
   420→     (title/description/location)
   421→2. **Entity Changes:**
   422→   - Calendar event listener needs to parse event metadata
   423→   - Extract slot number and PIN based on user-defined patterns
   424→   - Validate extracted values (numeric slot, PIN format)
   425→3. **Binary Sensor Changes:**
   426→   - Check if calendar event contains valid extracted values
   427→   - Use extracted PIN instead of configured PIN
   428→   - Handle multiple calendar events with different slots
   429→
   430→**Example Patterns:**
   431→
   432→- Title: "Guest Access: Slot 5, PIN 9876" -> Slot: `\d+`, PIN: `\d{4}$`
   433→- Description: "Code: 1234 for slot 3" -> Slot: `slot (\d+)`, PIN: `Code: (\d+)`
   434→- Location: "5:1234" -> Slot: `^(\d+):`, PIN: `:(\d+)$`
   435→
   436→**Challenges:**
   437→
   438→- Multiple calendar events with different slots
   439→- Error handling for invalid patterns
   440→- UI for testing patterns
   441→- Backward compatibility with existing simple calendar mode
   442→
   443→**Estimated Effort:** Very High (40+ hours)
   444→**Priority:** Medium
   445→**Status:** Not started
   446→
   447→### Add Relevant New Home Assistant Core Features
   448→
   449→**Analysis:** Review Home Assistant release notes from 2024.1 through 2025.10
   450→and integrate relevant new features.
   451→
   452→**Key Features to Evaluate (2024-2025):**
   453→
   454→1. **Entity Category Enhancements** (2024.x)
   455→   - New entity categories available
   456→   - **Action:** Review entity category assignments
   457→2. **Selector Improvements** (2024.x)
   458→   - New selector types for config flow
   459→   - **Action:** Review config flow UI for better selectors
   460→3. **Repair Platform** (2024.x)
   461→   - Notify users of configuration issues
   462→   - **Action:** Consider adding repairs for common misconfigurations
   463→
   464→**Already Evaluated (No Changes Needed):**
   465→
   466→- **Config Entry Runtime Data**: `hass.data[DOMAIN]` correctly holds global
   467→  cross-config-entry state (lock registry, resource flag). Per-entry data
   468→  already uses `runtime_data`.
   469→- **DataUpdateCoordinator `_async_setup()`**: All coordinator setup is
   470→  synchronous (timer registration). No async initialization needed.
   471→- **Config Entry Diagnostics**: No significant internal state to expose beyond
   472→  what's already visible via entities and config entries.
   473→
   474→**Estimated Effort:** Low-Medium (4-8 hours)
   475→**Priority:** Medium
   476→**Status:** Partially evaluated
   477→

   479→

   483→- Virtual (`virtual.py`) - for testing only
   484→

   486→

   490→- `homematic` - Homematic (CCU)
   491→- `homematicip_cloud` - Homematic IP Cloud
   492→- `homekit_controller` - HomeKit accessories

   556→
   557→**Recommended Priorities for Support:**
   558→
   559→**High Priority** (popular, widely used):
   560→
   561→1. **ZHA (Zigbee Home Automation)** - Very popular, supports many lock brands
   562→2. **Matter** - Future-proof, industry standard (PR open)
   563→3. **MQTT** - Generic protocol, many custom implementations

   573→- Vehicle locks (Tesla, BMW, Subaru) - different use case
   574→- Security system locks - usually managed by their own systems
   575→- Utility integrations (template, group) - may work without specific provider

   577→**Implementation Approach:**

   585→5. Add tests in `tests/INTEGRATION_NAME/test_provider.py`

> AGENT

All clean. Here's the summary of the simplified approach:

## Summary

**Before (6 commits, 785 insertions):**
- Remove `async_request_refresh` from `_base.py`
- CC version detection + `supports_push` branching
- V1-specific polling intervals / connection check
- Event suppression during hard refresh
- 3 regression tests in `test_base.py`
- TODOs for future V1/V2 work

**After (zwave_js.py only, 29 lines changed):**
1. **`_usercode_cc_version`** cached property — detects V1 vs V2
2. **`get_usercode_from_node()`** after set — polls the slot from the device, updating the Z-Wave JS value cache
3. **`get_usercode_from_node()`** after clear — same for clear operations

No changes to `_base.py`, `test_base.py`, `TODO.md`, or `coordinator.py`. The fix works because after polling, the cache has the correct value, so `async_request_refresh()` reads correct data instead of stale data — no sync loop.

> AGENT

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
Ruff has two mutually exclusive docstring rules:
- `D212`: summary on the **first** line (same line as `"""`)
- `D213`: summary on the **second** line (after `"""`)

Currently **both** are ignored. To enforce `"""\n<content>`, we need to enable `D213` (remove it from ignore list) while keeping `D212` ignored.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**D213 vs D212**: Ruff has two conflicting docstring rules — D212 (summary on same line as `"""`) and D213 (summary on next line after `"""`). They're mutually exclusive. This project ignores D212 and now enforces D213, meaning all multiline docstrings must use the `"""\n<summary>` format. Ruff's auto-fix handles the migration cleanly.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

**Summary of what was done:**
- Removed `D213` from the ruff ignore list in `pyproject.toml` to enforce the rule
- Auto-fixed all 68 existing violations across the codebase

(B[m{"body":"## Proposed change\n\nFix sync loops affecting Z-Wave locks using User Code Command Class V1 (e.g., Yale P-KFCON-MOD-YALE). V1 locks lack Supervision CC, so the Z-Wave JS driver always schedules verification polls after set/clear operations. This caused three problems:\n\n1. **`async_request_refresh()` after set/clear** defeated optimistic `push_update()` by reading stale cache, triggering retry loops\n2. **V1 treated as push-capable** — V1 nodes don't reliably send unsolicited User Code Reports, making push-based updates unreliable\n3. **Stale events during hard refresh** — the driver emits value-updated events as it re-queries each slot, overwriting correct data with intermediate cache state\n\n### Changes\n\n- **Remove `async_request_refresh()` after set/clear** (`_base.py`) — relies on optimistic `push_update()` for push providers and next poll cycle for poll providers. Benefits all providers.\n- **Detect CC version and branch behavior** (`zwave_js.py`) — V1 locks: poll every 2 min, hard refresh every 30 min, connection check every 30s. V2 locks: push updates, hard refresh every 1 hour, config entry state.\n- **Suppress push events during hard refresh** (`zwave_js.py`) — `_hard_refresh_in_progress` flag prevents stale value-updated events from corrupting data during cache rebuild. Benefits both V1 and V2.\n- **TODOs** for configurable hard refresh interval and managed/unmanaged slot splitting.\n\n## Type of change\n\n- [x] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)\n\n## Additional information\n\n- 261 tests pass, 13 new tests added covering CC version detection, property branching, optimistic update preservation, and hard refresh suppression\n- Design doc at `docs/plans/2026-02-15-usercode-cc-v1-support-design.md`\n- Tested against device diagnostics from a real Yale V1 lock (Node 136, firmware 33.16, User Code CC V1, no Supervision CC)\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","number":873,"title":"Fix sync loops for User Code CC V1 locks"}

  "command": "gh pr edit 873 --title \"Fix V1 sync loop by polling slot after set/clear\" --body \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n## Proposed change\n\nFix sync loops affecting Z-Wave locks using User Code Command Class V1 (e.g., Yale P-KFCON-MOD-YALE). V1 locks don't reliably update the Z-Wave JS value cache after set/clear operations. When `async_request_refresh()` fires after the optimistic `push_update()`, it reads stale cache data and overwrites the correct state, triggering a retry loop.\n\n### Fix\n\nAfter set/clear on V1 locks, call `get_usercode_from_node()` to poll the specific slot directly from the device. This force-updates the Z-Wave JS value cache before the coordinator reads it, so all downstream reads return correct data and no sync loop occurs.\n\n### Changes\n\n- **Poll slot after set/clear for V1** (`zwave_js.py`) — detect User Code CC version via `node.command_classes`; for V1, call `get_usercode_from_node()` after set/clear to update the cache\n- **Enforce D213 docstring rule** (`pyproject.toml`) — enable ruff D213 and fix all 68 existing violations\n\n## Type of change\n\n- [x] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)\n- [x] Code quality improvement\n\n## Additional information\n\n- 253 tests pass, 3 new tests added covering V1 set/clear polling and V2 no-poll behavior\n- Tested against device diagnostics from a real Yale V1 lock (Node 136, firmware 33.16, User Code CC V1, no Supervision CC)\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\nEOF\n)\"",
  "description": "Update PR title and description"
}

   241→async def test_set_usercode_skips_when_masked_code_matches(
   242→    hass: HomeAssistant,
   243→    zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock,
   244→    zwave_integration: MockConfigEntry,
   245→) -> None:
   246→    """
   247→    Test that set_usercode returns False when masked code resolves to same PIN.
   248→
   249→    Some locks (like Yale) return masked PINs (****) instead of actual codes.
   250→    When the masked code resolves to the same PIN we're trying to set, we should
   251→    skip the set operation to prevent battery drain from repeated writes.
   252→    """
   253→    lcm_entry = MockConfigEntry(
   254→        domain=DOMAIN,
   255→        data={
   256→            CONF_LOCKS: [zwave_js_lock.lock.entity_id],
   257→            CONF_SLOTS: {"2": {}},
   258→        },
   259→    )
   260→    lcm_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
   261→    await zwave_js_lock.async_setup(lcm_entry)
   262→
   263→    # Mock the cache to return a masked code
   264→    masked_slot = {"code_slot": 2, "usercode": "****", "in_use": True}
   265→
   266→    with (
   267→        patch(
   268→            "custom_components.lock_code_manager.providers.zwave_js.get_usercode",
   269→            return_value=masked_slot,
   270→        ),
   271→        patch.object(
   272→            zwave_js_lock, "_resolve_pin_if_masked", return_value="5678"
   273→        ) as mock_resolve,
   274→        patch.object(
   275→            zwave_js_lock, "async_call_service", new_callable=AsyncMock
   276→        ) as mock_service,
   277→    ):
   278→        # Try to set the same PIN that the masked code resolves to
   279→        result = await zwave_js_lock.async_set_usercode(2, "5678", "Test User")
   280→
   281→        # Should skip the set operation
   282→        assert result is False
   283→        mock_resolve.assert_called_once_with("****", 2)
   284→        mock_service.assert_not_called()
   285→
   286→    await zwave_js_lock.async_unload(False)
   287→

   427→async def test_set_usercode_optimistic_update(
   428→    hass: HomeAssistant,
   429→    zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock,
   430→    zwave_integration: MockConfigEntry,
   431→) -> None:
   432→    """
   433→    Test that set_usercode performs optimistic coordinator update.
   434→
   435→    When a set operation succeeds, the coordinator should be updated immediately
   436→    with the new value. This prevents sync loops where the binary sensor reads
   437→    stale cached data and triggers repeated sync attempts.
   438→
   439→    The Z-Wave command is acknowledged by the lock (via Supervision CC), but
   440→    the JS value cache updates asynchronously via push notifications. Without
   441→    the optimistic update, there's a race condition where coordinator refresh
   442→    reads stale cache data.
   443→    """
   444→    lcm_entry = MockConfigEntry(domain=DOMAIN, data={CONF_LOCKS: [], CONF_SLOTS: {}})
   445→    lcm_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
   446→    await zwave_js_lock.async_setup(lcm_entry)
   447→
   448→    # Set up a mock coordinator with stale data (simulating the race condition)
   449→    mock_coordinator = MagicMock()
   450→    mock_coordinator.data = {4: ""}  # Slot appears empty in stale cache
   451→    zwave_js_lock.coordinator = mock_coordinator
   452→
   453→    with patch.object(zwave_js_lock, "async_call_service", new_callable=AsyncMock):
   454→        result = await zwave_js_lock.async_set_usercode(4, "5678", "Test User")
   455→
   456→        assert result is True
   457→        # Verify optimistic update was called with new PIN
   458→        mock_coordinator.push_update.assert_called_once_with({4: "5678"})
   459→
   460→    await zwave_js_lock.async_unload(False)
   461→
   462→
   463→async def test_set_usercode_optimistic_update_prevents_stale_read(
   464→    hass: HomeAssistant,
   465→    zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock,
   466→    zwave_integration: MockConfigEntry,
   467→) -> None:
   468→    """
   469→    Test that optimistic update prevents sync loops from stale cache reads.
   470→
   471→    This test verifies the fix for the reported issue where out-of-sync slots
   472→    cause constant lock activity. The scenario:
   473→    1. LCM sets a code on the lock
   474→    2. Z-Wave command succeeds (lock acknowledges)
   475→    3. Without optimistic update: coordinator.data still has old value
   476→    4. Binary sensor sees mismatch → triggers another sync → loop
   477→
   478→    With the fix, push_update immediately sets coordinator.data to the new value,
   479→    so the binary sensor sees the expected value and doesn't retry.
   480→    """
   481→    lcm_entry = MockConfigEntry(domain=DOMAIN, data={CONF_LOCKS: [], CONF_SLOTS: {}})
   482→    lcm_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
   483→    await zwave_js_lock.async_setup(lcm_entry)
   484→
   485→    # Simulate stale cache: coordinator thinks slot is empty
   486→    mock_coordinator = MagicMock()
   487→    mock_coordinator.data = {4: ""}
   488→    zwave_js_lock.coordinator = mock_coordinator
   489→
   490→    with patch.object(zwave_js_lock, "async_call_service", new_callable=AsyncMock):
   491→        await zwave_js_lock.async_set_usercode(4, "9999")
   492→
   493→        # The optimistic update should have been called
   494→        mock_coordinator.push_update.assert_called_once_with({4: "9999"})
   495→
   496→        # Simulate what push_update does - update coordinator data
   497→        # (In real code, push_update calls async_set_updated_data which does this)
   498→        mock_coordinator.data[4] = "9999"
   499→
   500→        # Now coordinator.data reflects the expected value
   501→        # Binary sensor would see coordinator.data[4] == "9999" == pin_state
   502→        # → expected_in_sync = True → no retry loop
   503→        assert mock_coordinator.data[4] == "9999"
   504→
   505→    await zwave_js_lock.async_unload(False)
   506→
   507→
   508→async def test_clear_usercode_optimistic_update(
   509→    hass: HomeAssistant,
   510→    zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock,
   511→    zwave_integration: MockConfigEntry,
   512→) -> None:
   513→    """
   514→    Test that clear_usercode performs optimistic coordinator update.
   515→
   516→    When a clear operation succeeds, the coordinator should be updated immediately
   517→    with an empty string. This prevents sync loops where the binary sensor reads
   518→    stale cached data showing the old PIN and triggers repeated clear attempts.
   519→    """
   520→    lcm_entry = MockConfigEntry(domain=DOMAIN, data={CONF_LOCKS: [], CONF_SLOTS: {}})
   521→    lcm_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
   522→    await zwave_js_lock.async_setup(lcm_entry)
   523→
   524→    # Set up a mock coordinator with stale data (still shows old PIN)
   525→    mock_coordinator = MagicMock()
   526→    mock_coordinator.data = {2: "1234"}  # Stale: slot still shows PIN
   527→    zwave_js_lock.coordinator = mock_coordinator
   528→
   529→    with patch.object(zwave_js_lock, "async_call_service", new_callable=AsyncMock):
   530→        result = await zwave_js_lock.async_clear_usercode(2)
   531→
   532→        assert result is True
   533→        # Verify optimistic update was called with empty string
   534→        mock_coordinator.push_update.assert_called_once_with({2: ""})
   535→
   536→    await zwave_js_lock.async_unload(False)

   539→# V1 cache poll tests
   540→
   541→
   542→async def test_v1_set_usercode_polls_slot(
   543→    hass: HomeAssistant,
   544→    zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock,
   545→    zwave_integration: MockConfigEntry,
   546→    lock_schlage_be469: Node,
   547→    mock_get_usercode_from_node,
   548→) -> None:
   549→    """
   550→    Test that V1 set_usercode polls the slot from the device after set.
   551→
   552→    V1 locks don't reliably update the Z-Wave JS value cache after a set
   553→    operation. Polling the slot forces the cache to update before the
   554→    coordinator reads it, preventing sync loops.

   822→
   823→def async_capture_events(
   824→    hass: HomeAssistant, event_name: str
   825→) -> list[Event[dict[str, Any]]]:
   826→    """Create a helper that captures events."""
   827→    events: list[Event[dict[str, Any]]] = []
   828→
   829→    @callback
   830→    def capture_events(event: Event[dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
   831→        events.append(event)
   832→
   833→    hass.bus.async_listen(event_name, capture_events)
   834→    return events

   837→async def test_notification_event_keypad_lock_fires_lock_state_changed(
   838→    hass: HomeAssistant,
   839→    zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock,
   840→    zwave_integration: MockConfigEntry,
   841→    lock_schlage_be469: Node,
   842→) -> None:
   843→    """Test that a keypad lock notification event fires EVENT_LOCK_STATE_CHANGED."""
   844→    lcm_entry = MockConfigEntry(domain=DOMAIN, data={CONF_LOCKS: [], CONF_SLOTS: {}})
   845→    lcm_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
   846→    await zwave_js_lock.async_setup(lcm_entry)
   847→
   848→    # Capture LCM lock state changed events
   849→    events = async_capture_events(hass, EVENT_LOCK_STATE_CHANGED)
   850→
   851→    # Create a notification event matching the pattern from HA core tests
   852→    # Type 6 = ACCESS_CONTROL, Event 5 = KEYPAD_LOCK_OPERATION
   853→    event = ZwaveEvent(
   854→        type="notification",
   855→        data={
   856→            "source": "node",
   857→            "event": "notification",
   858→            "nodeId": lock_schlage_be469.node_id,
   859→            "endpointIndex": 0,
   860→            "ccId": 113,  # Notification CC
   861→            "args": {
   862→                "type": 6,  # ACCESS_CONTROL
   863→                "event": 5,  # KEYPAD_LOCK_OPERATION
   864→                "label": "Access Control",
   865→                "eventLabel": "Keypad lock operation",
   866→                "parameters": {"userId": 1},
   867→            },
   868→        },
   869→    )
   870→    lock_schlage_be469.receive_event(event)
   871→    await hass.async_block_till_done()
   872→
   873→    # Verify the LCM event was fired
   874→    assert len(events) == 1
   875→    assert events[0].data[ATTR_CODE_SLOT] == 1
   876→    assert events[0].data[ATTR_ACTION_TEXT] == "Keypad lock operation"
   877→    assert events[0].data[ATTR_TO] == "locked"
   878→    assert events[0].data[ATTR_FROM] == "unlocked"
   879→
   880→    await zwave_js_lock.async_unload(False)
   881→

   926→# Masked usercode tests
   927→
   928→
   929→async def test_get_usercodes_masked_pin_unmanaged_slot_returns_masked_value(
   930→    hass: HomeAssistant,
   931→    zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock,
   932→    zwave_integration: MockConfigEntry,
   933→) -> None:
   934→    """
   935→    Test mixed slots: managed with real code vs unmanaged with masked code.
   936→
   937→    This test verifies behavior when the lock cache contains:
   938→    - Slot 1: Managed by LCM, has real code "9999" -> should be returned
   939→    - Slot 5: NOT managed by LCM, has masked code "****" -> returns masked value
   940→
   941→    Unmanaged slots with masked PINs return the masked value so sync logic
   942→    knows a PIN exists on the lock, even if we can't resolve the actual value.
   943→    """
   944→    # Configure LCM to only manage slot 1 (not slot 5)
   945→    lcm_entry = MockConfigEntry(
   946→        domain=DOMAIN,
   947→        data={
   948→            CONF_LOCKS: [zwave_js_lock.lock.entity_id],
   949→            CONF_SLOTS: {"1": {}},  # Only slot 1 is managed
   950→        },
   951→    )
   952→    lcm_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
   953→    await zwave_js_lock.async_setup(lcm_entry)
   954→
   955→    # Mock the cache to include a slot with a masked PIN that isn't managed by LCM
   956→    masked_slots = [
   957→        {"code_slot": 1, "usercode": "9999", "in_use": True},  # Managed by LCM
   958→        {"code_slot": 5, "usercode": "****", "in_use": True},  # NOT managed, masked
   959→    ]
   960→
   961→    with (
   962→        patch.object(
   963→            zwave_js_lock, "_get_usercodes_from_cache", return_value=masked_slots
   964→        ),
   965→        # Slot 5 not in Z-Wave node data, so code_slot_in_use returns None
   966→        patch.object(
   967→            zwave_js_lock,
   968→            "code_slot_in_use",
   969→            side_effect=lambda s: True if s == 1 else None,
   970→        ),
   971→    ):
   972→        codes = await zwave_js_lock.async_get_usercodes()
   973→
   974→        # Slot 1 should have its code
   975→        assert codes[1] == "9999"
   976→        # Slot 5 returns masked value (so sync logic knows a PIN exists)
   977→        assert codes[5] == "****"
   978→
   979→    await zwave_js_lock.async_unload(False)
   980→

  1022→async def test_get_usercodes_masked_pin_skipped_when_inactive(
  1023→    hass: HomeAssistant,
  1024→    zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock,
  1025→    zwave_integration: MockConfigEntry,
  1026→) -> None:
  1027→    """
  1028→    Test that masked PINs are skipped when slot is inactive (active=OFF).
  1029→
  1030→    When the slot is managed but active=OFF (or entities not ready), the masked
  1031→    code cannot be resolved and the slot is skipped entirely.
  1032→    """
  1033→    lcm_entry = MockConfigEntry(
  1034→        domain=DOMAIN,
  1035→        data={
  1036→            CONF_LOCKS: [zwave_js_lock.lock.entity_id],
  1037→            CONF_SLOTS: {"2": {}},
  1038→        },
  1039→    )
  1040→    lcm_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
  1041→    await zwave_js_lock.async_setup(lcm_entry)
  1042→
  1043→    # Mock the cache to have a masked PIN on a managed slot
  1044→    masked_slots = [
  1045→        {"code_slot": 2, "usercode": "****", "in_use": True},
  1046→    ]
  1047→
  1048→    with (
  1049→        patch.object(
  1050→            zwave_js_lock, "_get_usercodes_from_cache", return_value=masked_slots
  1051→        ),
  1052→        patch.object(zwave_js_lock, "_resolve_pin_if_masked", return_value=None),
  1053→    ):
  1054→        codes = await zwave_js_lock.async_get_usercodes()
  1055→
  1056→        # Slot should be skipped entirely since it can't be resolved
  1057→        assert 2 not in codes

  1061→
  1062→async def test_resolve_pin_if_masked_detection(zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock) -> None:
  1063→    """Test _resolve_pin_if_masked returns value as-is when not masked."""
  1064→    # Not masked - returns value as-is
  1065→    assert zwave_js_lock._resolve_pin_if_masked("1234", 1) == "1234"
  1066→    assert zwave_js_lock._resolve_pin_if_masked("5678", 2) == "5678"
  1067→    assert zwave_js_lock._resolve_pin_if_masked("", 1) == ""
  1068→    # Partially masked - returns as-is (not all asterisks)
  1069→    assert zwave_js_lock._resolve_pin_if_masked("***1", 1) == "***1"

  1073→async def test_push_update_masked_code_resolved(
  1074→    hass: HomeAssistant,
  1075→    zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock,
  1076→    zwave_integration: MockConfigEntry,
  1077→    lock_schlage_be469: Node,
  1078→) -> None:
  1079→    """
  1080→    Test that push updates with masked codes resolve and update coordinator.
  1081→
  1082→    When a push update arrives with a masked code and it can be resolved,
  1083→    the resolved PIN should be pushed to the coordinator.

  1085→    lcm_entry = MockConfigEntry(

  1093→    await zwave_js_lock.async_setup(lcm_entry)
  1094→
  1095→    # Set up a mock coordinator (push_update is synchronous)
  1096→    mock_coordinator = MagicMock()

  1098→    zwave_js_lock.coordinator = mock_coordinator
  1099→
  1100→    # Subscribe to push updates
  1101→    zwave_js_lock.subscribe_push_updates()
  1102→

  1105→        # Simulate a value update event with masked code

  1114→                    "property": "userCode",
  1115→                    "propertyKey": 2,
  1116→                    "newValue": "****",
  1117→                },
  1118→            },
  1119→        )
  1120→        lock_schlage_be469.receive_event(event)
  1121→        await hass.async_block_till_done()
  1122→
  1123→        # Coordinator should receive the resolved PIN, not the masked value
  1124→        mock_coordinator.push_update.assert_called_once_with({2: "9876"})
  1125→
  1126→    zwave_js_lock.unsubscribe_push_updates()
  1127→    await zwave_js_lock.async_unload(False)

  1130→async def test_push_update_masked_code_skipped_when_unresolvable(

  1136→    """

  1140→    the update should be skipped entirely to prevent infinite sync loops.
  1141→    """
  1142→    lcm_entry = MockConfigEntry(

  1144→        data={

  1146→            CONF_SLOTS: {"2": {}},
  1147→        },
  1148→    )
  1149→    lcm_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
  1150→    await zwave_js_lock.async_setup(lcm_entry)
  1151→
  1152→    # Set up a mock coordinator (push_update is synchronous)
  1153→    mock_coordinator = MagicMock()
  1154→    mock_coordinator.data = {}
  1155→    zwave_js_lock.coordinator = mock_coordinator
  1156→
  1157→    # Subscribe to push updates
  1158→    zwave_js_lock.subscribe_push_updates()
  1159→
  1160→    # Mock _resolve_pin_if_masked to return None (can't resolve)
  1161→    with patch.object(zwave_js_lock, "_resolve_pin_if_masked", return_value=None):
  1162→        # Simulate a value update event with masked code
  1163→        event = ZwaveEvent(
  1164→            type="value updated",
  1165→            data={
  1166→                "source": "node",
  1167→                "event": "value updated",
  1168→                "nodeId": lock_schlage_be469.node_id,
  1169→                "args": {
  1170→                    "commandClass": CommandClass.USER_CODE,
  1171→                    "property": "userCode",
  1172→                    "propertyKey": 2,
  1173→                    "newValue": "****",
  1174→                },
  1175→            },
  1176→        )
  1177→        lock_schlage_be469.receive_event(event)
  1178→        await hass.async_block_till_done()
  1179→
  1180→        # Coordinator should NOT receive any update
  1181→        mock_coordinator.push_update.assert_not_called()
  1182→
  1183→    zwave_js_lock.unsubscribe_push_updates()
  1184→    await zwave_js_lock.async_unload(False)

  1413→async def test_push_update_user_id_status_available_clears_slot(

  1416→    zwave_integration: MockConfigEntry,
  1417→    lock_schlage_be469: Node,
  1418→) -> None:
  1419→    """
  1420→    Test that userIdStatus=AVAILABLE push update clears the slot.
  1421→
  1422→    When the lock sends a userIdStatus update with AVAILABLE status,
  1423→    it means the slot has been cleared. This should update the coordinator
  1424→    to mark the slot as empty.
  1425→    """
  1426→    lcm_entry = MockConfigEntry(
  1427→        domain=DOMAIN,
  1428→        data={
  1429→            CONF_LOCKS: [zwave_js_lock.lock.entity_id],
  1430→            CONF_SLOTS: {"2": {}},
  1431→        },
  1432→    )
  1433→    lcm_entry.add_to_hass(hass)

  1435→
  1436→    # Set up a mock coordinator with existing data
  1437→    mock_coordinator = MagicMock()
  1438→    mock_coordinator.data = {2: "1234"}  # Slot has a PIN
  1439→    zwave_js_lock.coordinator = mock_coordinator
  1440→
  1441→    # Subscribe to push updates
  1442→    zwave_js_lock.subscribe_push_updates()
  1443→
  1444→    # Simulate userIdStatus=AVAILABLE event (slot cleared)
  1445→    event = ZwaveEvent(
  1446→        type="value updated",
  1447→        data={
  1448→            "args": {
  1449→                "commandClass": CommandClass.USER_CODE,
  1450→                "property": LOCK_USERCODE_STATUS_PROPERTY,
  1451→                "propertyKey": 2,
  1452→                "newValue": CodeSlotStatus.AVAILABLE,
  1453→            },
  1454→        },
  1455→    )
  1456→    lock_schlage_be469.emit("value updated", event.data)
  1457→    await hass.async_block_till_done()
  1458→
  1459→    # Coordinator should be updated with empty string
  1460→    mock_coordinator.push_update.assert_called_once_with({2: ""})
  1461→
  1462→    zwave_js_lock.unsubscribe_push_updates()
  1463→    await zwave_js_lock.async_unload(False)
  1464→

  1796→async def test_push_update_user_id_status_available_ignored_when_slot_expects_pin(
  1797→    hass: HomeAssistant,
  1798→    zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock,
  1799→    zwave_integration: MockConfigEntry,
  1800→    lock_schlage_be469: Node,
  1801→) -> None:
  1802→    """
  1803→    Test that userIdStatus=AVAILABLE is ignored when slot expects a PIN.
  1804→
  1805→    This prevents sync loops where the lock sends stale AVAILABLE status
  1806→    after a code was successfully set.
  1807→    """
  1808→    lcm_entry = MockConfigEntry(
  1809→        domain=DOMAIN,
  1810→        data={
  1811→            CONF_LOCKS: [zwave_js_lock.lock.entity_id],
  1812→            CONF_SLOTS: {"2": {}},
  1813→        },
  1814→    )
  1815→    lcm_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
  1816→    await zwave_js_lock.async_setup(lcm_entry)
  1817→
  1818→    # Set up a mock coordinator with existing PIN
  1819→    mock_coordinator = MagicMock()
  1820→    mock_coordinator.data = {2: "1234"}  # Slot has a PIN
  1821→    zwave_js_lock.coordinator = mock_coordinator
  1822→
  1823→    # Subscribe to push updates
  1824→    zwave_js_lock.subscribe_push_updates()
  1825→
  1826→    # Mock _slot_expects_pin to return True (LCM expects a PIN on this slot)
  1827→    with patch.object(zwave_js_lock, "_slot_expects_pin", return_value=True):
  1828→        # Simulate userIdStatus=AVAILABLE event (stale status from lock)
  1829→        event = ZwaveEvent(
  1830→            type="value updated",
  1831→            data={
  1832→                "args": {
  1833→                    "commandClass": CommandClass.USER_CODE,
  1834→                    "property": LOCK_USERCODE_STATUS_PROPERTY,
  1835→                    "propertyKey": 2,
  1836→                    "newValue": CodeSlotStatus.AVAILABLE,
  1837→                },
  1838→            },
  1839→        )
  1840→        lock_schlage_be469.emit("value updated", event.data)
  1841→        await hass.async_block_till_done()
  1842→
  1843→        # Coordinator should NOT be updated (AVAILABLE ignored)
  1844→        mock_coordinator.push_update.assert_not_called()
  1845→
  1846→    zwave_js_lock.unsubscribe_push_updates()
  1847→    await zwave_js_lock.async_unload(False)
  1848→

set/clear, and suppressing stale value-updated events during hard refresh so intermediate cache rebuild states don’t overwrite correct data.\n\n**Changes:**\n- Remove `coordinator.async_request_refresh()` after set/clear operations in the base provider flow to preserve optimistic updates and avoid stale-cache retry loops.\n- Add User Code CC version detection to the Z-Wave JS provider and branch intervals/behaviors (V1: polling + shorter hard refresh; V2: push + longer hard refresh).\n- Ignore push “value updated” events while a hard refresh is in progress to prevent intermediate cache states from corrupting coordinator data.\n\n### Reviewed changes\n\nCopilot reviewed 8 out of 8 changed files in this pull request and generated 3 is a `cached_property` that reads `self.node.command_classes`. `supports_push` (and the coordinator init path) will access this during `BaseLock.async_setup()`, potentially before the Z-Wave JS config entry/client/node is ready. If `async_get_node_from_entity_id` or `node.command_classes` fails (or returns incomplete CC info early in interview), this can either raise during setup or permanently cache an incorrect version, leaving a V2 lock treated as V1 for the lifetime of the object. LOADED / node interview is `_usercode_cc_version` property returns a default of 1 when the User Code Command Class is not found in the node's command classes. While this provides a safe fallback, it might mask configuration issues where a lock genuinely doesn't support the User Code CC.\n\nConsider logging a warning when the CC is not found, or verifying during setup that the lock actually has the User Code CC. This would help identify misconfigured locks or integration issues earlier.\n```suggestion\n        cc = next(\n            (\n                cc\n                for cc in self.node.command_classes\n                if cc.id == CommandClass.USER_CODE\n            ),\n            None,\n        )\n        if cc is None:\n            _LOGGER.warning(\n                \"User Code Command Class not found for Z-Wave JS lock %s (node %s); \"\n                \"defaulting User Code CC version to 1. This may indicate a \"\n                \"misconfigured lock or node that does not support user codes.\",\n                getattr(self.lock, \"entity_id\", \"unknown\"),\n                getattr(getattr(self.node, \"node_id\", None), \"__str__\", lambda: \"unknown\")(),\n            )\n            return 1\n        return cc.version\n```","created_at":"2026-02-19T20:07:01Z","updated_at":"2026-02-19T20:07:04Z","html_url":"https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/pull/873#discussion_r2829911748","pull_request_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/raman325/lock_code_manager/pulls/873","_links":{"self":{"href":"https://api.github.com/repos/raman325/lock_code_manager/pulls/comments/2829911748"},"html":{"href":"https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/pull/873#discussion_r2829911748"},"pull_request":{"href":"https://api.github.com/repos/raman325/lock_code_manager/pulls/873"}},"reactions":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/raman325/lock_code_manager/pulls/comments/2829911748/reactions","total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"hooray":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"start_line":107,"original_start_line":107,"start_side":"RIGHT","line":114,"original_line":114,"side":"RIGHT","author_association":"CONTRIBUTOR","original_position":35,"position":35,"subject_type":"line"},{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/raman325/lock_code_manager/pulls/comments/2829911772","pull_request_review_id":3828244462,"id":2829911772,"node_id":"PRRC_kwDOJ7JjuM6orQbc","diff_hunk":"@@ -493,6 +510,11 @@ async def async_set_usercode(\n         await self.async_call_service(\n             ZWAVE_JS_DOMAIN, SERVICE_SET_LOCK_USERCODE, service_data\n         )\n+        # If the poll fails (e.g., due to network issues or the device being unresponsive), the exception will propagate and potentially cause the entire set/clear operation to appear failed, even though the service call on line 510/550 may have succeeded.\n\nConsider wrapping the poll in a try-except block and logging any errors. Done. Here's a summary:

**PR #873 (V1 sync loop fix):**
- Added error handling for `get_usercode_from_node()` calls (Copilot comment)
- Responded to 7 Copilot comments:
  - V2 fixture "bug" — not a bug (same node_id replacement)
  - CC version warning — unnecessary (lock must have User Code CC)
  - Error handling on set/clear — addressed in `8188f1a`
  - 3 old review comments — outdated (code was simplified)

**PR #878 (D213 enforcement):** https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/pull/878
- Removes D213 from ruff ignore list
- Fixes all 68 existing violations

Now regarding your question about retries instead of try-except — the current approach logs and continues because:
1. The optimistic `push_update()` still fires after the poll, giving the coordinator correct data immediately
2. The next scheduled coordinator refresh will pick up the correct cache value
3. Retrying a failed poll could delay the set/clear response and the poll failure likely indicates a transient network issue that the next refresh cycle handles anyway

Would you prefer retries? We could add a simple single retry with a short delay, but it adds latency to the set/clear path for a case that the coordinator refresh already covers.

> AGENT

Good point. Let me think through this carefully.

The poll is what prevents the sync loop for V1. If it fails and we silently continue:
1. Optimistic `push_update()` sets coordinator correctly
2. But `async_request_refresh()` still fires (in `_base.py`), reads stale cache, **overwrites** the optimistic update
3. Binary sensor sees mismatch → sync loop resumes

So best-effort silently reintroduces the exact bug we're fixing.

But retries add complexity and latency for something the sync mechanism already handles. The simplest correct approach: **remove the try-except entirely and let the exception propagate**.

If the poll fails:
- The lock already has the code (Z-Wave command succeeded)
- The exception prevents the optimistic update from running (no false positive to get overwritten)
- The caller in `_base.py` sees the failure, the binary sensor stays out-of-sync, and the sync mechanism retries the whole operation
- On retry: the lock already has the code, so the Z-Wave set is a harmless no-op. The poll likely succeeds this time → cache updates → sync loop avoided

This leverages the existing retry infrastructure instead of adding new retry logic, and avoids the silent failure that reintroduces the bug.

> AGENT

Done. Removed the try-except from both `async_set_usercode` and `async_clear_usercode`. The poll now propagates failures, which is the correct behavior because:

- **If poll succeeds**: cache updated → optimistic update → `async_request_refresh` reads correct data → no loop
- **If poll fails**: error propagates → optimistic update skipped → sync mechanism retries the whole set/clear → on retry, the Z-Wave set is a harmless no-op (lock already has the code), poll likely succeeds this time

     5→from typing import TypedDict, cast
     6→
     7→from ..const import CommandClass
     8→from ..const.command_class.lock import (
     9→    ATTR_CODE_SLOT,
    10→    ATTR_IN_USE,
    11→    ATTR_NAME,
    12→    ATTR_USERCODE,
    13→    CURRENT_AUTO_RELOCK_TIME_PROPERTY,
    14→    CURRENT_BLOCK_TO_BLOCK_PROPERTY,
    15→    CURRENT_HOLD_AND_RELEASE_TIME_PROPERTY,
    16→    CURRENT_TWIST_ASSIST_PROPERTY,
    17→    LOCK_USERCODE_ID_PROPERTY,
    18→    LOCK_USERCODE_PROPERTY,
    19→    LOCK_USERCODE_STATUS_PROPERTY,
    20→    CodeSlotStatus,
    21→    DoorLockCCConfigurationSetOptions,
    22→    OperationType,
    23→)
    24→from ..exceptions import NotFoundError
    25→from ..model.endpoint import Endpoint
    26→from ..model.node import Node
    27→from ..model.value import SetValueResult, SupervisionResult, Value, get_value_id_str
    28→
    29→
    30→def get_code_slot_value(node: Node, code_slot: int, property_name: str) -> Value:
    31→    """Get a code slot value."""
    32→    value = node.values.get(
    33→        get_value_id_str(
    34→            node,
    35→            CommandClass.USER_CODE,
    36→            property_name,
    37→            endpoint=0,
    38→            property_key=code_slot,
    39→        )
    40→    )
    41→
    42→    if not value:
    43→        raise NotFoundError(f"{property_name} for code slot {code_slot} not found")
    44→
    45→    return value
    46→
    47→
    48→class CodeSlot(TypedDict, total=False):
    49→    """Represent a code slot."""
    50→
    51→    code_slot: int  # required
    52→    name: str  # required
    53→    in_use: bool | None  # required
    54→    usercode: str | None
    55→
    56→
    57→def _get_code_slots(node: Node, include_usercode: bool = False) -> list[CodeSlot]:
    58→    """Get all code slots on the lock and optionally include usercode."""
    59→    code_slot = 1
    60→    slots: list[CodeSlot] = []
    61→
    62→    # Loop until we can't find a code slot
    63→    while True:
    64→        try:
    65→            value = get_code_slot_value(node, code_slot, LOCK_USERCODE_PROPERTY)
    66→            status_value = get_code_slot_value(
    67→                node, code_slot, LOCK_USERCODE_STATUS_PROPERTY
    68→            )
    69→        except NotFoundError:
    70→            return slots
    71→
    72→        code_slot = int(value.property_key)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    73→        in_use = (
    74→            None
    75→            if status_value.value is None
    76→            else status_value.value == CodeSlotStatus.ENABLED
    77→        )
    78→
    79→        # we know that code slots will always have a property key
    80→        # that is an int, so we can ignore mypy
    81→        slot = {
    82→            ATTR_CODE_SLOT: code_slot,
    83→            ATTR_NAME: value.metadata.label,
    84→            ATTR_IN_USE: in_use,
    85→        }
    86→        if include_usercode:
    87→            slot[ATTR_USERCODE] = value.value
    88→
    89→        slots.append(cast(CodeSlot, slot))
    90→        code_slot += 1
    91→
    92→
    93→def get_code_slots(node: Node) -> list[CodeSlot]:
    94→    """Get all code slots on the lock and whether or not they are used."""
    95→    return _get_code_slots(node, False)
    96→
    97→
    98→def get_usercodes(node: Node) -> list[CodeSlot]:
    99→    """Get all code slots and usercodes on the lock."""
   100→    return _get_code_slots(node, True)
   101→
   102→
   103→def get_usercode(node: Node, code_slot: int) -> CodeSlot:
   104→    """Get usercode from slot X on the lock."""
   105→    value = get_code_slot_value(node, code_slot, LOCK_USERCODE_PROPERTY)
   106→    status_value = get_code_slot_value(node, code_slot, LOCK_USERCODE_STATUS_PROPERTY)
   107→
   108→    code_slot = int(value.property_key)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
   109→    in_use = (
   110→        None
   111→        if status_value.value is None
   112→        else status_value.value == CodeSlotStatus.ENABLED
   113→    )
   114→
   115→    return cast(
   116→        CodeSlot,
   117→        {
   118→            ATTR_CODE_SLOT: code_slot,
   119→            ATTR_NAME: value.metadata.label,
   120→            ATTR_IN_USE: in_use,
   121→            ATTR_USERCODE: value.value,
   122→        },
   123→    )
   124→
   125→
   126→async def get_usercode_from_node(node: Node, code_slot: int) -> CodeSlot:
   127→    """
   128→    Fetch a usercode directly from a node.
   129→
   130→    Should be used when Z-Wave JS's ValueDB hasn't been populated for this code slot.
   131→    This call will populate the ValueDB and trigger value update events from the
   132→    driver.
   133→    """
   134→    # https://zwave-js.github.io/node-zwave-js/#/api/CCs/UserCode?id=get
   135→    await node.async_invoke_cc_api(
   136→        CommandClass.USER_CODE, "get", code_slot, wait_for_result=True
   137→    )
   138→    return get_usercode(node, code_slot)
   139→
   140→
   141→async def set_usercode(
   142→    node: Node, code_slot: int, usercode: str
   143→) -> SetValueResult | None:
   144→    """Set the usercode to index X on the lock."""
   145→    value = get_code_slot_value(node, code_slot, LOCK_USERCODE_PROPERTY)
   146→    return await node.async_set_value(value, usercode)
   147→
   148→
   149→async def set_usercodes(node: Node, codes: dict[int, str]) -> SupervisionResult | None:
   150→    """Set the usercode to index X on the lock."""
   151→    cc_api_codes = [
   152→        {
   153→            LOCK_USERCODE_ID_PROPERTY: code_slot,
   154→            LOCK_USERCODE_STATUS_PROPERTY: CodeSlotStatus.ENABLED,
   155→            LOCK_USERCODE_PROPERTY: usercode,
   156→        }
   157→        for code_slot, usercode in codes.items()
   158→    ]
   159→    # https://zwave-js.github.io/node-zwave-js/#/api/CCs/UserCode?id=setmany
   160→    data = await node.async_invoke_cc_api(
   161→        CommandClass.USER_CODE, "setMany", cc_api_codes, wait_for_result=True
   162→    )
   163→
   164→    if not data:
   165→        raise ValueError("Received unexpected response from User Code CC setMany API")
   166→
   167→    return SupervisionResult(data)
   168→
   169→
   170→async def clear_usercode(node: Node, code_slot: int) -> SetValueResult | None:
   171→    """Clear a code slot on the lock."""
   172→    value = get_code_slot_value(node, code_slot, LOCK_USERCODE_STATUS_PROPERTY)
   173→    return await node.async_set_value(value, CodeSlotStatus.AVAILABLE)
   174→
   175→
   176→async def set_configuration(
   177→    endpoint: Endpoint, configuration: DoorLockCCConfigurationSetOptions
   178→) -> SupervisionResult | None:
   179→    """Set lock configuration."""
   180→    # It is invalid to set the operation to timed with no timeout, or to constant
   181→    # with a timeout
   182→    if (configuration.operation_type == OperationType.CONSTANT) ^ (
   183→        configuration.lock_timeout_configuration is None
   184→    ):
   185→        raise ValueError(
   186→            "Invalid operation type and lock timeout configuration combination"
   187→        )
   188→    errors: list[str] = []
   189→
   190→    for property_name, attr_name in (
   191→        (CURRENT_AUTO_RELOCK_TIME_PROPERTY, "auto_relock_time"),
   192→        (CURRENT_HOLD_AND_RELEASE_TIME_PROPERTY, "hold_and_release_time"),
   193→        (CURRENT_TWIST_ASSIST_PROPERTY, "twist_assist"),
   194→        (CURRENT_BLOCK_TO_BLOCK_PROPERTY, "block_to_block"),
   195→    ):
   196→        # It a value for a particular configuration value is not provided and it exists
   197→        # on the node, use the cached value
   198→        cached_value = next(
   199→            (
   200→                value
   201→                for value in endpoint.values.values()
   202→                if value.command_class == CommandClass.DOOR_LOCK
   203→                and value.property_name == property_name
   204→            ),
   205→            None,
   206→        )
   207→        if (
   208→            val := getattr(configuration, attr_name)
   209→        ) is not None and cached_value is None:
   210→            errors.append(
   211→                f"- Can't provide value for {property_name} since it is unsupported"
   212→            )
   213→        elif cached_value is not None and val is None and not errors:
   214→            setattr(configuration, attr_name, cached_value.value)
   215→
   216→    if errors:
   217→        raise ValueError("\n".join(errors))
   218→
   219→    # https://zwave-js.github.io/node-zwave-js/#/api/CCs/UserCode?id=setconfiguration
   220→    data = await endpoint.async_invoke_cc_api(
   221→        CommandClass.DOOR_LOCK, "setConfiguration", configuration.to_dict()
   222→    )
   223→
   224→    if not data:
   225→        return None
   226→
   227→    return SupervisionResult(data)
   228→

Now I have the full picture. Here's what I found:

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**Lock entity discovery does NOT require User Code CC.** The Z-Wave JS integration creates lock entities based on **Door Lock CC** (`currentMode` property) or **Lock CC** (`locked` property) — see `discovery.py:712-733`. User Code CC is completely separate. A lock entity can exist without User Code CC.

**LCM config flow only filters by domain + integration.** The entity selector at `config_flow.py:72-82` filters by `domain=lock` and `integration=zwave_js`. No CC validation.

**Bad interview consequences:** If `command_classes` is incomplete:
- `_usercode_cc_version` silently defaults to `1` (misleading — it should mean "CC not found", not "V1")
- `get_usercode_from_node()` would call `async_invoke_cc_api(USER_CODE)` which checks `if not any(cc.id == command_class.value for cc in self.command_classes)` and raises `NotFoundError`
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Our response to the Copilot comment was **incorrect**. A lock entity doesn't require User Code CC — only Door Lock CC is needed. Copilot's suggestion to add a warning log was valid. Let me:

1. Add a warning log when User Code CC is not found on the node
2. Update the GitHub comment

     1→# AGENTS.md
     2→
     3→This file provides guidance to all coding agents (e.g., GPT-4/4o/5 via Codex
     4→CLI, Opus via Claude Code CLI, etc.) when working with code in this repository.
     5→`CLAUDE.md` points here so that Claude shares a consistent view of the project
     6→with other coding agents.
     7→
     8→## Overview
     9→
    10→Lock Code Manager is a Home Assistant custom integration that allows users to manage lock
    11→usercodes across multiple locks. It reduces entity/automation sprawl compared to
    12→alternatives by handling logic internally rather than generating numerous Home Assistant
    13→entities.
    14→
    15→## Follow these rules always
    16→
    17→- `git` and `gh` commands are automatically approved
    18→- When making changes to ts files, before handing it back over to me, run yarn test and build and fix any issues.
    19→- When making changes to python files, before handing it back over to me, run pytest in the venv and fix any issues.
    20→- When creating a PR, ALWAYS use the .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md template
    21→- When submitting a PR, note that Copilot will eventually add review comments which you must review -
    22→  either make changes as needed or explain why you are not addressing a comment (comments that you make
    23→  code changes for don't need a response). Resolve all comments as you address them or respond to them.
    24→  Provide a summary of what was done or not done and ask for confirmation before committing the changes.
    25→- When running hass, pre-commit, or any other python driven commands, always run from the venv
    26→- Before committing, ensure pre-commit succeeds and tests pass.
    27→
    28→## External repositories/directories that are relevant
    29→
    30→- `../lock_code_manager.wiki/` - hosts the GitHub wiki for this project. Changes are automatically live when pushed, and
    31→  changes related to user facing changes in the integration should only be pushed when that code is released.
    32→- `../home-assistant/` the `home-assistant/core` repo (I am a member of the `home-assistant` Organization)
    33→- `../zwave-js-server/` a server that enables clients like `zwave-js-server-python` to interact with the Z-Wave JS driver
    34→  over WebSockets. (`zwave-js/zwave-js-server`)
    35→- `../zwave-js-server-python` the Python library that the HA zwave_js integration uses to communicate with Z-Wave JS
    36→  (`home-assistant-libs/zwave-js-server-python`)
    37→- `../frontend/` the `home-assistant/frontend` repo
    38→- `../keymaster/` the `FutureTense/keymaster` repo, another integration to manage lock user codes
    39→- `~/.homeassistant/` the config folder that is used when I run HA locally for testing purposes
    40→
    41→## Architecture
    42→
    43→### Core Components
    44→
    45→**Providers System** (`custom_components/lock_code_manager/providers/`)
    46→
    47→- Plugin-based architecture for supporting different lock integrations
    48→- `_base.py`: `BaseLock` abstract class defining the provider interface
    49→- `zwave_js.py`: Z-Wave JS lock implementation
    50→- `virtual.py`: Virtual lock implementation for testing
    51→- Each provider implements: `async_get_usercodes()`, `async_set_usercode()`, `async_clear_usercode()`,
    52→  `async_is_connection_up()`, `async_hard_refresh_codes()`
    53→- Providers listen for lock-specific events and translate them to LCM events via `async_fire_code_slot_event()`
    54→
    55→**Coordinator** (`coordinator.py`)
    56→
    57→- `LockUsercodeUpdateCoordinator`: Home Assistant DataUpdateCoordinator that polls lock providers for usercode state
    58→- Each lock instance has its own coordinator
    59→- Default scan interval: 1 minute (configurable via `usercode_scan_interval` property)
    60→- Supports push-based updates via `coordinator.push_update()` for providers with `supports_push = True`
    61→
    62→**Main Module** (`__init__.py`)
    63→
    64→- Entry point manages config entry lifecycle
    65→- `async_update_listener()`: Core function handling dynamic entity creation/removal when config changes
    66→- Uses dispatcher signals to notify entities of changes (e.g., `{DOMAIN}_{entry_id}_add_lock_slot`)
    67→- Registers Lovelace strategy resource for dashboard UI
    68→
    69→**Config Flow** (`config_flow.py`)
    70→
    71→- Multi-step flow: select locks → configure slots → configure individual slot properties
    72→- Validates slots aren't already configured across other config entries
    73→- Supports YAML object mode for advanced slot configuration
    74→
    75→### Entities
    76→
    77→- `binary_sensor.py`: PIN active status (enabled + conditions met) and per-lock in-sync status
    78→- `sensor.py`: Per-lock slot PIN sensors showing current codes on each lock
    79→- `text.py`: Name and PIN configuration entities
    80→- `number.py`: Number of uses tracking (decrements on PIN use)
    81→- `switch.py`: Slot enabled/disabled toggle
    82→- `event.py`: PIN usage events (fires when code slot is used to lock/unlock)
    83→
    84→### Data Flow
    85→
    86→1. User configures slots and locks via config flow
    87→2. `async_update_listener()` creates coordinator and provider instances for each lock
    88→3. Lock provider sets up listeners for lock-specific events (e.g., Z-Wave JS notification events)
    89→4. Coordinator polls provider's `async_get_usercodes()` to keep state in sync (or receives push updates)
    90→5. When slot config changes (name, PIN, enabled), entities call provider's `async_set_usercode()` or `async_clear_usercode()`
    91→6. Provider fires `EVENT_LOCK_STATE_CHANGED` events when locks are operated with PINs
    92→
    93→### Key Design Patterns
    94→
    95→- **Dual storage**: Config entries use both `data` and `options` fields; active config in
    96→  `data`, options flow updates go to `options`, then merged back to `data`
    97→- **Internal methods**: Providers expose `async_internal_*` methods that wrap public
    98→  methods with asyncio locks to prevent race conditions
    99→- **Rate limiting**: `BaseLock._execute_rate_limited()` enforces 2-second minimum delay
   100→  between operations and serializes all lock operations via `_aio_lock`
   101→- **Dispatcher signals**: Heavily used for dynamic entity management without tight coupling
   102→- **Reauth flow**: Automatically triggered if configured lock entities are removed
   103→
   104→### Lock Codes Card - Slot State Logic
   105→
   106→The `lcm-lock-codes` card displays lock slot states with the following data model:
   107→
   108→**Data Fields from Websocket:**
   109→
   110→| Field | Source | Description |
   111→| ----- | ------ | ----------- |
   112→| `code` / `code_length` | Lock coordinator | Actual code on the lock (current state) |
   113→| `configured_code` / `configured_code_length` | LCM text entities | Desired code from LCM config |
   114→| `managed` | LCM config entries | Whether LCM manages this slot (authoritative field) |
   115→| `name` | LCM text entities | Slot name configured in LCM |
   116→| `active` | LCM binary sensor | True if enabled + conditions met, False if blocked |
   117→| `enabled` | LCM switch entity | True if user enabled the slot, False if disabled |
   118→
   119→**Frontend State Decision Table (for managed slots):**
   120→
   121→| `active` | `enabled` | Result | UI Treatment |
   122→| -------- | --------- | ------ | ------------ |
   123→| true | true | Active | Blue solid border, "Active" badge |
   124→| false | true | Inactive | Blue dotted border, "Inactive" badge (conditions blocking) |
   125→| false | false | Disabled | Blue dotted border, "Disabled" badge (user disabled) |
   126→| undefined | undefined | Fallback | Uses `code` presence to determine Active vs Inactive |
   127→
   128→**Unmanaged Slots:** Only have Active (has code) or Inactive (no code) states. They appear
   129→with gray borders and "Unmanaged" badge.
   130→
   131→**Key Insight:** The `managed` field (from config entries) determines LCM management status.
   132→The `configured_code` field indicates whether a PIN is configured, but a slot can be managed
   133→even without a configured code if the PIN text entity is empty.
   134→
   135→### Future: Slot Status Enum (TODO)
   136→
   137→Currently, the coordinator only stores `{slot: code}` and we infer status from code presence.
   138→Z-Wave locks provide richer status via `userIdStatus`:
   139→
   140→- **Enabled**: Slot has active code
   141→- **Available**: Slot can be used but is empty
   142→- **Disabled**: Slot cannot be used (locked out by lock firmware)
   143→
   144→**Planned Enhancement:**
   145→
   146→1. Define generic `SlotStatus` enum in `const.py`:
   147→
   148→   ```python
   149→   class SlotStatus(StrEnum):
   150→       ENABLED = "enabled"
   151→       AVAILABLE = "available"
   152→       DISABLED = "disabled"
   153→   ```
   154→
   155→2. Providers map their native status to this enum:
   156→   - Z-Wave JS: `userIdStatus` → `SlotStatus`
   157→   - Other providers: Infer from their equivalent states
   158→
   159→3. Change coordinator data schema from `dict[int, str]` to `dict[int, SlotData]`
   160→
   161→**Provider Guidance for Status Inference:**
   162→
   163→| Provider State | Maps To |
   164→| -------------- | ------- |
   165→| Code exists on lock | `ENABLED` |
   166→| Slot empty but usable | `AVAILABLE` |
   167→| Slot programmatically disabled | `DISABLED` |
   168→| Unknown/unsupported | Default to `AVAILABLE` if no code, `ENABLED` if code |
   169→
   170→See `TODO.md` for implementation details.
   171→
   172→## Development Commands
   173→

   179→
